The last time Cherry Au spoke to her 68-year-old father, the call lasted just 54 seconds before a prison guard ordered him to hang up.

A year later, Cherry is still waiting to speak to Au Kam-San, one of Macau’s longest-serving lawmakers who remains incarcerated awaiting trial under the China-ruled city’s national security law. He is being held at the city’s Coloane prison.

Au was arrested for alleged collusion with ⁠foreign forces to endanger national security, the first known ​arrest under that law in Macau, in a case that has many echoes of Beijing’s brutal crackdown on the pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong.

Au, who holds joint Portuguese citizenship, is one of the most prominent opposition figures in Macau and had been a lawmaker for two decades in a legislature dominated by Beijing loyalists. He decided not to seek re-election in 2021 after the Macau administration followed Hong Kong’s example by barring pro-democracy figures from running.

In an interview with The Independent, Au’s daughter says his arrest – one year ago on Thursday – came completely out of the blue.

“We didn’t have any sign that something like this would happen,” says Cherry, a London-based fashion photographer. On 30 July 2025, police barged into Au’s home without warning and seized his phone, laptop, and books, which included some titles related to the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre.

open image in gallery Enemy of the state: Au Kam-san in Macau in 2024 ( AFP/Getty )

Au was at home with his wife and one of their daughters when police came.

“They ... took my mother away first and then stayed in the apartment with my dad collecting evidence,” Cherry says. “They basically did a search, and then they took him away after a couple of hours.”

Cherry says police initially tried to treat her mother as a witness, but she declined after learning her legal rights and was released the following day. “She was very shaken and didn’t know what was happening,” she adds.

Since then, she alleges that Au has been denied calls and visits from his family and access to a private lawyer. He faces 10 years in prison if convicted following a closed-door trial conducted under Beijing’s national security procedures.

The family learned through a court statement that Au had a preliminary proceeding on 2 July, Au’s daughter Au Hon I says. The statement says his lawyer was appointed by the court and approved by Au.

“He always believed in the justice system of Macau,” she says. “He believed it so much that he feels that he will be protected by the very justice system that is putting him where he is right now.”

In August last year, Macau’s Public Prosecutions Office said “compulsory detention” had been imposed on Au after a “preliminary investigation” following his arrest at his home.

The European Union swiftly condemned the arrest by saying it heightened concerns about the “erosion of political pluralism” in the Chinese territory, but stopped short of calling for his release.

Cherry says the family fears for the health of her father, who suffers from diabetes, although the Chinese authorities claim he has been provided with appropriate medication.

open image in gallery Coloane prison in Macau, where Au is currently being held awaiting trial ( AFP/Getty )

Since 2020, public life in Hong Kong has been shaped around Beijing’s national security law, imposed to crack down on pro-democracy protesters. At least 400 people have been charged and 160 convicted under the law in Hong Kong.

Now, Chinese president Xi Jinping’s alleged crackdown on dissent has reached the former Portuguese colony across the Pearl River delta, where authorities are set to test the tightened law with Au’s prosecution.

The Macau court this month said a preliminary trial found Au was a “principal offender” and had committed crimes of “subversion of state power”.

The court said Au was suspected of “establishing links with organisations, groups or individuals outside Macau… to commit acts endangering national security”. Local police allege he had provided “a large amount of false and seditious information to an anti-China group” for public exhibitions online and abroad since 2022, and “stirred up hatred” against the Chinese government.

He was also accused of spreading false information to various groups, which disrupted the city’s 2024 chief executive election and caused foreign countries to take hostile action against Macau, police say.

Au’s family fears he was arrested for maintaining contact with foreign diplomats after he retired from politics, though they said there was nothing unusual about the meetings.

“What saddens me the most is seeing him being portrayed as a villain by the very government that he served for so many years. I hope people remember the person they knew throughout his career, the reason why they placed their trust in him and elected him time and again.

“Right now he is facing profound injustice. I hope those who remember his years of service will stand by him. We want a fair trial, due process, and for there to be more than three decades of dedication to the people of Macau, not to be erased or forgotten.”

Au is also a founding member of the Macau Union of Democratic Development, which organised annual candlelight vigils commemorating the Tiananmen Square massacre for almost 30 years. Beijing has banned public commemorations of the Tiananmen Square massacre, where at least 10,000 pro-democracy protesters were killed by the Chinese army.

The group disbanded in 2023 after years of government pressure and abuse braved by the organisers.

Unlike Hong Kong, which saw big social movements challenge Chinese Communist Party rule in 2014 and 2019, the democratic opposition in Macau has always existed on the fringes amid tight Chinese control.

In March this year, lawmakers in Macau unanimously approved a bill allowing court proceedings to be held behind closed doors when deemed necessary to protect national security interests. The city enacted its first national security law in 2009 and tightened ​it with amendments in 2023.

Through the years, Au had led protests and railed against opaque governance and rising social inequalities even as gambling revenues exploded in the city of around 680,000.

open image in gallery A demonstrator holds an electronic candle during a vigil at Liberty Square in Taipei on 4 June 2026, commemorating the anniversary of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Massacre in Beijing ( AFP/Getty )

Au’s wife and two daughters remain in Macau. They have spoken to a social worker who visited Au, but received only limited updates. They were also told to pay 7,000 patacas or £650 to apply to challenge his detention, which was later rejected by Macau authorities.

“We don’t know when these restrictions will be lifted,” Cherry says.

Au’s family has urged the EU to use diplomatic pressure to secure his release. It is understood that the Portuguese consulate in Macau had requested consular access to Au, which was also denied by the Chinese authorities. China does not recognise the concept of dual citizenship.

“This man doesn’t deserve to be in prison after decades, 30 years of working in the public service to help people who are in need and stand up for what’s right. There’s rarely a day that he wasn’t thinking about how he could make life better for the people he served,” Cherry says in her appeal to the EU.

“It is incredible, it’s so selfless. I can’t think of a man who has done more for the city than him throughout the decades. He’s an amazing dad as well. Most importantly, we must be allowed to visit him or at the very least communicate with him somehow, not through a social worker.”

Michael Polak, director of Justice Abroad, who has been helping the family, says Au’s arrest violated the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights that applied to Macau as well.

He says with the national security prosecution in Macau, “It seems like they are following the footsteps of Hong Kong. It’s a big mistake in relation to the reputation of Macau as somewhere where people can do business and people can discuss things.”

It is important to put Au’s case in the spotlight because otherwise they might just continue to hold him without trial, he adds.

“Portugal still sends judges to Macau. So if these kinds of extrajudicial cases are going to be brought, it’s not really a court process when you hold someone incommunicado without a lawyer of their own choosing. Then the Portuguese judges and Portuguese authorities need to consider whether they can continue to do that,” he says, urging the EU to raise Au’s case at the highest level.

Human Rights Watch previously said in a statement that Au’s arrest reflected “broadening repression” under the Chinese president.

“Macau’s authorities should stop suppressing peaceful criticism and immediately and unconditionally free this activist and former legislator,” says Maya Wang, associate China director at the organisation.

The Independent has reached out to the Chinese embassy in London, the European Union, and the Portuguese consulate in Hong Kong and Macau for a statement.

Three-time Olympic champion Adam Ramsay-Peaty has insisted he has found peace despite his bid for Commonwealth Games gold concluding with a bronze medal, following an emotional defeat in the 100m breaststroke.

The 31-year-old broke down in tears after being bested by Australia’s Sam Williamson, with Jersey’s Filip Nowacki securing silver in Glasgow.

Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Ramsay-Peaty reflected on his resilience, stating: "I’ve got very tough skin that has been built quite aggressively over these last six months."

"I know what my values are, my morals are. I can look in the mirror and be at peace with myself and the person that I am."

Dismissing the setback, he remarked: "No matter what way we look at it, it’s two lengths of the swimming baths and we’re trying to do it as fast as we can. My issue is a simple one I can fix."

The swimmer also highlighted his "support circle", including his "incredible wife" Holly, who is expecting their first child.

open image in gallery Ramsay-Peaty hugs his wife, Holly ( Reuters )

Ramsay-Peaty is already a father to five-year-old George from a previous relationship with Eirianedd Munro, and he spoke warmly about fatherhood.

"When you have children, they take a lot of work and a lot of energy and you’re gonna miss a lot of sleep, but what an incredible gift, an incredible blessing.

"I don’t want to get lost in just being an athlete, I want to get lost in being a father and being a husband."

Ramsay-Peaty’s personal life drew headlines last year amid reports of an ongoing family dispute with his parents, Mark and Caroline, who were notably absent from his lavish wedding to Holly, daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay.

Caroline Peaty also did not attend Holly’s hen party in the Cotswolds, which saw guests including Holly’s mother Tana and family friend Victoria Beckham.

Following his Commonwealth Games performance, the swimmer appeared to allude to the family tensions in an interview with TNT Sports.

"It’s hard because I know how hard I’ve worked. I know the s*** I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own. It does take a toll,” he said.

open image in gallery Caroline Peaty released a statement following her son’s outburst ( Getty )

His mother, Caroline, subsequently posted on Instagram, suggesting external forces were at play.

"There is something or someone at play who wants to destroy our family,” she wrote. "We continue to support Adam from afar. He’s our son who we love, whom we supported to reach his aspirations."

Caroline Peaty emphasised their selfless dedication: "Our love, our time, our sacrifices were given freely with no expectation of financial reward just genuinely given with the love as any mother and father would do for their child.

"We are strong, we love and are always there for each other. The very nature of our strength as a family has helped us move past the nastiness, the lies that have been told about us."

An 86-year-old pensioner with Parkinson’s disease has been convicted over an unpaid car tax bill amounting to just £3.34.

The octogenarian, who lives on the outskirts of Newcastle, told the fast-track court that the annual £20 tax bill for his silver Ford Fiesta was inadvertently missed in January when their daughter, who manages his finances, was moving house. His wife, also 86, suffers from Alzheimer’s.

The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) launched a criminal prosecution covering a six-week period between February and mid-March, during which the vehicle had not been properly taxed.

The pensioner noted to the court that he had already settled an £80 financial penalty, which he believed was linked to the same issue, leaving him confused as to why he was now being prosecuted for a criminal offence.

He was convicted at Lincoln Magistrates’ Court last Thursday, and issued with a court order to pay £3.34 in compensation to the DVLA.

The case was prosecuted through the Single Justice Procedure (SJP), a controversial fast-track court process where magistrates sit behind closed doors to deal with low-level criminal cases.

open image in gallery The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) launched a criminal prosecution when the car had not been properly taxed ( PA )

The Government has spent the last 17 months considering whether to reform the SJP system, after a slew of reports of elderly and vulnerable people being harshly convicted of crimes over unpaid household bills.

The DVLA started the criminal case against the pensioner by sending a letter, at a point where his personal circumstances were unknown to the agency.

He responded by entering a guilty plea in writing to the charge of using a vehicle without a valid licence. He then set out his health difficulties in the mitigation section of the online form, writing that his daughter “has control of my financial and health and welfare as lasting POA (power of attorney)”.

“She has to do much on keeping on top of everything for my wife and I.

“We are both nearly 87. I have Parkinson’s disease and my wife has Alzheimer’s. (She) overlooked paying my tax renewal of £20.

“She had moved address and we assumed the original letter or reminder re tax went to her old address.”

open image in gallery The man was convicted at Lincoln Magistrates’ Court last Thursday ( PA )

His letter sets out that the vehicle is now being sold “as I am no longer capable of driving my car”.

And he wrote: “I am not sure why I have received the Single Justice Procedure notice”, ending with a plea to call his daughter “to confirm this matter is resolved with no further action necessary”.

Magistrate Lynda Briggs decided to accept the pensioner’s guilty plea and spared him another fine, concluding the case with an absolute discharge as well as the £3.34 compensation order.

Due to the design of the Single Justice Procedure, prosecutors such as the DVLA do not routinely see mitigation letters, and are at risk of missing important information that could bring into question the public interest of a prosecution.

Magistrates can decide to adjourn a case, either for an open court hearing where a prosecuting lawyer would be present, or to send the case back to the DVLA for a further public interest check in light of the new information.

The Labour Government consulted last spring on the possibility of greater safeguards in the SJP system, including the idea of a mandatory prosecution check of each case after defendants have entered their mitigation.

The DVLA supported the idea of this reform, but since the consultation closed last May the Government has not made any public announcements on possible changes to the system.

The magistrate in Lincoln convicted and sentenced 60 other defendants in DVLA cases on the same day as the pensioner, imposing fines, costs, court fees, and compensation totalling almost £25,000.

According to court data, 1,950 people across England and Wales were prosecuted last week in the Single Justice Procedure for keeping or using a vehicle while their vehicle tax was unpaid.

Keepers at Prague Zoo used tons of ice on Thursday to give its animals some much-needed relief as yet another heat wave hit Europe.

Polar bears Aleut and Gregor wasted no time and were rolling in the beds of ice cubes after entering their outside enclosure.

The twins looked to have fun with the ice treat that was meant to keep them cool amid the extreme temperatures forecast to soar to 38 degrees Celsius (100.4 degrees Fahrenheit) later in the day.

“The bears cool off with it and at the same time it's an enrichment of their life in the zoo,” said zoo spokesperson Filip Mašek.

The zoo began providing ice to some of the animals two years ago in response to climate change and the increasing number of days with extreme temperatures.

The polar bears, who were born in Nuremberg, Germany, 16 years ago and have adapted to the European climate, were the ones who enjoyed it the most.

This year, the plan was to order ice for the animals in July and August, which are traditionally the hottest months. But the first heat wave struck early and the Czech Republic experienced its hottest day ever with 41.9 C (107.4 F) on June 28.

“The weather keeps surprising us,” Mašek said. He said the ice will be ready sooner next year. “We’ve been taught a lesson.”

Other animals that have benefited from the provision of ice to keep cool in previous years include otters, elephants and parrots.

Some animals in the zoo are used to heat, others could stay in the shade or inner enclosures and use various pools to keep cool. Gorillas were given pieces of ice with frozen fruits in the previous years.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibungyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibungyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibungyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibungyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

Sports.title: PSG chief makes decision over UEFA plea to replace FIFA villain Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
PSG chief makes decision over UEFA plea to replace FIFA villain Gianni Infantino

Gianni Infantino has came under waves of criticism this summer following a controversial World Cup in North America, with PSG chief Nasser Al-Khelaifi tipped to run for FIFA presidency

View Image Gianni Infantino has received criticism (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Nasser Al-Khelaifi will not launch a bid to succeed Gianni Infantino as FIFA president, despite calls from UEFA. The Paris Saint-Germain chief was touted to challenge at an upcoming presidential election for World Football next March.

‌



Politico claim that executives saw Al-Khelaifi as a potential force to replace Infantino as FIFA head, following widespread criticism as a result of this summer's World Cup in North America - as well as the body's plans to sell portions of commercial rights.

‌



However, Al-Khelaifi has no interest in entering the race to secure FIFA presidency. A source close to the 52-year-old told RMC Sport : "Nasser has absolutely no ambition, no intention, nor any interest in this role at FIFA. He will continue to quietly support all global and European football institutions."

‌



It comes despite vocal opposition of FIFA's selling of commercial stakes from European Football Clubs, whom Al-Khelaifi is also chairman of.

However, sources close to the executive, who is also at the helm of the BeIN Media Group, have dismissed any rumours of him running next year - citing how his priorities are elsewhere.

‌



It comes as Infantino will be difficult to succeed at next year's election, considering the support he is thought to receive from member associations across South America, Asia and Africa.

There will be more to follow on this breaking news story and Mirror Sport will bring you the very latest updates, pictures and video as soon as possible.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe was FAILED by Newcastle United owners - he should have walked away earlier
Sports.content:
In late March, David Hopkinson, chief executive of Newcastle United, was asked about Eddie Howe’s future. And this is how he replied: “I don’t have a stance on his future. I expect to have a great run to the end of the season and we’ll talk about the future when it is time.”

It is a wonder Howe did not walk out of St James’ Park there and then.

What Hopkinson should have said is that the club has a manager who has taken them from the lower reaches of the Premier League to TWO Champions League campaigns and has helped them to a first domestic trophy in 70 years.

He should have said Howe, over a period of four and a half years, has brilliantly managed a club that is notoriously difficult to manage, and that they would be doing all they can to make sure he was happy to lead them for many seasons to come.

‌



Instead, he did not ‘have a stance on his future’.

Eddie Howe's final words as Newcastle boss speak volumes after Toon exit READ MORE :

Howe had given life and soul to re-energising a great institution and that was his thanks. That was an ill-advised interview from Hopkinson.

The chief executive might claim to have just chosen the wrong words. But more significantly, Howe was let down by actions, as well as words.

The club had little choice but to take Liverpool’s £125million for Alexander Isak and in Anthony Gordon’s case, it is hard to stop a player going to Barcelona. You can even make a compelling argument that £100million for Sandro Tonali was too good an offer to turn down, although losing one of his best players to Tottenham, who had just finished 17th, must have been a very bitter pill for Howe to swallow.

‌



But by the looks of it, they are about to sell Bruno Guimaraes, their talisman. That was probably the final straw for Howe, who has seen the Saudi owners promise the moon, but, since Howe's magic produced a trophy, delivered very little against what they promised

The executives and owners will argue that it is hard to keep players who want to leave and that they have to trade - buy AND sell - to comply with the Premier League’s financial regulations. Fair enough.

But it is the job of the executives and the owners to make sure the marquee players do not want to leave. When they want to leave in numbers, the executives and owners are not doing something right.

‌



Which is why, in a way, Howe’s tenure might have come to a natural end, and the suggestions are that his departure has been amicable. He is such a respectful character that Howe - who is likely to be succeeded by Al-Ahli’s 38-year-old German manager, Matthias Jaissle - is not likely to say anything different when he does talk about leaving a job he clearly loved for a long time.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe and Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

It's understood Howe had wanted to leave for two weeks, with an exit plan in place since early in pre-season.

Neither Newcastle CEO David Hopkinson and sporting director Ross Wilson were shocked by his departure today. Howe's exit is deemed an "energy thing", and club sources insist that it is NOT about politics or transfers or the players that have been signed in the last month or so.

‌



But Howe's comments at Ashton Gate, after being trounced 4-1 by Bristol City in a pre-season friendly on Wednesday night, particularly on Guimaraes - declaring wistfully "what will be, will be" - suggested different.

Some fans might point to a turbulent season that saw Newcastle finish 12th in the Premier League as evidence that his time on Tyneside was coming to an end. No matter that they made it to the last 16 of the Champions League and to the Carabao Cup semi-finals.

When you look beyond the fact that Jaissle is coming from the Saudi Pro League, it will be an intriguing appointment if it happens.

But you can’t help feeling Howe could have created a dynasty in Newcastle and that it is a shame it is over.

‌

Sports.content:
Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure

Eddie Howe has left Newcastle United after a five-year tenure in surprising fashion, but one former Premier League star saw the writing on the wall after last season's tough watch at St James' Park

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has left Newcastle United (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

Dwight Yorke believes that Newcastle United's home and away losses to Sunderland AFC last season made Eddie Howe's job 'unsustainable.' He also believes that finishing five places below them in the Premier League didn't help matters.

‌



The 48-year-old has decided to part ways with the Magpies after a largely successful five-year tenure, with Matthias Jaissle touted to take the reins at St James' Park following his exit. It comes after months of criticism from select Newcastle fans, coupled with the club's damning approach to the summer transfer window thus far.

‌



The Magpies have already lost Anthony Gordon to Barcelona and Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur, and are on the verge of parting ways with club captain, Bruno Guimaraes, amid a wealth of interest from Arsenal. That would ultimately leave Howe without star talent for the upcoming season, making it incredibly difficult to improve on last term's 12th-place finish.

‌



However, the performances on the pitch in 2025/26, particularly against their biggest rivals, were especially problematic for Howe, with Yorke claiming that back-to-back losses to the Black Cats made the Englishman's position 'unsustainable.'

Speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer football odds, Yorke - who played for Sunderland between 2006 and 2009 - said: "Eddie Howe losing twice to Sunderland and finishing below them last season didn’t resonate very well with the fans.

Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle with immediate effect as replacement lined up READ MORE :

Premier League rival and six other clubs Eddie Howe could join after shock Newcastle United exit READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"It doesn’t matter where you are in the world, when it comes to your local derby, you cannot lose both of those games in a season. No matter what else is going on against the other teams, you have to get a result in these games.

"To lose both home and away to your rival like that, it’s unsustainable because the local fans know what comes with it."

It was an increasingly tough watch for Newcastle United fans last season, who lost local bragging rights with an inability to defeat Regis Le Bris' Sunderland. The Black Cats hosted the Magpies at the Stadium of Light in December, winning 1-0 through a catastrophic Nick Woltemade own-goal.

‌

While Newcastle were heavy favourites to atone for the loss during March's reverse at St James' Park, Sunderland prospered once again. While Gordon opened the scoring for his team just 10 minutes into play, Chemsdine Talbi levelled matters early in the second-half.

Brian Brobbey then converted from close range at the death to secure a 2-1 win for Sunderland, and bragging rights for another season. It comes as Al-Ahly coach Jaissle is set to take up tenure on Tyneside following Howe's departure.

Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes' next 24 hours set to prove crucial in Arsenal transfer pursuit

Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes continues to be linked with Arsenal, and an update on his future is set to emerge in the next 24 hours

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes continues to be linked with Arsenal (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is set to rejoin Newcastle United for pre-season training on Friday – though his future at the club remains uncertain. Arsenal are attempting to negotiate a £70million deal for the midfielder as Mikel Arteta looks to add to his squad that won the Premier League last season.

‌



The 28-year-old is a priority target for the Gunners, with the Brazil star receptive to the move . Newcastle are conscious of Guimaraes' position, and ChronicleLive has reported selling him for £70m as a 'non-starter'.

‌



It is additionally reported that the Magpies are becoming increasingly exasperated with Arsenal's tactics, with no direct communication yet established between the two clubs. The North East outfit remain optimistic about retaining their star midfielder, though Eddie Howe's departure may now alter circumstances and suggest Newcastle have accepted losing Guimaraes.

‌



Speaking on Wednesday regarding whether Guimaraes would link up with the squad in La Manga for pre-season following his prolonged World Cup absence, Howe stated: "The details I don't actually know, but I don't see any reason why that wouldn't be the case [him being back on Friday]."

Howe also conceded on Wednesday night following Newcastle's 4-1 loss at Bristol City that the Guimaraes transfer rumours represent an unwelcome distraction. Whether Guimaraes opts to train within the next 24 hours remains to be seen, as Howe remarked: "Any distraction, if it's not healthy, is unhealthy.

"So, yeah [it would be negative for things to drag on], but we're not in control of that. And to some degree, I don't think Bruno's in control of that either."

Howe then introduced a fascinating element to the situation, referencing external 'forces' outside his remit that could affect the midfielder's circumstances.

The 48-year-old stated: "What will be, will be. We can't control the forces that are at play here, we've just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I'm sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done."

When Chronicle Live pressed him on whether he had received any guarantees during their conversations, he continued: "We've spoken numerous times. Assurances? I don't think you can push too hard for those.

It is suggested that the Gunners have established a firm maximum price for Guimaraes and are refusing to exceed it despite their eagerness to acquire the midfielder.

Nevertheless, they may have to stretch further for a player who still has two years left on his existing deal, but Newcastle have the option to prolong his contract by a further year, affording them some negotiating power.

Sports.title: Premier League rival and six other clubs Eddie Howe could join after shock Newcastle United exit
Sports.content:
Premier League rival and six other clubs Eddie Howe could join after shock Newcastle United exit

Eddie Howe is likely to have a number of job opportunities once he is ready to return to football after unexpectedly departing Newcastle United

View 3 Images Eddie Howe could have up to seven interested parties in appointing him as head coach (Image: (Photo by Ed Sykes/Getty Images))

Manchester United and England could be among several options for Eddie Howe's next job in football after his unexpected departure from Newcastle United. Having been at St James' Park for half a decade, it has been reported by our sister-title Chronicle Live that Howe will be taking a break from football with his exit not entirely surprising, as Newcastle are understood to have been working on an exit plan for the last two weeks.

‌



With that in mind, it is perhaps no surprise that Matthias Jaissle has already been lined up as Howe's replacement. News of the latter's decision emerged on Thursday morning after a 4-1 pre-season defeat to Bristol City.

‌



However, several other factors appear to have led to his decision, rather than just a poor showing against Championship opposition.

‌



Alexander Isak, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon have all departed St James' Park in the last two summer transfer windows with Bruno Guimaraes possibly set to become the fourth big-name exit. Having lost so many key players, it would have been hard to see the Magpies getting back into European competitions.

In two of the last four seasons, Howe achieved Champions League qualification but the 2025/26 campaign was particularly disappointing as they finished in the bottom half. Despite those struggles, Howe should have no problems getting another Premier League job and we've taken a look at just a few places he could end up.

Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle with immediate effect as replacement lined up READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Everton

Howe has previously been linked with the Everton job and it could be the perfect next role for him. The Toffees were on the cusp of European qualification last season but David Moyes failed to get them over the line.

Despite the incredible job he has done, supporters have grown frustrated by his tactics and comments after defeats which could mean it is the right moment for change. Talented players such as James Garner, Illiman Ndiaye and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall have seemingly left many with the belief that 13th was not good enough.

Moyes has definitely earned another season but if he fails to make significant progress, Howe could feasibly step into the job after a one-year break and potentially get Everton into Europe, as he did with Newcastle.

‌



View 3 Images David Moyes and Eddie Howe before a Premier League game between Everton and Newcastle United (Image: (Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images))

England

There is a real lack of elite-level English managers but Howe is arguably right up there and could replace Thomas Tuchel as head coach of the national team if Tuchel fails in another major tournament.

Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes certainly believes he will take charge of the Three Lions in the future. He told FourFourTwo last May: “He is by far the best European coach I’ve had. No doubt he’ll be England manager one day. As a person, he’s a sensation – a true legend.

‌



“He’s gifted with strong man-management skills. He knows exactly the best way to talk to you in private, in the dressing room and in the press. He still has a long and promising career ahead of him.”

Howe was linked to replacing Gareth Southgate but was settled at Newcastle when he departed. The FA could certainly look to the 48-year-old over the coming years, though.

Manchester United

Eddie Howe has also been linked to the Manchester United head coach position over the last few years. Michael Carrick has only recently taken over permanently but that does not rule out a swift move for someone like Howe if things do not work out for the club's former midfielder.

‌



View 3 Images Eddie Howe ended Michael Carrick's unbeaten start at Manchester United

He is likely to be given time following his impressive interim spell but that could work in Howe's favour given his desire to have a break from football.

Perhaps the only thing working against him is his struggle to balance Premier League and European football, as evidenced at Newcastle.

‌



Nottingham Forest

Though Oliver Glasner has only just taken charge at Nottingham Forest, do not rule out a mid-season departure given his history and the volatile Evangelos Marinakis.

Forest are undoubtedly a big club; therefore, it would not feel like a backward step for Howe. It could actually turn out to be the ideal job for him given their ambitions to become a club that regularly qualifies for Europe and will spend money to get there.

Brentford, Brighton or Leeds United

Most Premier League teams would arguably be open to appointing Howe but Brentford, Brighton and Leeds United stand out.

‌



That is largely because all three do not have new managers and thus could seek a change fairly soon, particularly if improvements aren't made this season. Keith Andrews had a great start but there are fears that Brentford will regress this season.

Daniel Farke kept Leeds United up but they may seek more stability going forward which Howe would undoubtedly provide.

Fabian Hurzeler only just signed a new contract at Brighton but like Howe, he may become frustrated by marquee player sales which could create a vacancy.

Sports.title: Chelsea sign Lacroix from Palace
Sports.content:
Chelsea have completed the signing of Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace in a deal worth £51m.

The 26-year-old central defender has signed a six-year contract at Stamford Bridge. Lacroix's arrival takes the club's spending to beyond £250m this summer.

Lacroix becomes the first player Chelsea have signed for a fee aged 26 or over since the summer of 2022, with the club also set to complete deals for 35-year-old Danny Welbeck and 36-year-old Jordan Henderson.

This is a deliberate change in transfer policy from Chelsea to target more experienced palyers that has been embraced by new manager Xabi Alonso.

Palace were seeking around £55m in negotiations, given the fee Tottenham paid for Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton.

Chelsea are expected to move on a number of defenders in this window, including Trevoh Chalobah, Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi, having already raised more than £130m from player sales and the compensation received from Manchester City for Enzo Maresca.

Sky Sports News understands Chelsea gave Palace the chance to discuss signing one of their defenders available for transfer during talks.

Palace and Chelsea have a good relationship and they have done deals for players such as Chalobah and Ben Chilwell in the past.

'Chelsea is the best club in the world'

Lacroix said: "I think it's the best move for me because it's the best club in the world.

"I spoke with Malo [Gusto]. I spoke with Trev [Chalobah]. I spoke with Benoit [Badiashile]. It's easy for people to speak well about this club because it has a lot of big history and I'm really proud to be a part of it now.

"I spoke with the manager on the phone. We spoke about tactics, we spoke about how he sees the game. First of all, I was happy just to speak about football with him, and I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

"When I spoke with the gaffer, when I spoke also with the people I know from the national team who play for Chelsea, like Malo, they told me it was the best club I can go to.

"So already I was saying: "Okay, I don't need to think too much". After talking to people I said to myself: "This is the best step forward for me"."

Sky Sports' Adam Bate:

Far from a veteran, Lacroix, 26, is entering his prime after two strong seasons with Palace. Beyond Selhurst Park, perhaps the Frenchman has gone a little under the radar. But, particularly since Marc Guehi's exit, there is growing awareness of his key role.

Oliver Glasner, who worked with him in both Germany and England, rather summed it up with his own verdict on the player recently. "There is Maxence Lacroix, who came from Wolfsburg, and many asked, 'Why did you sign this player?' I think he stepped up."

Few defenders boast his skillset. Lacroix ranks among the top five fastest centre-backs in the Premier League since his arrival from Wolfsburg in 2024. That recovery speed helps make him one of the most formidable one-on-one defenders in the competition.

The numbers back that up to. In one-on-one situations, nobody is better than Lacroix at winning the ball back. He is the only player in the Premier League to have faced 50 or more such situations in the past two seasons and won the ball more often than not.

At 6ft 4in, Lacroix is a robust physical presence who has adapted easily to the demands of the Premier League. He has all the stats to support that, ranking third for clearances and seventh for aerial duels won. But he can do more than defend his box.

Sports.title: Who is Matthias Jaissle?
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle, the man tipped to replace Eddie Howe at Newcastle United, might not be too well known given that his only head coaching roles to date have been in Austria and Saudi Arabia. So who is the man linked with a move to St James' Park?

The 38-year-old German played for Hoffenheim before embarking on a coaching career that took him to Denmark and into an academy role at Red Bull Salzburg. His first senior job was at FC Liefering, moving on to the top job at Salzburg in the summer of 2021.

Jaissle won the double in his first season and retained the league in his second. He worked with Karim Adeyemi and Benjamin Sesko in Salzburg, competing in the Champions League, before moving on to Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League in 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Eddie Howe’s final interview as Newcastle head coach

He has spent the past three years in the Gulf, winning the Saudi Super Cup in Hong Kong last year. But before that he spoke to Sky Sports as part of our Future of Football series for an illuminating discussion of his ideas and how he saw the game progressing.

Here's what we found out…

Inspirations as a coach

Jaissle is steeped in the Red Bull school, having been the head coach at FC Liefering and Red Bull Salzburg at a young age. This means a particular emphasis on high pressing and relatively direct play, looking to move the ball forwards whenever possible.

But his Salzburg team also had plenty of possession and Jaissle would not want to be pigeonholed. "You have to develop your game, you have to always make progress." He has indicated that he is willing to look to all of the game's top coaches for inspiration.

"They always have some principles you can see which make sense to include in your philosophy. It's not about copying, exactly, but seeing interesting things, creating your thoughts about it, and then, if it fits, you can bring it into your way of playing."

What formation does he play?

That has been reflected in the evolution of his preferred formation. At Salzburg, it was often built around the narrow 4-4-2 with wingers coming inside that Ralf Rangnick popularised across the Red Bull teams. But he switched things up in Saudi Arabia.

With Al Ahli, he often adopted a 4-2-3-1 formation building with either a 3-2-5 or a 2-3-5 structure - something that is de rigueur in the Premier League. Speaking to Sky Sports, he explained that it was more about principles of play than the precise formations.

Image: Red Bull Salzburg's formation in the Champions League under Jaissle

"It is not about formations that much. It is more how you want to play, how you want to attack, how you want to defend. If you understand that and the players understand that, tactically you are much more flexible and the formation is not that important."

It can be demanding for players. "These days the players are more and more involved in tactical things. Every coach and every club works with principles, so every player has to know a lot of things, tactically, in each phase of the game. I think that's a big change."

Predicting the future

Speaking to Sky Sports in 2023, Jaissle anticipated some of the changes that have been seen in the Premier League since then with its increased robustness and the growing focus on set-pieces. "It could be more dynamic and more physical also," he suggested.

He added: "Only the most professional players will survive at the top, top level, I would say." Jaissle also predicted that "there will be more and more so-called all-rounders" in football in the future - meaning defenders who attack, attackers who defend, and more.

"Players who are able to play in more positions, which makes total sense and makes it easier for the manager to change within the game or alter the formation. That is quite easy if the players understand it and know how to live your principles on the pitch."

That extends to the goalkeeper role with his preference for those who can be part of the build-up. "Goalkeeper is not a position by itself any more. It is completely included with the other guys. A goalkeeper has to have an understanding of all phases of the game."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the friendly between Bristol City and Newcastle [Credit: Robins TV]

But motivation still matters

Jaissle has experience working in multi-cultural dressing rooms, citing the fact that the number of different nationalities at Salzburg was into double figures. And for all the focus on tactics, technique and physicality, motivation remains key to management.

"I think the communication and the connection with the players is always the base for leadership and being a good coach," he explained to Sky Sports. "You really have to take care of that. I would always prioritise one on ones and face-to-face conversation.

"You really have to take care that you don't have too much information. This is a big challenge. As a manager or coach, you know so much about tactics, but you cannot just give everything to the players. You have to really take care not to overwhelm them."

Sports.title: Women's Super League fixtures announced for 2026/27 season
Sports.content:
Manchester City will begin their Women's Super League title defence against newly-promoted Birmingham City after London City Lionesses have opened the 2026/27 season against Manchester United, live on Sky Sports.

The fixtures for the upcoming campaign have been released, with kick-off times and broadcast picks confirmed for the first four weekends, featuring more matches than ever after the league expanded from 12 teams to 14 after Birmingham City, Crystal Palace and Charlton Athletic secured promotion from WSL 2.

Sky Sports will show 90 per cent of all WSL matches live on Sky Sports and NOW - 163 matches in total, as well as the play-off - with selected games also shown on the Sky Sports WSL YouTube channel. There will be greater flexibility over fixtures, with fewer matches kicking off at the same time.

London City, who signed two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas this summer, will launch the new season in front of the Sky Sports cameras on Friday September 4 against Man Utd before champions Man City host newcomers Birmingham City on a bumper day of action on Sunday September 6 featuring five live games.

The other matches on the first Sunday of the season see last year's runners-up Arsenal start with a trip to Brighton, while Tottenham host a London derby against West Ham, Liverpool visit newly-promoted Charlton and Crystal Palace, who secured an immediate return to the top flight, face Everton.

Eight-time winners Chelsea host Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge on Saturday September 5.

Sports.title: Howe leaves Newcastle - Saudi-based Jaissle set to replace him
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left his role as Newcastle United head coach.

The decision has been taken following discussions with the club's hierarchy over the last 48 hours, although Howe had started the ball rolling on a potential departure a number of weeks ago.

In this time, Howe continued to focus on preparing the Newcastle team for their season opener against Liverpool on August 23, live on Sky Sports. Howe's departure comes 25 days before that fixture.

Matthias Jaissle of Al Ahli Is the favourite to replace Howe and Newcastle are hopeful of putting him in charge within 24 hours. Sky Sports News understands talks are at an advanced stage with the 38-year-old German coach. Al Ahli are one of the four clubs owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) - who also own Newcastle.

Kieran McKenna and Antonio Conte were other names on the shortlist before Newcastle decided on Jaissle, who will take charge of Newcastle's pre-season training camp in La Manga.

Newcastle have already had a challenging summer after the sales of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon - and that continues with uncertainty over their captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is wanted by Arsenal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Howe discussed the rumours surrounding Bruno Guimaraes and revealed he wanted to keep him at the club, before news of his departure emerged

Those sales have played a factor in Howe's decision amid concerns about what the squad will look like at the start of the new campaign. Newcastle also sold striker Alexander Isak for a British-record £125m to Liverpool last summer.

Howe has spent a number of months reflecting on his time at Newcastle and believed he could take the club forward this season, providing Newcastle recruited well this summer.

Eddie Howe's Newcastle reign November 2021 - Howe replaces Steve Bruce as Newcastle United head coach

May 2022 - Howe guides Newcastle to 11th-placed finish in first season in charge. Newcastle become first Premier League team to stay up after failing to win any of their first 14 games

August 2022 - Howe signs new long-term contract

February 2023 - Howe leads Newcastle to first final in 24 years but they lose Carabao Cup final 2-0 to Manchester United

May 2023 - Howe leads Newcastle to a fourth-placed finish earning the club qualification for the Champions League for the first time in more than 20 years

January 2024 - Howe leads Newcastle to victory in an FA Cup Tyne-Wear derby - their first win over Sunderland in almost 13 years

May 2024 - Newcastle finish seventh despite scoring 85 goals and posting their highest Premier League goal tally ever

Mar 2025 - Newcastle beat Liverpool 2-1 in the Carabao Cup final to win their first major trophy in 56 years

May 2025 - Howe leads Newcastle into the Champions League again with a fifth-placed Premier League finish

September 2025 - Howe loses star striker Alexander Isak to Liverpool in a £125m deal on Deadline Day

February 2026 - Newcastle advance to the knockout stages of the Champions League via the play-offs, where they are later beaten by Barcelona

May 2026 - Newcastle finish the season 12th

May 2026 - Anthony Gordon leaves for Barcelona in a deal that nets Newcastle almost £70m

July 2026 - Howe sees Sandro Tonali leave for Spurs in a deal worth £100m

July 2026 - Club captain Bruno Guimaraes tells Newcastle he wants to leave

July 2026 - Howe steps down as Newcastle head coach less than 24 hours after 4-1 pre-season defeat to Championship side Bristol City

Newcastle have signed 20-year-old winger Bazoumana Toure from Hoffenheim for £42m, 18-year-old midfielder Sean Steur from Ajax for £23m and 20-year-old goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen from Reims for £18.5m.

They have recently, however, appeared to miss out on Johan Manzambi, who decided to move to Aston Villa - which was a big blow for Howe and the club.

Howe has been one of Newcastle's greatest-ever managers, winning the League Cup to end the club's 70-year wait for silverware as well as taking the club into the Champions League on two occasions after sealing top-five finishes in the Premier League.

Last season, they progressed further in the Champions League than they had ever done before.

Howe's final game in charge was a brutal 4-1 pre-season loss to Championship side Bristol City on Wednesday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights of the pre-season friendly between Bristol City and Newcastle. Credit: Robins TV

When did Howe decide to leave Newcastle?

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie:

Eddie Howe informed his coaching staff upon return from Bristol City, where they lost 4-1 in a friendly. The decision had nothing to do with the match, it had been in the pipeline for two weeks.

Howe gave his full commitment to the club at the end of the season, but has changed his mind. He is set to take a break from football and Howe wanted the club to have a replacement lined up before he left.

This is Howe's decision, the club tried to convince him to stay. He feels he has taken it as far as he can after nearly five years at the helm.

There is no acrimony, the club love him and think he's done an amazing job.

The players have yet to be told. They are on a day off today. The squad fly out to Spain for a pre-season training camp on Friday. Newcastle are yet to comment or put out a statement.

This is not ideal timing as far as the club are concerned, but they are moving swiftly to try and replace Howe. They are in advanced talks with Jaissle of Al Alhi, having also spoken to Antonio Conte and Kieran McKenna.

'I cannot assure Bruno future' - Howe's final words as boss

In his final words as Newcastle boss, Howe refused to offer assurances over the future of captain Guimaraes amid heavy interest from Arsenal - but added the player is not in control of his own future.

Sky Sports News reported earlier this month that Guimaraes had told Newcastle he would like to leave the club in favour of a move to the Premier League champions, but the Magpies had no intention of selling the 28-year-old Brazil international.

Asked about Guimaraes, who is yet to rejoin his team-mates following the World Cup, Howe said on Wednesday night: "Assurances - I don't think you can push too hard for those. I think I've said many times you want players that are committed.

"Bruno's always been committed here. His training performances, his game performances, have been outstanding. Every time he's worn the shirt, he's played with the fans by his side. I'd love to see that continue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look back at when Arsenal target Guimaraes took on the Gunners in a fiery clash at St James' Park in 2023

"I think we want to keep all of our best players. They're so valuable, and as I said numerous times, there aren't many of them, and to get them and develop them is so difficult.

"So when you have them, you want to keep them. And Bruno's very much in that category; he's an outstanding player."

Asked if this saga dragging on creates a negative mood, Howe replied: "Any distraction, if it's not healthy, is unhealthy. So, yeah.

"But we're not in control of that. And to some degree, I don't think Bruno's in control of that either.

"What will be, will be. We can't control the forces that are at play here, we've just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I'm sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done."

Bothroyd: Newcastle in relegation scrap without Howe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Arsenal and England striker Jay Bothroyd worries for Newcastle following the departure of Howe and predicts they could end up in a relegation battle this season

Sky Sports News' Jay Bothroyd:

"There's so many players leaving, so to be honest I can understand why he [Howe] would want to leave now.

"He's saying: 'I had a strong squad. You've taken away some of the best players I had. Some of the best players in the Premier League. You're replacing them with unproven players in the Premier League.'

"It seems to me that he doesn't have the control he wants. He doesn't want to see these players leave.

"It's just really bad times for Newcastle, yet again. This is even worse than last year. Losing [Alexander] Isak and him not turning up to training is one thing, but now you're losing one of the best managers in the country and all your best players.

"Where do Newcastle go from here? It's going to be an unproven manager because who wants to put themselves in a situation where you don't have a strong side.

"I said mid-table [as a Premier League prediction]. Now I'm saying bottom half of the table.

"They're way off it. They're going to be in a relegation battle this year."

Your views on Howe's exit...

HullToon: I cannot believe it. Does he feel supported enough? Does the project still match the original plan that he set out for? There are so many questions raised because of this. Last season was disappointing, but there's mitigating circumstances.

JimmiDee: Regardless of last years disappointment, Howe has done an unbelievable job, and he's had to put up with his team being pillaged the last two seasons and expected to produce the same results with bargain bin replacements which is just completely unrealistic. He deserves better.

SPritc80: A section of our short sighted fans are to blame for Eddie leaving and some big hitters choosing to leave. Results have not gone our way at times. Jumping on the back of players and the head coach in the way they have is disrespectful. No wonder they are all leaving.

BrettJ2002: Why didn't Eddie Howe decide to do this before pre-season started so new manager can get a lot more time in with the squad? Thanks to Eddie for what he has done, but his time was definitely up.

Chris W: Strongly support Eddie - that's two new statues we need this month!

Fez71: Didn't look like Eddie was getting backed, selling all our best players. Very sad times, thanks for all the memories, Eddie.

Sports.title: Norrie into Los Cabos quarter-finals as Osaka advances in Washington
Sports.content:
Cameron Norrie continued his return to form at the Los Cabos Open by beating James Duckworth in straight sets to reach the quarter-finals.

Norrie had lost six successive matches across clay and grass before starting his summer hard-court campaign with victory over Aleksandar Kovacevic on Monday night.

The British No 2 backed up that performance with a 6-4 6-4 win over Duckworth on Wednesday evening to set up a last-eight clash with another Australian, Bernard Tomic.

Norrie lost his first service game of the match to fall 2-0 down, but would then claim two successive breaks of serve himself to take a 4-3 lead, before routinely closing the set out with a couple of holds.

The 30-year-old looked to be cruising to victory when he went up a double break in the second set to lead 5-2, but had to survive a brief wobble before getting over the line.

Wolverhampton is the centre of attention on Thursday night, with eight races scheduled on the all-weather, all live on Sky Sports Racing.

5.47 Wolverhampton - Exciting newcomers Pyramid and Bintward headline

Exciting newcomers Pyramid and Bintward headline a classy field of eight for the attheraces.com/marketmovers Maiden Stakes.

The Juddmonte-owned Kingman colt Pyramid has a fine pedigree, being related to the likes of Fingerpoint and Set Piece. With his trainers John and Thady Gosden arriving in red-hot form, he ought to go close under Rab Havlin.

Bintward cost a whopping €780,000 at the Deauville Arqana yearling sale and has been given plenty of time by his trainer Roger Varian. A daughter of Night Of Thunder, she is sure to be popular with Sean Dylan Bowen in the saddle.

Chimes Of Thunder rates the best of those with racecourse experience and William Haggas' 76-rated filly will hope to put that to good use as she switches to the all-weather. Sea The Stars filly Walking On Stars made little impression on debut

6.22 Wolverhampton - Angel Sense and Supreme Star seek first success

Angel Sense and Supreme Star feature among 12 runners for an open-looking Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes.

The Marco Botti-trained Angel Sense had finished in the first three on his opening three starts before suffering a heavy defeat when favourite at Newbury and he could be involved if able to bounce back.

Stablemate Supreme Star improved on his debut to finish an excellent second at Nottingham last month and that form entitles him to hit the frame.

Fresh from his Group Two win earlier this week, Kaiya Fraser will be looking for further successes and rides Location Location - who kept on when second at Thirsk on his last start and must be feared. Archie Watson's Ouragan is another for the shortlist, having ran well at Newbury the last day. If she adapts to the tapeta, she could trouble the judge.

10.14 Saratoga - Survie and Gezora seek Grade Two honours

A fantastic renewal of the Grade Two Glens Falls Stakes sees ex-European runners Gezora and Survie clash at Saratoga.

Gezora enjoyed a fruitful campaign last season, winning the Prix de Diane and Breeders' Cup Filly & Mare Turf when trained by Francis-Henri Graffard. However, she is yet to score since heading to the United States. Second in the Modesty Stakes at Churchill Downs on her first start of the campaign, she failed to fire when well beaten in the New York Stakes and has a point to prove on debut for Bill Mott.

Survie has been a fine servant for her connections picking up over £700,000 in prize money in her eighteen starts. George Boughey's five-year-old has run with credit on her last couple of runs at Newmarket and Royal Ascot and could be suited by this sharp 12-furlong test.

Last-time winners Massarat and Dona Clota make each-way appeal in a superb heat.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe leaves Newcastle United with Matthias Jaissle set to replace him
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has left Newcastle and is set to be replaced by the German coach Matthias Jaissle, who is currently in charge of the Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli.

Although the timing of Howe’s abrupt departure following almost five years in charge at St James’ Park is unexpected, his position had been under intense scrutiny from Newcastle’s Saudi Arabian owners for some time.

Sources have suggested the 48-year-old told them he wanted to take a break from football following a transformative Tyneside tenure that saw Newcastle win the League Cup in 2025 and twice qualify for the Champions League.

Not that Howe gave any indication of the events about to unfold when he spoke to reporters following Wednesday night’s 4-1 pre-season friendly defeat at Bristol City. “Every day as Newcastle manager is a great day for me,” he said. “I absolutely love the football club and that will never change. I think there’s always reasons to be optimistic and that’s very much my default setting. I believe great things are possible every season with a real buzz of what’s ahead. I see no reason for it be any different this year.”

Earlier on Wednesday though, bookmakers’ odds on Howe becoming the first manager to be sacked this season had shortened dramatically.

By Thursday morning the Newcastle hierarchy’s negotiations with Jaissle were said to be at an advanced stage. Given that Al-Ahli are also owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, the split from his current club is unlikely to prove problematic.

Although a disappointing 12th-place Premier League finish last season left some Newcastle fans calling for his sacking, Howe appeared to have convinced PIF to offer him another season during a summit meeting at a Northumberland country house hotel in April.

This, though, has been a turbulent summer featuring the exits of high profile Newcastle first teamers, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively allied to considerable doubt surrounding the future of the Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimarães.

Howe’s previously considerable influence over transfers had been reduced significantly since Ross Wilson’s installation as director of football. Wilson has introduced a new policy of signing largely young players with high resale potential priced, broadly, in the £20m to £40m bracket.

Sports.title: Fifa ‘undermining the very foundations of football’, says AFC as Uefa talks loom
Sports.content:
The Asian Football Confederation has accused Fifa of undermining the foundations of football by failing to consult the confederations over their plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

In a letter sent on Thursday by president Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa to AFC’s 47 members, which has been seen by the Guardian, Fifa’s unilateral actions in doing a deal with Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital to buy 20% of a new company that would control the commercial rights of all global tournaments is roundly condemned.

Al-Khalifa’s intervention appears significant, as the AFC has previously been strong supporters of Gianni Infantino and has already pledged to vote for him en masse in next year’s Fifa presidential election.

With the South American confederation Conmebol and the Confederation of African Football (Caf) firmly behind Infantino the AFC’s position is critical, as they appear to have the balance of power.

Uefa and the North American confederation Concacaf have both strongly opposed the sell-off, but with just 65 votes between them would not have sufficient numbers to block Fifa’s proposal, which requires a simple majority of their 211 to pass.

The AFC had issued a statement echoing Uefa’s concerns over governance yesterday, but al-Khalifa’s letter goes further.

“The AFC notes with great concern and disappointment that it was not consulted by Fifa at any level prior to the public announcement of this proposal, and nor has it received any detailed governance, financial or legal analysis of the proposal and its potential repercussions, which is totally unacceptable,” he wrote.

“Furthermore, the AFC is deeply concerned that Fifa’s unilateral actions appear to undermine the very foundations of Continental football, which are based on solidarity, cooperation and transparency. Moreover, such an initiative will not succeed without the support of all the Confederations, which is not the case now.”

Al-Khalifa also called on Fifa to alter their timetable after Infantino gave national associations a deadline of 19 September to decide whether to accept an initial payment of $20m (£15m) that would be generated by the sale.

“The AFC is surprised that the current timeline allows an extremely limited period for consideration of a proposal of such significance, when such decisions should never be rushed, and it is imperative that all factors be considered and debated,” he wrote.

“The AFC firmly believes that sufficient time must be afforded for a comprehensive assessment, including appropriate legal and governance due diligence, meaningful consultation and careful consideration of the long-term implications of such an initiative.

“Above all, it is essential that the appropriate Fifa bodies be involved in the decision-making process and that the matter is handled at all times in accordance with the Fifa Statutes and the highest standards of ethics and good governance.”

Uefa will hold an emergency ­meeting of its 55 members on Thursday afternoon to discuss their next steps, with a senior source telling the Guardian on Thursday morning that a boycott of Fifa tournaments would be the main discussion point.

Sports.title: WSL fixtures: London City Lionesses open 2026-27 season against Manchester United
Sports.content:
Those desperate to see what London City Lionesses will look like with two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas in their ranks do not have to wait long, with the big-spending club kicking off the new Women’s Super League season against Manchester United on Friday 4 September.

The Michelle Kang-owned side welcome United to Hayes Lane in the first game of the 2026-27 season, which will also likely feature goalkeeper Mary Earps, who returns to the WSL for an opener against her former club after leaving Paris Saint-Germain to join London City this summer.

The full fixture list for the new season has been announced, and comes after an extremely complex scheduling process, with WSL Football running more that 1.5 billion scheduling iterations as it juggles the stadium availability and broadcast windows following the announcement of the calendars and fixtures of the Premier League, EFL and men’s National League and men’s FA Cup, women’s FA Cup, Carabao Cup, and men’s and women’s Champions League.

Also on the opening weekend, WSL champions Manchester City, who have added the former Arsenal forward Beth Mead and Chelsea defender Niamh Charles to their ranks, begin their title defence against WSL2 champions Birmingham. The Midlands side were promoted alongside Charlton and Crystal Palace with the top flight expanding to 14 teams for the first time.

Arsenal start their campaign against Brighton, who knocked them out of the FA Cup at the quarter-final stage shortly before they earned a draw in the league against the Gunners that handed Manchester City their first title since 2016.

Elsewhere, Charlton, who earned a playoff win over Leicester to earn their promotion at the expense of the WSL’s bottom-placed side, will play Liverpool at home, Tottenham host West Ham, Chelsea welcome Aston Villa to Stamford Bridge and Crystal Palace mark their return to the WSL against Everton.
