Following the 2025-26 transition season, as the top flight expanded to 14 teams, new relegation and promotion rules begin between the top two divisions for next season. The team that finishes top of the WSL2 will be promoted to replace the team relegated from the WSL in bottom place and at the end of the season the teams that finish in second and third place in WSL2 will meet to determine who will face the team that finishes 13th in the WSL in a playoff for a place in the top flight.

Sports.title: Experimental Liverpool down Wrexham thanks to Rio Ngumoha’s winner
Sports.content:
Liverpool turned the Empire State Building red when launching a new away kit on Tuesday but neither they nor Wrexham could illuminate Yankee Stadium 24 hours later. It was rough in the diamond, although Rio Ngumoha’s deflected goal made it two wins out of two for Andoni Iraola on his first pre-season tour as Liverpool head coach.

Ngumoha, a second half substitute who Iraola deployed on the right, satisfied the majority of a 42,204 crowd with a 75th-minute shot that looped in off Wrexham defender Lewis Brunt. Wrexham’s Hollywood co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney (now simply Rob Mac) were in attendance for what the former had labelled a “punch-me moment” but in truth few blows were traded at the iconic baseball stadium.

Liverpool’s preparations for the second game of pre-season were not exactly smooth, in fairness to Iraola’s team. Their flight from Chicago was cancelled on Tuesday night with players and staff on the tarmac ready to take off. Poor weather conditions in the New York area delayed their arrival until the day of the game, and Liverpool only checked into their Midtown hotel around midday. They were flying back to Chicago straight after the match too.

Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch did not make the trip from Liverpool’s training base despite joining up with the squad following their post-World Cup holidays. The game came too early in their pre-season preparations to be considered. With Joe Gomez injured and Federico Chiesa also absent through illness, Iraola had little choice but to select another young and experimental side. Six of Liverpool’s starting line-up had no Premier League experience whatsoever but at least the emphasis on youth offered the crowd a glimpse of the highly-rated Joshua Abe.

View image in fullscreen Joshua Abe reacts after failing to score at Yankee Stadium. Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images

Abe, a pacy and prolific right winger, is regarded as one of the brightest prospects in the country and was inundated with offers before committing his future to Liverpool when turning 16 earlier this month. Manchester City, Manchester United and Chelsea were all interested in the Warrington-born England youth international, with deals worth £40,000-a-week reportedly on his table. There was understandable relief inside Anfield when he agreed scholarship terms in June with a three-year professional contract to follow on his 17th birthday next July.

Abe could have marked his first senior Liverpool start with an early goal when released clear of the Wrexham defence by Harvey Elliott. A heavy first touch gave the Wrexham and former Liverpool goalkeeper Danny Ward opportunity to save at the feet of the teenager. Iraola started with a front line of Calum Scanlon, Lewis Koumas and Abe. Koumas went close from distance and had a penalty shout waved away but, aside from a few surging midfield runs by Dominik Szoboszlai, it was a quiet friendly.

Wrexham are further along in their pre-season work – their first competitive game is a week on Friday against Middlesbrough in the Carabao Cup – and it showed as the first half progressed and Phil Parkinson’s team gained a physical edge. Sam Smith and Callum Doyle were unable to trouble Giorgi Mamardashvili with the chances that fell their way.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Abe, Scanlon, Milos Kerkez and Trey Nyoni were replaced at half-time by Ngumoha, Kieran Morrison, Kostas Tsimikas and Curtis Jones respectively. Elliott was presented with a sight of the Wrexham goal by Koumas minutes after the restart but his first-time shot from 20 yards was well saved by Ward. The Wales international also denied Szoboszlai from distance but this was a Liverpool performance – and pre-season friendly – that failed to ignite.

Wrexham substitute Nathan Broadhead almost succeeded with a powerful drive from 25 yards that was pushed away by Mamardashvili. Brunt and Kieffer Moore both had good late chances to equalise but miscued from close range.

Sports.title: England’s 1966 World Cup heroes were fun, humble and unlike today’s stars
Sports.content:
With each passing World Cup I am reminded of the times I spent in the company of those wonderful “Boys of 66”. What a privilege it was getting to know them in a much simpler era when, unlike today’s mollycoddled stars, household names remained unaffected by money and fame.

Where were you on 30 July 1966, the day England won the World Cup? I was at my nan and grandad’s house. They had a minute television which seemed no bigger than a matchbox. Intermittently the picture, which was in black and white, would roll around the screen. It was infuriating. My grandad talked about needing to get the “horizontal hold fixed” (unless you are of a certain age you will need to Google that). I was nine years old.

Thirty years (of hurt) on from that final, there was a knock at my front door. It was a surreal experience to see Geoff Hurst standing on my doorstep and even more bizarre as he went to one end of my front room and stood behind the settee. I went to the other end and sat on a chair.

Geoff, England’s World Cup hat- trick hero, had come to my house to rehearse his after-dinner speech. The settee acted as a makeshift top table. I was the only member of his audience.

His performance began. “I was at Paddington station one day and a chap came running up to me and said, ‘Geoff, Geoff, I’ve been waiting 20 years to meet you, I know exactly where I was that day in 1966 when you scored your hat-trick.’ ‘Where was that?’ asked Geoff. ‘Pentonville prison,’ replied the man. ‘We were so happy we smashed the cell up.’”

I had written some of Geoff’s script and I helped him with his presentation, but he quickly became a natural performer.

Another of Geoff’s stories provides a fascinating insight into how the manager, Alf Ramsey, made sure his players never became complacent. In one England match Hurst played in, after the World Cup final, the players returned to the team hotel. They said their goodbyes and Hurst turned to Ramsey and said: “See you next time Alf.”

“Perhaps, Geoff, perhaps,” replied Ramsey. Geoff said it was a comment that really made him think that, despite scoring a hat-trick, his place wasn’t guaranteed.

Ramsey’s starting salary as England manager was £4,500 a year rising to a maximum of £5,000. He also asked the Football Association to help him buy a house.

In the 1980s, and for many years afterwards, there was a huge circuit of sporting dinners. They were often in the north of England and held at the traditional working men’s clubs. Many of the 1966 England team were regular performers. Unlike today’s Premier League stars, who earn hundreds of thousands of pounds a month the “Boys of 66” supplemented their income by performing on the circuit, which is where I got to know them.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Charlton raises the Jules Rimet trophy in the air after the 1966 final at Wembley. Photograph: Hulton Archive/Getty Images

Sometimes they would do their own routines, on other occasions I would interview them and tee them up for their anecdotes. On stage one night I said to Jack Charlton: “Jack, how’s your brother Bobby?” Bobby could sometimes be very serious and he didn’t smile very often. “Not great” replied Jack. “Oh, why’s that?” I enquired. “Well, he’s now been banned from his local pub, the landlord said he didn’t want him there during the happy hour.”

Those England players were involved in English sport’s greatest day but you would never have known. They didn’t act like unapproachable superstars. If I left a message on their home answerphone they would call straight back. It was so different to the majority of football personalities I tried to interview in later years for the BBC.

Some of the events I worked at with the 1966 team were for amateur football clubs. We would be part of the entertainment alongside a tribute act, or a local comedian. The evening would sometimes start with a game of bingo. One dinner was very different. I was asked by the Institute of Directors to host a show and book as many of the England team as possible for a corporate lunch in London. I waited in the green room and they started filling in. It was like being in a dream and I imagined I was in the Wembley dressing room. In they trooped: George Cohen, Ray Wilson, Nobby Stiles, Hurst, Roger Hunt, Alan Ball, Martin Peters, Bobby and Jack Charlton, and for good measure BBC TV’s Kenneth Wolstenholme, who delivered the greatest commentary line in the history of sports broadcasting.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Stiles was a great raconteur. One of his favourite anecdotes was based around the game England played against Argentina in the quarter-final. Before the match, Nobby, the hard man of the team, was taken to one side by Ramsey. “Nobby, Argentina’s best player is Antonio Rattín, I want you to mark Rattín,” said Ramsey. After a perfectly timed pause Nobby delivered the punchline: “Alf, do you want me to mark him for the match or for his entire life?”

View image in fullscreen England’s manager Alf Ramsey (left) celebrates his team’s 4-2 victory over West Germany with the captain, Bobby Moore, and Nobby Stiles. Photograph: Keystone/Getty Images

It was a story that brought the house down.

In 1982 I was asked by Ian Thomas, my editor at BBC Radio Sport, to meet Ramsey at Liverpool Street station. Ramsey had been booked by the BBC to give his reaction to the draw for the 1982 World Cup finals. He immediately reminded me of Captain Mainwaring from Dad’s Army. He spoke with a posh voice, in clipped tones, and came across as a very serious man. I was just 24 years old, and I couldn’t believe my luck.

These were very different times. I still find it incredible that, on the morning of the 1966 final, Peters told me that, “time seemed to be dragging” so some of the players went shopping on Hendon’s high street. And after England’s win at Wembley the FA arranged an evening banquet for the players but, astonishingly, their wives were not invited. The players were very angry and when the dinner finished Hurst told me that he and several of the other players and their wives headed to Danny La Rue’s cabaret club.

How times have changed and how lucky was I knowing the 1966 team? They were humble and really fun to be with and I still find it incredible that I spent so many great times with them.

Garry Richardson presents a special 1966 World Cup anniversary programme on Boom Radio on 30 July

Sports.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
Sports.content:
Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta.

As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

The dispute over the islands, which have been ruled by Britain since 1833, is long running and led to a 74-day conflict in 1982, during which more than 900 people – 649 Argentinians and 255 Britons – lost their lives.

Fifa’s disciplinary code ­prohibits “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature” and the banner prompted political debate on both sides of the ­Atlantic. A spokesperson for the then UK prime minister, Keir Starmer, said: “The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands ­definitely are.” Andrew Giuliani, the head of the White House Fifa taskforce, defended Argentina’s players, saying the US believed in free speech.

The incident was not the first time an Argentina team had expressed such sentiments. In 2014, Fifa fined Argentina £20,000 for a far larger banner held ‌up by players before a friendly with Slovenia in La Plata.

Fifa’s full World Cup charge sheet against the Argentinian Football Association also includes ­“discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, failure to comply with match and security protocols, the display of inappropriate messages by the team and spectators and the throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches”.

0:18 Ugly scenes as Argentina lose World Cup final – video

Several players are also under investigation in relation to the ­chaotic scenes that followed ­Argentina’s 1-0 extra-time defeat by Spain in the final. As Spain attempted to celebrate, ­altercations broke out across the pitch at New York New Jersey Stadium.

The Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes, who was seen wrestling Spain’s Eric García to the ground, faces three counts of assault under the Fifa disciplinary code, while the defender Nahuel Molina faces two counts of assault (one completed and one attempted) and one count of unsporting behaviour.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The assistant coach, Roberto Ayala, faces one count of assault, and Thiago Almada, an unused substitute in the final, one count of unsporting behaviour. Spain’s Gavi also faces an unsporting behaviour charge.

“In accordance with the Fifa ­disciplinary code, the respondents have now been provided with the opportunity to present their position, following which a decision will be issued by the Fifa disciplinary committee in due course,” said Fifa.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Jack Grealish to make Saudi switch to Al-Hilal?
Sports.content:
Having been left behind like an unloved t-shirt by Enzo Maresca as Manchester City departed for their pre-season tour of Asia, Jack Grealish is attracting admiring glances from elsewhere. Eyeing up the England attacker’s shapely calves are Al-Hilal of the Saudi Pro League, who would certainly have the funds to fulfil City’s desire of slapping a big ‘SOLD’ sticker on Grealish and preparing him for international shipping.

The latest highly-touted prospect set to be whisked away after an impressive short stint at Bournemouth is Rayan. Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, PSG, Arsenal, and Liverpool all want the Brazilian winger. The link with Andoni Iraola at Anfield appears strong, but with the 19-year-old’s release clause not said to kick in until 2027, the fee required to move him from the south coast would be significant. Although probably still less than the price of a Bradley Barcola.

There’s been more outs than ins at Crystal Palace this summer and that looks set to continue after a move for Augsburg’s Chrislain Matsima stalled. The French defender, 24, had been lined up as the replacement for Maxence Lacroix, who is on the verge of being shown Jordan Henderson’s magic tricks at Chelsea.

Inter Milan’s remarkably coherent cohort of cast-offs could well be joined by Curtis Jones. The Liverpool midfielder has been consistently linked with the Serie A club this summer, but the sticking point appears to be price. The Reds rejected a £21.5m offer back in June and were said to be seeking closer to £35m for the 25-year-old. With Inter potentially saving some of their transfer kitty earmarked for Cristian Romero by instead moving for free agent John Stones, they may be able to find a little more cash down the back of the sofa to return to Liverpool with a revised bid.

Aston Villa have a few readies burning a hole in their pocket after trousering £117m for Morgan Rogers, and want to spend some of it on a Brazilian striker named after a Surrey golf club member, Allan of Palmeiras. Villa have gone in with a £26m offer for the 22-year-old but the São Paulo club think they can extract a bit more than that – at least £12m more, in fact.

Danny Welbeck’s impending arrival at Cobham looks likely to push Liam Delap down the pecking order at Chelsea and Everton are “ready to revive” their interest. The Toffees have been persistent in suggesting they would like to offer the 23-year-old a platform to reboot his career, and may now actually do something about it.

Another Englishman looking for an upturn in fortunes is Kalvin Phillips, who remarkably is still officially on the books at Manchester City. Last season the midfielder spent some time on loan at Sheffield United and it seems that worked well for everyone, as the Blades want to bring the Yorkshire-born metronome back to Bramall Lane.

Sports.title: Manchester City leading opposition to Premier League’s £1.5bn EFL proposal
Sports.content:
Manchester City are leading the opposition to the Premier League’s plans to offer £1.5bn to the English Football League in a landmark financial settlement which will be discussed at a meeting of the 20 clubs on Thursday.

The Premier League wants to put its proposed offer, which would be spread over 10 years, to a vote in the hope of getting the matter resolved before the start of the season, but City are understood to have come up with a counterproposal amid concerns about how the package will be funded.

A number of City’s misgivings are shared by other members of the so-called big six, who will be asked to pay more than other Premier League clubs towards the New Deal for Football, but it is unclear how many of them are prepared to back their rivals.

City remain short of allies within the top flight as they wait for the much-anticipated judgment of an independent tribunal after being charged with 115 breaches of financial fair play rules, despite settling a long-running legal dispute with the Premier League over its associated party transaction rules last year.

Quick Guide How do I 

The Guardian has learned that City irritated several clubs by submitting a series of late amendments to proposed rule changes before the Premier League’s annual general meeting in June, which were defeated by 19 votes to one.

City and other big clubs are understood to be unhappy with the Premier League’s proposal to fund the financial redistribution package by increasing the levy on transfer fees from 4% to 6%, which would leave the bigger spending clubs with a large bill. The Premier League will only ballot clubs on Thursday if it is confident of getting the 14 votes required for the proposal to pass, with sources describing executives as cautiously optimistic despite facing some opposition.

At an average of £150m a year, the Premier League’s proposed contribution has not altered significantly since a similar offer of £750m over five years was put forward in September 2023, although it has doubled the length of the deal.

If approved by the clubs and accepted by the EFL an initial payment of £100m would be made this season, with larger contributions to be made in subsequent years until the 2035-36 season.

It is unclear whether the EFL would accept the Premier League’s first offer however, with its chair, Rick Parry, believed to be holding out for a bigger deal.

If approved the EFL would allocate 80% of the New Deal to the Championship clubs, 12% to League One and 8% to League Two.

City and the Premier League declined to comment.

Sports.title: Arne Slot in line for surprise new job after Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit
Sports.content:
Arne Slot in line for surprise new job after Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit

Arne Slot is a candidate to replace Matthias Jaissle as Al Ahli manager, talkSPORT understands.

Jaissle is set to take over as Newcastle boss, with Eddie Howe leaving the club after five years in charge.



3 Slot is a contender to replace Jaissle at Al Ahli in a surprise move after leaving Liverpool Credit: Getty

The German headed to Saudi Arabia in 2023 to take over Al Ahli, leaving his role with Red Bull Salzburg for the Middle East.

During his three years in the job, he has won 92 of his 138 games, winning back-to-back Asian Champions League titles.

But he's now heading for the Premier League to replace Howe, which leaves the Al Ahli hotseat vacant.



And that could end up being filled by former Liverpool boss Slot.

Slotting in?

Slot was sacked by the Reds in May after just over two seasons in charge of the club, winning the top-flight title in 2025.

Since then, he hasn't taken on another role, despite being approached by Fulham to become their manager.



He rejected that offer, with the Cottagers then going on to appoint ex-Real Madrid boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

The Dutchman was also linked with the AC Milan job before they appointed Ruben Amorim, while he was tipped to potentially become the next Netherlands boss too.



However, he remains a free agent and he is now on the radar of Al Ahli now that Jaissle is on his way to Newcastle.

Slot is one of multiple contenders for the job, including someone he has come up against before in the Premier League...

3 Slot has been linked with multiple jobs but could now end up in Saudi Arabia Credit: AFP

Vying for Vitor

As well as being interested in Slot, Al Ahli also appreciate former Wolves and Nottingham Forest manager Vitor Pereira.



No approach has been made yet, but Pereira is an option.

He has had three different roles over the last two years, becoming Wolves boss in 2024 after leaving Al Shabab.

The 58-year-old has experience in Saudi Arabia, as he spent 10 months in the Saudi Pro League with Al Shabab, while he also previously managed Al Ahli in 2013.

Pereira was sacked by Wolves in November 2025 after losing eight of the first 10 games of last season.

Just four months later, he was then named Nottingham Forest manager, but that stint only lasted a short period.



3 Pereira is another candidate to take over at Al Ahli when Jaissle leaves Credit: Getty

Pereira was blindsided, as he was dismissed by Forest at the start of July, despite achieving Premier League safety and reaching the Europa League semi-finals last term.

Now, he has Al Ahli interested and that could end up seeing him return to Saudi Arabia for a third spell in the Middle East.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi teases imminent Tottenham transfer ‘bomba’ after pre-season game
Sports.content:
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi teased a transfer 'bomba' is not far away.

Spurs have been one of the busiest Premier League teams in the summer window and have broken their transfer record twice.



3 De Zerbi has given his squad a serious face-lift ahead of the new season Credit: Getty

Matheus Fernandes was the first to raise the bar when he joined for £85million from West Ham United, only to be usurped days later by Sandro Tonali's £100m arrival.

Tottenham has also undergone a significant revamp at the back, headlined by the £52m addition of Jan Paul van Hecke along with Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, who both joined on free transfers.

'Bomba' inbound

Despite the large number of incomings, De Zerbi believes the club's transfer dealings are only '60 per cent' complete.



But that number looks set to increase once the Italian lands yet another new face.

"In the transfer market, when I want one player, I become like a shark, no chance to say no," De Zerbi told football.london after the club's penalty shootout win over Sydney FC.



"The transfer market, it's not finished for sure, but we completed 60 per cent of our project in the transfer market.

"Now we have another bomba!"

For those of you not chronically online, 'bomba' is a Gen Z phrase which roughly translates to 'significant transfer development'.



De Zerbi confirmed this particular 'bomba' was in relation to a forward.

And when pressed on whether the deal was close to completion, the Italian replied: "I hope, but it's not finished for sure."

3 Savinho has been wanted by Spurs for a number of windows now Credit: Getty

It is also believed the transfer is separate to Spurs' pursuit of Manchester City winger Savinho.



talkSPORT understands Savinho has already informed City he would like to join, with Spurs working on a deal worth approximately £60m.

Rash decision?

One name who would certainly fit the bill of a transfer 'bomba' is Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford.

The 28-year-old is due to report back to Carrington for United's pre-season preparations after Barcelona opted not to sign him permanently following a season-long loan.

Rashford has not played for the Red Devils since 2024 and although boss Michael Carrick previously promised a clean slate for the forward, the club is still expected to try and offload him before the window shuts.



Tottenham could stand to be the beneficiaries of United's desire to move Rashford on, and it's a deal talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook claimed was certainly possible.

3 Rashford will join a new club off the back of a World Cup Credit: Getty

"I think if he goes anywhere in London, I'm keeping an eye on Tottenham," Crook said on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs.

"I could see that deal happening. Roberto De Zerbi believing that he can get the best out of Marcus Rashford."



Away from transfers, De Zerbi is in the midst of his first pre-season as Spurs boss.

The north London side is next in action on Saturday against Premier League rivals Chelsea, with the match taking place at Accor Stadium in Sydney, Australia.

Spurs' clash against the Blues comes after they drew 1-1 with Sydney FC on Wednesday, although De Zerbi's side came away as winners following a post-match penalty shootout.

Sports.title: Lewis Hall tipped for immediate £50m exit after Eddie Howe quits Newcastle
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe will leave Newcastle and it could turn into open season for St James’ Park transfers.

Lewis Hall could be one out of the door this summer and Manchester United have been told to go all out for the left-back.

4 Hall has established himself as one of the top left-backs in the Premier League Credit: Getty

Howe will leave as Magpies boss just weeks before the start of the season to leave the North East club in complete disarray.

The 53-year-old is said to have informed the club of his decision several weeks ago, but stayed on while a replacement was found. That will be Al Ahli coach Matthias Jaissle.

Newcastle have already sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali, meanwhile Arsenal are pushing to sign club captain Bruno Guimaraes.

Lewis Hall transfer

talkSPORT's Inside Devils panel want Man United to make a bid for the 21-year-old defender as soon as possible.

The former Chelsea player made 46 appearances under Howe last year, scoring once and registering an assist.

He was unlucky to miss out on a place in England's World Cup squad to the USA, Canada and Mexico.

Man United are expected to add a new left-back to their squad, as Michael Carrick plans to build depth ahead of a return to the Champions league.

So far this summer, the Manchester-based outfit have added midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and goalkeeper Karl Darlow to their ranks.

Those three signings aren't enough, according to talkSPORT pundit Flex, who began: "I think we need to do everything we can to get Lewis Hall. Newcastle United is a tough place at the minute.

Rippling the Toon

"There's Bruno Guimaraes who’s probably about to leave for Arsenal, then [Sandro] Tonali and [Anthony] Gordon are already gone.

4 Howe delivered a first trophy in 70 years for Newcastle Credit: Getty

"People are looking around the place, and players are probably thinking, 'what’s happening here?'

"Harvey Barnes has committed his future, but there were rumours and reports that he [Hall] might have been a bit agitated.

"[Athletic writer] Andy Mitten has been talking, saying he’s someone who Manchester United like.

"We’re not in charge of the purse, but I’m saying you slap £50million down - opening bid - and just ruffle some feathers in there.

"Newcastle could say, 'Listen, we can’t have this because fans are going to turn this place upside down.'

"You can’t lose Tonali, Guimaraes, Gordon and Hall in one window, plus Isak last season. They will say absolutely not. So for the fans, they might put their foot down and say, 'Sorry Lewis'.

4 Hall was a standout player for the North East side last term, despite not being picked for the World Cup squad Credit: Getty

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. MUTV is the home of all Manchester United pre-season fixtures. It’s the opportunity to watch new faces, young players, returning names, tactical clues and the first signs of what United might become over the next season. MUTV on Sky: £7 extra a month. Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

"But then he might put his foot down and say, ‘I’m off, I don’t want to play here.'"

Newcastle denied any falling out between Hall and Howe following media reports which highlighted the player's frustrations.

However, leading up to the World Cup, the youngster was granted limited minutes towards the conclusion of the campaign.

It is understood he feels the lack of game time was a factor that contributed to his omission from the Three Lions squad that travelled stateside.

Newcastle eventually finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League, having achieved a fifth-placed finish to secure Champions League qualification the previous year.

4 Shaw has played nearly every minute under Carrick Credit: Getty

Levelling up

Presenter Angelina Kelly added: "If I was Lewis Hall I would feel disrespected that you’ve lost your place to Dan Burn. That cost him his place at the World Cup, essentially because of what Eddie Howe decided to do at Newcastle.

"So, I would be absolutely fuming if I was him, and I would be looking at Newcastle and thinking, ‘you don’t value me, so I’m going to go somewhere that will.’

"I think Man United would value him because, we have to be honest about our full-backs, we’ve been struggling.

"Are Diogo Dalot and Luke Shaw of the calibre we need to challenge for a Premier League title? No."

Newcastle have not sold a player to United since Andy Cole completed a then-British record £7million move in January 1995.

Hall scored twice at Old Trafford during the 2023/24 campaign in what was a 3-0 victory for Newcastle in the Carabao Cup and again in a 3-2 defeat at the end of that season.

Sports.title: Manchester City agree Ayyoub Bouaddi deal but talks continue over possible discount clause
Sports.content:
Manchester City agree Ayyoub Bouaddi deal but talks continue over possible discount clause

Manchester City have agreed terms with Ayyoub Bouaddi, talkSPORT understands.

The Premier League giants are in advanced talks with Lille to sign the breakout World Cup star.

2 City have continued their pursuit of Bouaddi Credit: Getty

It remains to be seen whether he immediately goes into City's squad for the 2026/27 season or gets loaned back to Lille for one year.

As talkSPORT reported at the beginning of July, Lille are seeking a fee of €100million (£86m) for the Morocco international.

They are willing to discount the price if a loan or pre-agreement can be reached with City, although the English club's preference is to sign and keep him.

Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Bayern Munich are also understood to have shown interest in Bouaddi.

Midfield overhaul

A deal for Bouaddi could lead to Rodri leaving City for Real Madrid.

Madrid have opened initial talks to sign the Spanish midfielder, who has made it clear that he wants to move.

City are keen to keep Rodri beyond the summer even if he doesn't sign a new contract, with his current deal expiring in June 2027.

However, the Premier League giants would be more inclined to let him leave if they sign Bouaddi.

Ahead of their first campaign under Enzo Maresca, City have already spent big in the market.

They completed a £116m move for Elliot Anderson, who joined from Nottingham Forest at the start of the month.

2 City are keen to complete a transfer now rather than next summer Credit: Getty

It was a British record fee at the time, but Chelsea surpassed it when they splashed £117m on Morgan Rogers.

City begin their season on August 16 when they face Premier League champions Arsenal in the Community Shield.

This will be their first competitive match without Pep Guardiola at the helm in a decade.

A home match against Bournemouth a week later marks the start of their league schedule.

Sports.title: Chelsea transfer spending soars to £280m mark as Maxence Lacroix announced
Sports.content:
Chelsea have announced the signing of Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace.

The centre-back has moved from Selhurst Park to Stamford Bridge in a deal worth a guaranteed £52million.



2 Lacroix has joined Chelsea from Premier League rivals Palace Credit: Getty

Lacroix has become the fifth player to sign for Chelsea this summer, with fellow defender Marco Palestra joining from Atalanta for £47m.

A pre-agreed transfer for striker Emmanuel Emegha has been made official, with the Blues reportedly paying Strasbourg £22m.

Geovany Quenda is another new face after Chelsea hijacked a move from Manchester United to sign him from Sporting for £42m.



Chelsea have also broken the British transfer record with Morgan Rogers, who has arrived from Aston Villa in a £117m switch.

The Blues also remain in talks over the surprise signings of Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson, who have a combined age of 71.



Their summer spending has now reached at least £280m with the arrival of Lacroix.

Lacroix - Chelsea 'best club in the world'

"I am really happy to be part of this beautiful club," Lacroix said upon signing. "Everyone knows the legend of Chelsea, its tradition of winning, and to be a part of that is a proud moment.



"When I spoke with the manager (Xabi Alonso), I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club. We want to win.

"When you see the quality of the players here, everything we have around the club, it's something that we can achieve.

"The ambition is to lift trophies, and I can't wait to contribute."

He added: "I think it's the best move for me because it's the best club in the world.

"I spoke with Malo. I spoke with Trev (Chalobah). I spoke with Benoit (Badiashile). It's easy for people to speak well about this club because it has a lot of big history and I'm really proud to be a part of it now.



"I spoke with the manager on the phone. We spoke about tactics, we spoke about how he sees the game.

"First of all, I was happy just to speak about football with him, and I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

"When I spoke with the gaffer, when I spoke also with the people I know from the national team who play for Chelsea, like Malo, they told me it was the best club I can go to.

"So already I was saying, 'Okay, I don’t need to think too much'. After talking to people I said to myself, 'This is the best step forward for me'."



2 Lacroix has swapped Selhurst Park for Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

Lacroix spent two seasons at Palace, with whom he won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League.

The 26-year-old was named in the Team of the Season for the latter competition, featuring in 14 matches and scoring two goals.

He also has Champions League experience on his CV, having made six appearances for VfL Wolfsburg.



Lacroix was part of the France squad that finished fourth at the World Cup, so is unlikely to join Chelsea on their pre-season tour.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe’s final comments as Newcastle boss hint at imminent player exit
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe admitted Newcastle 'can't control the forces that are at play' as speculation surrounding Bruno Guimaraes continues to swirl.

Those comments proved to be Howe's last in the public eye before his shock departure from the Magpies was revealed on Thursday.

3 Newcastle's transfer dealings are no longer something for Howe to stress over Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands Howe's frustration over big players being sold this summer coupled with Newcastle consistently missing out on their main targets was a factor behind his exit from the club.

Looney Toons

In the last two years, Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have all left Newcastle for big transfer fees.

Gordon and Tonali were among the latest to go, with the former joining Barcelona earlier this summer for £70million.

As for Tonali, he was snapped up by Tottenham for a club-record £100m.

The summer heartbreak may not be done just yet for Toon supporters though as Guimaraes' future is yet to be resolved.

talkSPORT understands Arsenal are in advanced talks with Newcastle over the midfielder, who doubles as the club captain.

The Magpies have denied formal contact, but it is understood progress has been made on a verbal agreement upwards of £75m.

Howe non-committal on Guimaraes' future

And Howe, speaking after Newcastle's 4-1 pre-season loss to Bristol City on Wednesday, conceded 'what will be, will be,' regarding Guimaraes' future.

“Any distraction, it’s not healthy, it's unhealthy,” Howe said.

“So, yeah [it would be negative for the speculation to drag on].

3 Guimaraes has been at Newcastle since January 2022 Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

“But we’re not in control of that. And to some degree, I don’t think Bruno’s in control of that either. What will be, will be.

“We can’t control the forces that are at play here, we’ve just got to make sure that when Bruno comes back, we look after him and he trains well, which I’m sure he will do. And he makes a difference as he always has done.”

Howe also insisted Guimaraes would not follow Isak's suit and allow a transfer saga to drag on throughout the summer.

Last year, Isak went on strike to force a move to Liverpool, which only went through on deadline day last year for a British transfer record fee of £125m.

In contrast, Howe claimed Guimaraes 'has always been committed' to the cause but could not guarantee that would mean the skipper will stay put.

“We’ve spoken numerous times,” Howe said.

3 The potential loss of Newcastle's skipper may have been the final straw for Howe Credit: Getty

“Assurances? I don’t think you can push too hard for those.

“I’ve said many times we want players who are committed, and Bruno has always been committed. His training performances and his game performances have been outstanding, every time he’s worn the shirt, he’s played with the fans by his side. I’d love to see that continue.

“The details [of him coming back] I don’t actually know, but I don’t see any reason why that wouldn’t be the case."

Sports.title: West Ham fans start petition as devastated staff member sacked after 25 years and left in tears
Sports.content:
West Ham fans start petition as devastated staff member sacked after 25 years and left in tears

West Ham's stadium DJ has been left 'absolutely devastated' by the club's decision to axed him as part of its cost-cutting efforts.

"So, got the call that I'm no longer going to be the club's 'button monkey,'" Russ Budden, also known as DJ RussyB, wrote on X.

3 DJ RussyB also explained the decision in a nine-minute video on YouTube Credit: West Ham Network - YouTube

"After 25 years working at the club, my services are no longer needed as they are cutting costs following the club's relegation.

"I'm absolutely devastated. For over 50 per cent of my life I've been working at West Ham, a position I've never taken for granted and was extremely proud to have done.

"Absolutely gutted, maybe the club will change their mind - especially with 50k season ticket holders, would have loved to be pressing that button!"

In a video shared on YouTube, Budden added he 'cried' when he learned of the news.

Hammers fans reacted with disbelief to Budden's announcement and have since launched a petition to reinstate him.

In the petition, Budden is described as 'synonymous with the matchday experience' and 'part of the fabric and identity of West Ham United'.

Hammers' summer of change

The Hammer's cost-cutting measures at the London Stadium comes amid a string of major outgoings ahead of the upcoming Championship season.

Matheus Fernandes was sold to Tottenham for £85million, making him the north London outfit's record signing until it was broken shortly after by Sandro Tonali who joined for £100m.

Crysencio Summerville was another to depart West Ham as he moved to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal in a £68m deal.

But it hasn't been a total fire sale, as the Hammers rejected Brentford's offer for left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf.

3 Bowen will be tasked with leading West Ham out of the Championship at the first attempt Credit: Getty

In another boost for West Ham ahead of the upcoming season, Jarrod Bowen committed his future by inking a revised deal until 2030.

However, talkSPORT understands the new deal includes a clause which would allow Bowen to leave next summer if the club don't secure an instant return to the Premier League.

Bowen had been linked with moves to Liverpool, who were in the market for a Mohamed Salah replacement, as well as Aston Villa.

West Ham's next DJ in waiting?

It remains to be seen if West Ham will find a replacement for DJ RussyB, but they might not have to look terribly far for one if they do decide to take such action.

Hammers goalkeeper Alphonse Areola knows his way around a DJ deck and was captured playing a set hours after the club drew with Bournemouth in February.

Areola headed to The Star of Bethnal Green where, according to pub manager and Hammers fan Archie Balloo, he more than held his own.

3 Areola may have already worked out his post-playing career Credit: Getty

"He was a very good DJ, actually," Balloo told talkSPORT's Rushden and Jacobs.

"I don't want to say surprisingly, but I've seen professional DJs who've been worse than him. He was good.

"I think he read the room. That's kind of the point of the DJ, it's less so about putting physical records anymore. It's about looking out at the crowd, seeing what they respond to. And he managed to get people dancing and people singing along.

"I mean, he's doing what we want from a DJ. He's selecting the right tunes - something you can cut shapes to instead of bailing out."

However, with Areola still contracted to West Ham, he'll need to have his full focus on what happens on the pitch rather than being behind the decks at the London Stadium.

And, if Hammers fans get their wish with the petition to reinstate DJ RussyB, there won't be a need to find someone else to, as Budden himself put it, be the 'button monkey'.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe makes immediate decision on next move after Newcastle exit
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe makes immediate decision on next move after Newcastle exit

Eddie Howe has no immediate plans to return to management after he leaves Newcastle United, talkSPORT understands.

As talkSPORT reported on Thursday morning, Howe will leave his role as manager after nearly five years at the club.



2 Howe is heading out of Newcastle amid a difficult summer Credit: Getty

Howe joined in November 2021, weeks after the club were taken over by the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund.

He led Newcastle to their first trophy in 56 years when they won the Carabao Cup in 2025, and oversaw two Champions League campaigns.

talkSPORT understands he informed the Magpies he wanted to leave weeks ago but stayed until a replacement was found.



Matthias Jaissle, the current head coach at Saudi Pro League club Al Ahli, will replace him.

The summer exits of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali are also understood to be a factor, with Bruno Guimaraes widely expected to leave as well.



What next for Howe?

Howe won 116 of his 231 matches at Newcastle and, coupling this with his success at Bournemouth, would likely be in demand.

However, the 48-year-old is not looking to return to the dugout once he officially departs St. James' Park.



talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara called upon England to replace Thomas Tuchel with Howe after their World Cup semi-final exit this summer.

The Football Association did not make any contact with him when looking for the permanent successor to Gareth Southgate in 2024.

Former Premier League boss Sean Dyche, who replaced Howe at Burnley in 2012, has also backed such an appointment.

2 Howe is unlikely to make an instant return to management Credit: Getty



Plenty of change

News of Howe's exit comes the morning after Newcastle were beaten 4-1 by Championship side Bristol City in a pre-season friendly.

As mentioned earlier, they have lost two key players in Gordon and Tonali this summer in deals worth a combined £170million.

They have joined Barcelona and Tottenham Hotspur respectively, and Arsenal are in advanced talks to sign their club captain Guimaraes.

talkSPORT understands that progress has been made on a verbal agreement worth in excess of £75m.



Newcastle have spent a combined £118m on deals to sign Bazoumana Toure, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen.

However, the outlook at St. James' Park looks very different now that Howe is departing, 22 days before the new Premier League season.

Sports.title: Who is Matthias Jaissle? Newcastle's managerial target has won titles in Austria and Saudi Arabia, bases his style on the likes of Thomas Tuchel and Jurgen Klopp... but had no dreams of becoming a boss!
Sports.content:
Who is Matthias Jaissle? Newcastle's managerial target has won titles in Austria and Saudi Arabia, bases his style on the likes of Thomas Tuchel and Jurgen Klopp... but had no dreams of becoming a boss!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Newcastle's summer of upheaval has continued with news that manager Eddie Howe is leaving.

The stunning news broke on Thursday morning and comes the morning after their 4-1 pre-season defeat at Championship side Bristol City.

With Howe's four-year and eight-month tenure coming to an end, Daily Mail Sport has detailed that Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle is the leading candidate for the role. Newcastle and Al-Ahli are both majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.

The 38-year-old German has held talks with the Newcastle hierarchy about succeeding Howe and has a track record of success despite his relative infancy into first-team management.

His first job only came in January 2021 when he was announced as head coach of Austrian second-tier side Liefering. With just a few months remaining of that campaign he guided them to second place - their joint-highest finish in their history.

That summer he replaced Jesse Marsch as manager of RB Salzburg and the 2021-22 campaign yielded success as he led the club to the domestic double of the Austrian Bundesliga and Austrian Cup titles. He also led the club to the Champions League knockout phase for the first time in their history.

Al-Ahli manager Matthias Jaissle is being lined up to replace Eddie Howe as Newcastle boss

Howe left his role as Newcastle boss on Thursday morning after four years and eight months

Jaissle backed up that silverware with more the following term as Salzburg were crowned Austrian league winners once more. However, he was sacked on the eve of the 2023-24 season with Al-Ahli becoming his next destination.

Joining the Saudi club on a three-year contract, his success has continued in the Middle East - with the club winning their first-ever Asian Champions League title in 2024-25 and repeating the feat this season - with the likes of Ivan Toney, Riyad Mahrez and Edouard Mendy in his side.

His managerial success is the more remarkable considering it is not a career he desired. Having come through Stuttgart's youth system under Thomas Tuchel, Jaissle was a promising young defender at Hoffenheim - who were managed by Ralf Rangnick - before injury befell him. In 2009, the Germany Under-21 international suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear against Hannover and was never the same and eventually retired at 26 years old in 2014.

Reflecting on what could have been, he told Give Me Sport in December 2024: 'My knee injury was a shock. Probably the only advantage of it was that I could start management earlier.

'I am still young for a coach but have quite good experience already. I would still love to be playing, even at 36. I kick every ball when given the chance in training!

'I like to think I'd be in my last season now as a player if I was fit, but that's life, and I am grateful for the next chapter and the opportunities I have had so far.'

His pathway to management began when he was invited by Rangnick, then RB Leipzig's head of sport, onto a trainee programme within the club's youth department. The rest is now history.

Rangnick and Tuchel are two managers Jaissle looks up to as well as someone he could be facing in the opposition dugout next season in Tottenham counterpart Roberto De Zerbi: 'I have had quite a unique coaching path, eventually leading me here to the Al-Ahli job in Saudi Arabia,' he continued.

The 38-year-old German has won silverware at old side RB Salzburg (left) as well as at Al-Ahli

'I have always tried to be authentic as a coach and find my own way. Of course, I have influences. Ralf Rangnick played a big part in developing my ideas because I played under him for most of my playing career. And in my youth, I had Thomas Tuchel, so I have followed his principles and career.

'Then there's Jurgen Klopp - I often looked at the transitions he put in place with Liverpool. In possession, I like how Pep Guardiola finds structure and balance. And there's a lot to take from Roberto De Zerbi's build-up as well.

'It's a constant learning process. And in the next few years, I'm sure there will be a different coach to draw inspiration from. It's not about copying other coaches, it's just about being inspired by them.'

Speaking about his management philosophy to The Athletic in January, he said: 'I want stress on the opponent as soon as possible.

'And when we win the ball, I want to go as quickly as possible towards the opponent's goal. I'm very vertical in that approach.'

With key duo Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali having already departed, and with captain Bruno Guimaraes' future increasingly uncertain, Jaissle will have a big rebuild on his hands if he does swap Saudi for Tyneside.

Compatriots Thomas Tuchel (left) and Jurgen Klopp are among the influences on his tactics

And with all the turmoil going on at St James' Park, club legend Alan Shearer insists Jaissle will need time if he does take the job.

'It's being reported that Matthias Jaissle is set to come in. I think we have to be careful if that is the case not to pile on,' Shearer told Betfair.

'Clearly, he's got a great record in Saudi. Clearly, he's very young and inexperienced. The Premier League is a beast of a league. It's a big ask for anyone to come in and take over after what Eddie's done.

'I don't think it's a great look for what's happening at the minute with Newcastle, you know, it's like what's going on? We're selling all our best players. The fans are seeing [Alexander] Isak go, the fans are seeing Tonali go, the fans are seeing Gordon go.

'My guess is it's probably only a matter of time before Bruno goes, because he'll look at what's happening with all those players and look at what's happening with Eddie and think, 'Well, from a personal point of view, from his point of view, I guess I'm going to be next.

'It's certainly not a good look, and they'll have to navigate some tough waves coming their way now, because it's the unknown. I mean, if Jaissle does come in, you're asking a 38-year-old to come in and navigate very, very tricky waters.'

Buckle up, Newcastle fans, whatever happens.

Sports.title: Manchester City and Lille locked in negotiations over £80m-rated Ayyoub Bouaddi - after Morocco wonderkid's dazzling World Cup
Sports.content:
Talks between Manchester City and Lille are reaching a crucial stage over the transfer of Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is ready to make the move now though his club have been keen to keep him in France for another season as part of negotiations.

City are ready to use him this season with Rodri a target for Real Madrid while interest is building in Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders.

City have lost Bernardo Silva and also have interest from Tottenham in Omar Marmoush and Savinho.

Bouaddi was valued around £60m before the World Cup but is now considered to be worth around £80m.

Man City are stepping up their pursuit for Lille's Moroccan wonderkid Ayyoub Bouaddi

City want to strengthen in midfield with Rodri attracting strong interest from Real Madrid

City also want to add another goalkeeper to replace Leeds-bound James Trafford with Marseille's Geronimo Rulli one name under consideration.

They also want to strengthen at right-back and on the wing with Chelsea's Pedro Neto and Paris St Germain's Ibrahim Mbaye among names discussed.

Sports.title: AC Milan forced to release statement to deny rumour that club legend Franco Baresi had passed away: 'Respect his privacy'
Sports.content:
AC Milan have been forced to release a statement confirming that one of their greatest ever players Franco Baresi is still alive, after online rumours suggested that he had passed away.

The former defender was a one-club man at the San Siro and was named honorary vice-president of Milan following his retirement.

But fans in Italy were prompted on Wednesday to share poignant tributes to the legend also known by the diminutive nickname 'Piscinin' on the pitch after sports newspaper Tuttosport claimed he had passed away.

Tributes were shared by supporters and luminaries alike, with Italy's deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini among those who fell for the misinformation.

In a bid to shut down speculation, Milan stressed in the strongest possible terms that the news was untrue, and urged fans to consider the 'difficult and delicate time' their club legend and his family were going through.

'AC Milan denies the false reports concerning Franco Baresi that have begun circulating in recent minutes,' the club's official statement read.

AC Milan were forced to deny that their club legend Franco Baresi had died on Wednesday

The six-time Serie A champion and World Cup winner made his most recent public appearance at the Winter Olympics' Opening Ceremony

'Franco is going through a difficult and delicate time, and the Club stands firmly alongside him and his family.

'We urge everyone to respect their privacy and refrain from spreading entirely unfounded information.'

Baresi underwent lung surgery in August 2025 to remove a pulmonary nodule, with the 66-year-old then undergoing a course of cancer-prevention immunotherapy.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Baresi is currently being monitored at the Humanitas hospital in Rozzano, in the Milanese suburbs.

He is thought to have pulled out of visiting Milan's pre-season training camp at Milanello earlier this month due to ill-health.

The six-time Serie A winner's last public appearance came as a torchbearer ahead of this year's Winter Olympics, with Baresi handing over the flame alongside his friend and Inter Milan rival Beppe Bergomi inside the San Siro - which played host to Games' Opening Ceremony.

Baresi held the role of club captain for a staggering 15 seasons during his time in red and black, where he cemented his position as one of the greatest defenders in the history of the game.

A World Cup winner with Italy in 1982, he also won three European Cups, and in 1999 was voted Milan's Player of the Century.

Sports.title: Up to his old clicks? Local 'Clicky Ponting' cricket player at centre of 'cheat' row 'used same ploy at previous club'
Sports.content:
The ‘Clicky Ponting’ scandal gripping amateur cricket has spread across Yorkshire amid claims that the man behind it began cheating at a second club five years ago.

Brian Devine, whose club Saltburn CC faces a corruption investigation, has been caught on camera attempting to mislead umpires during a game for his previous side, Pudsey St Lawrence.

Footage of a Bradford Premier League match from August 2021 shows him repeatedly clicking his fingers while opponents are batting, in an apparent effort to mimic the sound of a ball hitting the bat.

At the time, Devine was captain of Pudsey St Lawrence’s second XI. On the day in question, his side restricted their opponents New Farnley to 136 runs in a rain-affected game they eventually lost.

The team came third in the league that year, and fourth in 2022, before winning the title in Devine’s final season at the club. As skipper, he was photographed on the club’s social media feeds brandishing a large trophy.

Only a tiny number of matches were filmed at the time. But statistics survive showing that during the three seasons Devine captained Pudsey St Lawrence, its second XI wicketkeeper Jacob McDonald took 96 catches, an average of 32 per year.

Devine then returned to Saltburn, his childhood club, in 2024 after taking a job as company secretary to a livestock auctioneer in Northallerton.

In the two years that followed his departure, McDonald took 22 and 15 catches respectively. So far this season, he’s managed just five.

Pictured: Brian Devine whose club Saltburn CC faces a corruption investigation after he was spotted 'clicky pointing' during a game

Footage from 2021 shows Devine attempting to mislead umpires during a game for his previous side Pudsey St Lawrence

Footage of Devine flamboyantly clicking his fingers five years ago, which was uncovered by the Daily Mail yesterday, has sparked calls for the Bradford Premier League to mount a formal investigation.

Sources at other clubs now believe umpires in the league, which was founded in 1902, were for years being routinely misled into ruling that opposing batsmen had touched the ball and been caught by McDonald.

‘Our lads have been looking back at surviving film and score books and we have come to the conclusion that he’s been at it for years,’ said a source at one rival club.

‘Young players will have lost opportunities because of this, match results will have undoubtedly been affected, and there is a good case for now stripping Pudsey St Lawrence of its 2023 title.

Devine was a highly competitive and quite bumptious captain, and the bigger question is of course what club staff and his team-mates did or didn’t know about his antics.’

Bradford Premier League officials were not returning calls last night. But a finding of wrongdoing would send shockwaves through Yorkshire cricket.

Pudsey St Lawrence, which was founded in 1845, is one of the most venerable teams in club cricket and produced two of Yorkshire and England’s greatest ever players: Herbert Sutcliffe, who averaged more than 60 in Test matches, and Sir Leonard Hutton, who scored 368 against Australia in 1938.

Martin Reed, Chairperson at Pudsey St Lawrence Cricket Club, told the Daily Mail: 'We were not aware of any issues with Mr Devine's behaviour during his time at the club, nor were concerns raised with us by other clubs or officials.

'Had we been made aware of any issues at the time we would have taken appropriate action.

'It is some time since Mr Devine left Pudsey St Lawrence and we are aware that the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League and Saltburn Cricket Club are currently investigating the matter.'

Sports.title: John Stones arrives in Italy for Inter Milan medical - as Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero: WINDOW WATCH

John Stones arrives in Italy for Inter Milan medical - as Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fulham to spend big on Garcia

Fulham are closing on agreement with Real Madrid over a deal that could be worth £60m for striker Gonzalo Garcia.

Madrid have been discussing a buy-back option and a sell-on percentage as talks draw to a conclusion.

Fulham also working to add midfielder Cesar Palacios on loan from Madrid.

Gonzalo Garcia looks set to join Fulham from Real Madrid in a deal worth £60m

Hull's Nobel quest

Hull are advancing in talks for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Hull had made enquiries and proposed a £15m offer for the 21-year-old who can play centre back and left back.

Rangers tried to sign Mendy a year ago from Real Betis but Vallecano got him for £2.5m and a 20 per cent sell-on clause.

Hull face competition from Ipswich for Burnley's Florentino Luis but have enquired about Augsburg's midfielder Mert Komur.

The Brazilian made 132 appearances for the club scoring 19 goals which included a strike in the Championship play-off final against Luton Town at Wembley.

Atletico reignite Romero interest

Atletico Madrid have rekindled their interest in Tottenham defender Cristian Romero.

The Argentina international's agents held talks with Inter Milan last weekend and director Piero Ausilio confirmed interest but that the deal would be complicated owing to the financial package.

Atletico Madrid are exploring a potential move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero

Atletico had interest last year and are exploring the figures involved in a deal for the 28-year-old Spurs captain again.

Inter are in the market for centre backs this summer, with one new recruit expected to be John Stones if all goes to plan in his medical today.

Stones set for Inter switch

England defender John Stones has arrived in Italy ahead of his medical with Inter Milan.

Stones, 32, left Manchester City at the end of last season following 10 years with the club.

"Sono entusiasta di essere qui". John Stones è arrivato a Milano ⚫️🔵 pic.twitter.com/Xp2rS66VL9 — Fcinter1908 (@fcin1908it) July 30, 2026
