Sports.title: Chelsea complete £52m signing of Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Chelsea complete £52m signing of Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have completed their £52million move for centre-back Maxence Lacroix, taking their summer spend to almost £275m.

The 26-year-old, who played at the World Cup for France, joins the Blues on a contract until 2032 after two seasons with Crystal Palace.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish met in New York ahead of the World Cup final to accelerate talks.

Lacroix brings trophy-winning experience after lifting the FA Cup and Conference League with the Eagles, as well as the Community Shield.

He is their seventh arrival of the summer after Morgan Rogers, Marco Palestra, Geovany Quenda, Denner, Dastan Satpaev and Emmanuel Emegha. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson are expected to complete moves to west London in the coming days.

Palace are making a healthy profit on the Frenchman, a devout Christian, after signing him for £18m from Wolfsburg in 2024.

Maxence Lacroix has swapped south London for west London by joining Chelsea for £52m

LACROIX'S 2025-26 DISPLAY Won the Conference League with Crystal Palace last season

Started 35 Premier League matches and kept 11 clean sheets

Had the best success rate in one-on-one defensive situations of any PL player last season to have faced at least 50, winning possession 50.5% of the time.

Was the only player in the PL last season to record at least 50 tackles (52), 250 clearances (252) and 200 duels won (204)

Ranked 1st at Palace for clearances, 3rd for defensive contributions, 2nd for most accurate passes, and 2nd for interceptions (all per 90)

Was in the Conference League team of the season

Made his France debut on March 26 in an international friendly against Brazil

Played in three World Cup matches, including the third-place match against England

By WOODY BRAY

Lacroix said of his move to Chelsea: 'I am really happy to be part of this beautiful club. Everyone knows the legend of Chelsea, its tradition of winning, and to be a part of that is a proud moment.

'When I spoke with the manager, I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

'We want to win. When you see the quality of the players here, everything we have around the club, it's something that we can achieve. The ambition is to lift trophies, and I can’t wait to contribute.'

The defender also sent a personal message to Palace fans after his departure was confirmed on Thursday morning.

'Dear Palace fans, it has been a true privilege to wear the Eagles shirt and to be part of this club's history.

'The memories I will cherish forever are the love, the unwavering support, and the incredible moments of success we shared together. I have enjoyed some truly unforgettable seasons with you.

'From day one until my very last, I have always felt at home. Selhurst Park will forever hold a special place in my heart, and I already look forward to seeing you all again.

'This is simply my way of saying thank you. Thank you for who you all are and for everything you have given me.

'But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint - Isaiah 40:31 KJV.

'May God bless you all.'

Palace chairman Steve Parish said of Lacroix's departure: 'Max has been fantastic since he came to the club, being a huge part of our trophy-winning seasons and building a special bond with everyone at the club and the supporters.

'Thank you Max, for everything, and all the very best for the next phase of your career.

'As outstanding a figure off the pitch as he has been on it, we are all grateful to him for the role he has played over the last two seasons, and – although we are sad to bid him farewell – we do so wishing him the very best for the future.'

He is expected to play an important first-team role in west London under new manager Xabi Alonso.

The task will be to return the Blues to the Champions League after a dismal end to last season which saw them slip to 10th, as close to the relegation zone on points as the top four.

His switch to Stamford Bridge comes after Daily Mail Sport reported that Italian side Como are willing to offer £35m for Trevoh Chalobah as talks continue over his future.

Como were rebuffed in their opening two proposals for the 27-year-old and are working to meet Chelsea's valuation with a structured offer.

Chalobah was on World Cup duty with England and made a fleeting appearance against France in the hectic third-place match.

Sports.title: England confirm appointment of Stephen Fleming as Test coach - with former captain Joe Root returning to the role
Sports.content:
England confirm appointment of Stephen Fleming as Test coach - with former captain Joe Root returning to the role

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

England have confirmed the appointment of Stephen Fleming as Test coach with Joe Root named as new captain.

Fleming, 53, takes over from fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum, who remains in charge of the white-ball teams, after terminating an 18-year association with Chennai Super Kings.

Thirty-five-year-old Root deputised for the suspended Ben Stokes at The Oval against New Zealand recently and will now extend his record of captaining England more times than anyone else when he leads the team into the three-match series against Pakistan, starting on August 19.

Marcus Trescothick will serve as interim head coach for that series as Fleming has been granted time with his family in New Zealand before beginning the role with the ECB later this summer.

‘I’m incredibly excited to be joining England as Test coach. It’s one of the most prestigious coaching positions in world cricket and I am honoured to be appointed,’ Fleming said.

‘I am looking forward to working with the players and bedding in the gains made by Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes. Of course, the ambition is always to win now. But equally, it’s about ensuring the team is well placed for the medium and long-term future. There is a lot of young talent in and around the team and our aim is to help them fulfil their potential as world-class cricketers.

Stephen Fleming has never coached red-ball cricket before but has been named the new England Test coach

Joe Root will return as Test captain despite former coach Brendon McCullum endorsing Harry Brook for the role

'I’m particularly looking forward to working with Joe Root as captain - a generational talent who has achieved so much already. There is still plenty more to come from him, and I’m excited to support him so he can enjoy and thrive in the role in what is a different context to his first stint.

‘I’m also excited to work with Harry Brook. The best players are never finished products, and helping Harry continue to develop his extraordinary talent and his leadership will be an important part of this journey.’

Root, who will look to add to his England record 27 Test wins as captain on his home ground of Headingley in three weeks’ time, said: ‘It is a great honour and privilege to be asked to be England Test captain again.

‘The Test captaincy is a difficult but hugely rewarding job and, after enjoying a brief taste of it again working with Baz McCullum last month, I am excited to lead this next generation of players forward.

‘The opportunity to do that alongside Stephen is also a huge motivator. He has proved over a long period of time that he is an exceptional leader with a great knowledge of the game, and I am looking forward to working with him and helping to build a winning environment.’

Daily Mail Sport revealed that Root had been lined up to return to the captaincy permanently at the end of the Trent Bridge defeat to New Zealand that brought down the curtain on Stokes’ career and condemned England to a winless sequence in Test series spanning back to 2024.

It was a set of results that cost McCullum his job as all-format coach, but Rob Key, England’s director of cricket, said Root deserved the ‘opportunity to lead free from the Covid restrictions that the Test team faced at the end of his first stint as captain.’

Root’s first spell ended in just one win in 17 matches, but that included a 4-0 Ashes loss down under played under the strictest of restrictions.

Sports.title: Curtis Jones caught appearing to have furious argument with Liverpool team-mates at the end of their pre-season win over Wrexham
Sports.content:
Curtis Jones caught appearing to have furious argument with Liverpool team-mates at the end of their pre-season win over Wrexham

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Curtis Jones appeared to be caught up in a furious discussion with his Liverpool team-mates moments after the Reds won their second pre-season match against Wrexham.

Andoni Iraola's reign continued positively on Wednesday in New York after their opening win against Sunderland on Saturday, with teen talent Rio Ngumoha grabbing the second-half goal necessary to claim the win against Championship opposition.

But after the final whistle, Jones - who had featured as a second-half substitute from the 50th minute - seemingly took issue while speaking to Dominik Szoboszlai on the pitch.

Jones was captured in a fan's video speaking expressively to the Hungary captain, who appeared to be attempting to cool his ire.

After Jones turned his back on Szoboszlai, he was immediately caught up in conversation with Kostas Tsimikas and Jeremie Frimpong, with the latter appearing to push Jones out of potentially stepping forward and starting another conflict.

The 25-year-old was eventually led away from the fray by Frimpong, but continued to seemingly make his case.

Jones right after the game. Think he’s gone to be honest. Was fuming at something or someone pic.twitter.com/ZyUk8Z7Tsu — Arqade (@Arqade4) July 30, 2026

Curtis Jones (hidden left) appeared to engage Liverpool team-mates including Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong in a dispute after beating Wrexham

Academy graduate Jones is widely understood to be set to leave the club this summer, but Liverpool have been firm on their asking price for the midfielder.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that Inter Milan had seen a second attempt to tempt Jones to Serie A rebuffed, with their £21.7million offer deemed too low.

Jones has only one season left on his contract, but the club would prefer to allow him to enter his final year than see him leave this summer for less than their preferred price of between £35m and £40m.

Towards the end of last season under former manager Arne Slot, Jones found himself increasingly frustrated as he missed out on places in the starting XI.

But Liverpool remain keen to stress that they do not wish to push their player - who has been at the club since boyhood - out of the door at Anfield.

At present however, there are no further talks planned for a new deal, with a chasm having opened up between the expectations of player and club.

One midfield academy graduate who enjoyed a brighter night at Yankee Stadium was Trey Nyoni, who played just 21 Premier League minutes last season, but caught the eye in the Bronx.

Sports.title: England name new Test coach as Joe Root returns as captain
Sports.content:
England name new Test coach as Joe Root returns as captain

England have landed Stephen Fleming as their new Test head coach with Joe Root returning for a second spell as captain - four years after stepping down

View 2 Images Stephen Fleming has been named England's Test coach

England have confirmed the appointment of Stephen Fleming as their new Test head coach as Joe Root returns for a second stint as captain.

‌



The ECB have been scouring the market for a new individual to lead the red-ball side after Brendon McCullum was moved aside and told his role is solely focused on limited-overs cricket.

‌



England's Test Series defeat to New Zealand proved the final straw and the country's cricket bosses have again turned to a Kiwi in Fleming.

‌



He has enjoyed an 18-year association with Chennai Super Kings whilst he remains New Zealand’s most successful Test captain. Fleiming knows the English county game well having played for Middlesex, Yorkshire and Nottinghamshire. With the latter he was able to help lead them to a drought-breaking County Championship title in 2005.

Fleming has also led Southern Brave to the final of The Hundred men's competition in 2023 and his role with England starts after the beginning of the Test Series against Pakistan, which will see Marcus Trescothick come in as interim Head Coach.

He said: “I’m incredibly excited to be joining England as Test Coach. It’s one of the most prestigious coaching positions in world cricket and I am honoured to be appointed.

‌



"I am looking forward to working with the players and bedding in the gains made by Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes. Of course, the ambition is always to win now. But equally, it’s about ensuring the team is well placed for the medium and long-term future. There is a lot of young talent in and around the team and our aim is to help them fulfil their potential as world-class cricketers.

“I’m particularly looking forward to working with Joe Root as Captain - a generational talent who has achieved so much already. There is still plenty more to come from him, and I’m excited to support him so he can enjoy and thrive in the role in what is a different context to his first stint."

View 2 Images Joe Root is back for a second spell as captain

Article continues below

Root initially stepped down as England captain in 2022 after a damaging defeat in the West Indies and confessed that leading the side had taken a "toll" and "impact" on him.

Despite that, the Yorkshireman is back in the role and has said: “It is a great honour and privilege to be asked to be England Men’s Test captain again. The Test captaincy is a difficult but hugely rewarding job and, after enjoying a brief taste of it again working with [Brendon] McCullum last month, I am excited to lead this next generation of players forward.

"The opportunity to do that alongside Stephen is also a huge motivator. He has proved over a long period of time that he is an exceptional leader with a great knowledge of the game, and I am looking forward to working with him and helping to build a winning environment."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua opponent finally addresses fight 'fix' claim
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua opponent finally addresses fight 'fix' claim

Kristian Prenga knocked down Anthony Joshua twice last weekend before being knocked down and out in the second round, prompting conspiracy claims to be made

View Image Anthony Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga (Image: Getty Images)

Kristian Prenga has lashed out at Simon Jordan over his claim his fight with Anthony Joshua was fixed.

Prenga knocked down Joshua twice in the opening session last weekend before being knocked down and out in the second round, prompting talkSPORT pundit Jordan to share a conspiracy theory. He wrote on social media: "Not having that [in the] Anthony Joshua fight. Dropped twice and sets the tempo, how’s that? Prenga totally different in second [round]. Something not quite right, all designed to rinse maximum amount of money."

But asked about those comments, Prenga told SveaCasino: "What do I make of Simon Jordan’s comments? Completely false, and irresponsible for anyone to suggest it. AJ and I have integrity, we would never engage in this stupidity. I felt I needed to preserve energy and catch my breath, so I thought I would start slow and replenish my energy. Unfortunately, it didn't happen, and that slower pace allowed AJ to flip control of the fight to him."

Anthony Joshua survives knockdowns to KO Kristian Prenga in Tyson Fury warm-up READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua team member slams Simon Jordan after wild conspiracy theory READ MORE :

Prenga also revealed he was ill during training camp, and added: "What did I learn? Try not to get sick during training camp because you feel the difference from losing those training days and cardio workouts after the first round."

Earlier this week, Sergey Lapin, Director of Team Usyk, also hit back at Jordan's remarks. Joshua teamed up with the Ukrainian's team prior to his bout with YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul back in December - and Lapin once again played a key role on Saturday night.

In an interview with Action Network, Lapin said: "What do I think of Simon Jordan’s comments? I suppose they also told Prenga to walk straight into a punch that weighed one and a half tonnes. Everyone is entitled to their own theories. I have a friend who still believes the Earth is flat and that space doesn’t exist. Personally, I’d rather discuss what actually happened inside the ring than someone else’s imagination."

Sports.title: ‘I do not believe I should’ve lied’ - Oisin Murphy defends conduct at Goodwood inquiry
Sports.content:
‘I do not believe I should’ve lied’ - Oisin Murphy defends conduct at Goodwood inquiry

The four-time champion jockey posted a statement after being accused of not arguing that interference had cost him victory in the first race on Wednesday

View 2 Images Oisin Murphy: defended his evidence (Image: Getty Images)

Oisin Murphy has defended his conduct at the Goodwood stewards inquiry, saying, “I do not believe I should have lied”.

‌



The four-time champion jockey riding Hatteen came off second best to the Tom Marquand-ridden Infraad in the first race on Wednesday. The two were separated by a head.

‌



But the stewards called an inquiry into interference on the run to the line after the winner edged to the left, slightly taking Murphy’s mount off his line. The hearing was broadcast on ITV when both jockeys gave evidence before the panel ruled that the interference was accidental and that Marquand had made every effort to correct his horse.

‌



Murphy told the stewards said: "My horse is running straight and Tom's horse is a bit more babyish. We never made contact.

“I didn't know Tom's horse had shifted until quite close to the line. I can't for any certainty say I would have won if Tom's horse hadn't shifted out."

However Murphy’s evidence did not satisfy some punters with controversial podcast The Barstewards Enquiry labelling his testimony as “disgraceful”.

‌



View 2 Images Infraad (far side) and Hatteen finished just a head apart at Goodwood (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

Their post said: “Whether it's the correct call or not, that was disgraceful from Oisin Murphy in the stewards, you argue a case for the people you are riding for, not go in there saying 'there is nothing to see here’.

Responding directly, Murphy said: “With regards to my evidence in the stewards enquiry after Race 1 at Goodwood today. I felt my horse had every chance in the race.

Article continues below

“He went a head up about a furlong out. I believe Tom Marquand did everything he could to stay straight.

“I do not believe I should’ve lied in order to attempt to have the result called in my favour. I wouldn’t want it happening to me.”

Sports.title: Eddie Howe's final words as Newcastle boss speak volumes after Toon exit
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe's final words as Newcastle boss speak volumes after Toon exit

Eddie Howe confessed in his final interview as Newcastle boss that more change was on the cards with Bruno Guimaraes' sale still very much a possibility in the transfer market

Eddie Howe to step down as Newcastle manager

Eddie Howe didn't shy away from admitting there was "potentially more upheaval to come" in his final Newcastle interview as his five-year spell comes to an end.

‌



The Englishman took charge of the Magpies when they were in the relegation zone and has since made them a Champions League outfit and a side who claim silverware.

‌



Those glory days do appear a thing of the past and the Newcastle decline has been notable, owing to them selling the bulk of their leading lights. Alexander Isak's forced exit last summer set in motion a period of events that has led to Howe quitting the club.

‌



A dire off-season of transfer business meant Newcastle finished last year in 12th. They've since lost Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali whilst Bruno Guimaraes has made it clear he wants to move to Arsenal - and Howe claimed more changes are likely.

Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle with immediate effect as replacement lined up READ MORE :

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has left Newcastle just 24 days before the Premier League starts (Image: Ian MacNicol, Getty Images)

He said: "There's been a lot of upheaval at the football club with potentially more to come. I think there's always reasons to be optimistic and that's very much my default setting. I believe great things are possible every season with a real buzz of what's ahead. I see no reasons to be any different this year."

‌



His comments came after a 4-1 humiliation at Championship side Bristol City, which was far from the ideal preparation for the new Premier League season. It did not show a team in harmony despite several first-team stars running out at Ashton Gate.

Howe has earned huge plaudits for the work he's done at St James' Park but he's seen his best players leave over the last year and Guimaraes, who has not yet returned to the squad, is the latest to want out. The former Bournemouth boss conceding he wasn't getting any promises that the Brazilian would remain.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe was determined to keep hold of Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

‌



He told the Chronicle: "We’ve spoken numerous times. Assurances? I don’t think you can push too hard for those. I’ve said many times we want players who are committed, and Bruno has always been committed.

"His training performances and his game performances have been outstanding, every time he’s worn the shirt, he’s played with the fans by his side. I’d love to see that continue."

Howe also admitted: "What will be, will be. We can’t control the forces that are at play here".

‌



It will no longer be Howe who is left to pick up the pieces from that decision with the 48-year-old walking away from the job. "Every day as Newcastle manager is a great day for me. I absolutely love the football club and that will never change," he said less than 24 hours before leaving."

Sports.title: 19 countries have pulled out of World Cup as UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino boycott
Sports.content:
19 countries have pulled out of World Cup as UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino boycott

A potential World Cup boycott is being considered following revelations this week

View 5 Images Gianni Infantino is under major fire for his FIFA sale plans (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

UEFA are threatening to boycott the World Cup if Gianni Infantino goes forward with his plans to sell off part of FIFA. The governing body's president is considering selling shares to private investors to create a £15billion ($20bn) subsidiary.

‌



UEFA will hold an emergency meeting at 2pm today to ward off FIFA's attempt to launch a new commercial company with outside investment. Infantino wants to sell off more than 20% of the FIFA Forward Enterprise and raise £3.16bn ($4.2bn).

‌



It is reported that these plans were not raised during meetings with football associations in New York the night before the World Cup final. UEFA said in a statement: "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously.

‌



"So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino responds to furious backlash over World Cup sale as nations consider boycott READ MORE :

UEFA holding emergency meeting over World Cup boycott to stop FIFA villain Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."

‌



In the wake of this, Mirror Football examines previous occasions when nations have withdrawn from the World Cup.

Uruguay - 1934

The reigning world champions were due to head to the second edition of the tournament in 1934, having triumphed four years earlier. However, they withdrew in protest after several European sides refused to travel to South America for the 1930 World Cup in Uruguay.

The 1934 World Cup remains the only edition where the defending champions failed to take part.

‌



Austria - 1938

View 5 Images Austria were unable to compete at the 1938 World Cup (Image: RDB/ullstein bild via Getty Images)

Among the favourites heading into the 1938 tournament, Austria were unable to compete after Nazi forces annexed the nation at the time. Several Austrian stars joined up with the German squad, though standout player Matthias Sindelar refused to represent the Nazi-led side.

India - 1950

On the sole occasion India reached the World Cup, they chose not to attend. In 1950, the Asian nation progressed to the finals by default following withdrawals during qualifying.

‌



Their absence was attributed to travel costs, training time and squad selection difficulties.

15 African teams - 1966

View 5 Images The 1966 World Cup was actually boycotted by 15 nations (Image: Rolls Press/Popperfoto via Getty Images)

The 1966 tournament holds fond memories for England, but one often-overlooked element is the absence of African nations. The continent's teams boycotted the qualifying stages in protest against FIFA's decision to grant just one place for the African, Asian and Oceania confederations combined.

‌



These nations include: Algeria, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Gabon, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Libya, Mali, Morocco, Nigeria, Senegal, Sudan, Tunisia and the United Arab Republic (now called Egypt).

Chile - 1974

In 1974, the world watched as a qualified nation came close to boycotting the World Cup on political grounds. During the intercontinental play-off between Chile and the Soviet Union, the latter refused to participate in the fixture in protest against Augusto Pinochet's dictatorship.

Pinochet had overthrown the socialist government, turning Chile from a former Soviet ally into an enemy. As a result, the Chilean players took to the pitch alone, with captain Francisco Valdes scoring into an empty net before the match was abandoned.

‌



World Cup protests and issues

View 5 Images There have been more recent protests (Image: ANP via Getty Images)

In more recent times, outright boycott threats have been few and far between, though tensions did surface during the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. All 32 qualified nations took part in the tournament, yet some players staged demonstrations concerning alleged human rights abuses and the host nation's controversial stance on LGBT rights.

Captains from seven European nations - England, Wales, the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Germany and Switzerland - had planned to wear "OneLove" armbands promoting inclusivity.

‌



View 5 Images Seven European nations planned a protest in 2022 (Image: Alain Pitton/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

They abandoned the plan just hours before their matches after FIFA threatened to issue automatic yellow cards to any player wearing the unauthorised armband.

Meanwhile, in March this year – ahead of the 2026 World Cup – following escalating regional conflict and U.S./Israeli airstrikes, Iranian sports minister Ahmad Donyamali publicly declared that the national team would not participate in the tournament "under any circumstances."

Article continues below

However, Iran did not officially withdraw and instead petitioned FIFA to have their matches relocated to co-host nation Mexico. This request was rejected and Iran ultimately played in the tournament, although they were subject to travel restrictions and were forced to travel in and out of the USA on the day of each match.

Sports.title: Man United slammed by Gary Neville over failure to land no-brainer Chelsea signing
Sports.content:
Man United slammed by Gary Neville over failure to land no-brainer Chelsea signing

Danny Welbeck looks set to join Chelsea from Brighton and Hove Albion, 12 years after leaving Man Utd

View 2 Images Gary Neville has given his thoughts on Danny Welbeck (Image: Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has told Manchester United that they made a mistake in selling Danny Welbeck. 12 years after leaving Old Trafford, the striker is closing in on a transfer to Chelsea.

‌



Welbeck made his first-team United debut in the 2008/09 campaign. Over the six years in the first team, he scored 29 goals and provided 16 assists. The now 35-year-old was sold to Arsenal for £16 million in 2014, and has since played for Watford and Brighton.

‌



The striker has been with the Seagulls for six years and has proven himself to be a dependable goalscorer in the Premier League. As Chelsea search for more experience, they have moved to add him to their squad.

‌



Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed as Michael Carrick set to axe four players READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford swap deal proposal could trigger £51m Man Utd transfer READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The rumours surrounding Welbeck's potential move to Stamford Bridge have sparked suggestions for United to launch a bid of their own. Neville has adopted a more reflective stance on the matter.

Speaking on Sky Sports, he said: "I said ten years ago that Manchester United should never have sold Danny Welbeck. He's gone away and done brilliantly well.

‌



"He's coming into a little cameo at the end of his career, but he's a fantastic player. I worked with him obviously as a team-mate, I worked with him with England as a coach and he was fantastic for England.

"And he's been good in the Premier League as well. It's a good move for Chelsea and it gives them a real option up front."

View 2 Images Danny Welbeck looks to be heading to Chelsea. (Image: George Wood, Getty Images)

‌



Alongside Welbeck, Chelsea also appear to be edging closer to landing former Liverpool midfielder Jordan Henderson, with Brentford having confirmed his departure on a free transfer.

Neville has outlined why both signings will prove beneficial to United's Premier League rivals. "They're still good players, they can contribute maybe 25 to 35 games a season at a good level," he said.

"But what they will do is all those young players there at Chelsea, they will make sure they turn up every single day, give their all, come back the same the next day and do it again.

‌



"That's been a problem. I don't think the young players at Chelsea have had any particular guidance or leadership around them either on the pitch or off the pitch.

"They've now got people around them who can do that and know how to get around the block."

While United wrapped up last season in the Champions League positions, Chelsea are embarking on a fresh rebuild under new boss Xabi Alonso, having failed to qualify for European football altogether in the previous campaign.

Sports.title: Who is Matthias Jaissle? Newcastle's next manager who was picked out by ex-Man Utd boss
Sports.content:
The Eddie Howe era at Newcastle has ended after five years, which involved so much success, but has ended on a low note.

Clearly a departure that has not come as a surprise to the St James' Park hierarchy, who have lined up Matthias Jaissle as his replacement. The 38-year-old is among the current generation of young European coaches, already thriving in their 30s.

Howe was once in that category and moving for Jaissle is thought to be aided by the fact his currently employers, Al Ahli, are owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) like Newcastle.

Already Jaissle's CV includes back to back Austrian Bundesliga titles and the Austrian Cup with Red Bull Salzburg. Those exploits earned him the move to the Middle East, where he's become a two-time Asian Champions League winner.

‌



Eddie Howe to leave Newcastle with immediate effect as replacement lined up READ MORE :

View 4 Images Eddie Howe's time at Newcastle has ended on a sour note (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

He is poised to inherit a team that, two years ago, was tracking in an upward trajectory at a fierce rate. Fast forward to 2026 and they've been gutted of some of their best players, more could yet leave, and Howe looks to have had enough with a 4-1 drubbing a Bristol City the final straw.

Jaissle has pretty much known only success during his time as a manager, but could be about to take charge of a team who are not among the most well equipped sides in their respective league for the first time. It will be a test, the like of which he's yet to come up against, but the 38-year-old has overcome more than enough adversity and hardship already.

Who is Matthias Jaissle?

During his playing days the German was part of a Hoffenheim side who embarked on a journey that took them from the eighth tier of German football to the summit of the Bundesliga. Like Howe though Jaissle was forced into early retirement due to injury, meaning he called time on his career in his mid-20s in 2014.

‌



View 4 Images Matthias Jaissle's move to the Premier League is set to be made easier by his Saudi Arabia connections

Ralf Rangnick, a man who doesn't have a sky high reputation in England, but is revered in Germany, immediately saw Jaissle as a future manager. He had been working as the sporting director for the Red Bull project in Salzburg and Leipzig and Jaissle was invited to join a trainee program in the youth department.

"Ralf already saw a coach in me, even when I didn't think about it at all," he previously told Kicker.

At Leipzig he helped coach the the U17 side and followed former Leipzig manager Alexander Zorniger to Danish side Brondby in 2016 after the pair struck up a friendship.

‌



Rangnick kept tabs from a far and in 2019 called on Jaissle to return to the Red Bull stable so that he could take over as a youth team coach at Salzburg.

View 4 Images The young manager had his playing career cut short by injury

Jaissle was unconventional in ways. He looked at New Zealand's rugby team for inspiration and, having disliked sitting through video sessions as a player, he didn't want to put his own teams through that. As with all young managers, he plays energetic, fast-paced football, but has shown those ideals actually bring him success, not just pretty football.

Julian Nagelsmann taking the Bayern Munich job in 2021 set about a chain of events that saw Jaissle become the Red Bull Salzburg manager and since then he's never really looked back.

‌



If there's one thing Red Bull's teams in Germany and Austria do well, its spot young talent. Erling Haaland, Dominik Szoboszlai, Josko Gvardiol, Nagelsmann and Marco Rose have all been signed or hired.

Salzburg sporting director, Christoph Freund, was convinced that they'd found another gem in Jaissle: "Matthias's qualities speak for themselves. I have known him for a few years already. He is young, ambitious and suits our club really well.

View 4 Images Matthias Jaissle first proved himself at Red Bull Salzburg, where his side were dominant

"The way he works and develops young players is exceptional. He was our ideal candidate as a result. He is not a big name yet, but we are all about giving young players and also young coaches a chance."

‌



Fans were sceptical initially but soon came round to the grand plan. Jaissle is not that much older than a lot of the players he manages, it makes him very relatable. He saw his main job as creating the right team spirit. His players enjoy working as a unit, which makes effective high pressing much easier to implement.

It would be easy to label a young manager with a blossoming reputation who moves to Saudi Arabia as a sell out. Going for the money. But leading Al Ahli has allowed him to manage the likes of Ivan Toney and former Chelsea goalkeeper Edouard Mendy. It means a move to Newcastle will not leave him overawed by some of the players in the dressing room.

In April this year Jaissle ensured Al Ahli became the first club in more than two decades to win back-to-back Asian Champions League Elite titles.

If that is the way he bows out, he can have done little more with the resources available to him, but now comes the biggest test of his managerial prowess.

‌

Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha provides Bradley Barcola transfer hint as Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha provides Bradley Barcola transfer hint as Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York

Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha was handed a positional switch last night as Andoni Iraola makes plans for the possible arrival of Bradley Barcola from PSG

View 2 Images Rio Ngumoha scored for Liverpool in pre-season

Rio Ngumoha handed Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola a timely reminder of his quality - all whilst leaving scope for him and Reds' target Bradley Barcola to thrive in the same team.

‌



Ngumoha was a bright spark for the Merseysiders last season, in what was largely a forgettable campaign. He continued to excel during his limited opportunities and came off the bench to score the winner as Liverpool saw off Wrexham in pre-season.

‌



The 17-year-old's deflected goal in New York kept up the team's perfect record so far and his deployment off the right, having played almost exclusively off the left previously, serves to highlight what could come next for Iraola.

‌



There have been clamours for Ngumoha to play more regularly, but he and Barcola, another left-sided forward, could've been in a scenario whereby they were battling for the same spot.

Jamie Carragher highlights major Bradley Barcola concern as Liverpool make move for star READ MORE :

Liverpool are ready to ramp up their interest in the PSG man, whose exit from the European Champions is looking all the more likely, and Ngumoha's impressive cameo off the right shows that he and the Frenchman could play in tandem either side of a striker, whoever that may be.

Iraola, should he get a deal for Barcola over the line, could spend up to £140million, which is what the Parisians are demanding. He'd need a return on that investment, which could've left Ngumoha's route towards more minutes blocked off, but playing off the right is now a viable option.

‌



The teenager said on his new boss: “The manager has been very good, getting his points across really well. He’s been top and all the coaching staff have been very good as well.”

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is being linked with a blockbuster move to Anfield (Image: Dan Mullan - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Iraola's style earned him huge plaudits at Bournemouth but the Spaniard insists his Reds side still have a way to go before they've locked in his principles.

‌



"I think we’re still not there," he said. "We are sometimes arriving late, but I think it’s a step forward, since especially the first half against Sunderland. That is more of a reference than the second half.

"Slowly, slowly I hope every game we are closer and closer. We start to add new bodies, because now we are playing with a lot of the young players. Slowly, slowly we have to add the senior players that are starting to train with us, so we can arrive to the beginning of the season in a good place."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
