World.title: Promoted Orlando Pirates winger chooses Mofokeng’s jersey number
World.content:
Mpho Padime winger has officially bearned promotion to the Buccaneers’ senior squad ahead of the 2026/27 Betway Premiership season after an outstanding campaign in the DStv Diski Challenge.

MPHO PADIME EARNS ORLANDO PIRATES PROMOTION

Born in June 2007 in Katlehong, Johannesburg, Padime first made his name in township football while playing for Khathorus Juventus FC. His dazzling dribbling, blistering pace and entertaining “Kasi Flava” style quickly attracted interest from several clubs.

Although Kaizer Chiefs offered him a development contract, the teenage star chose to join Orlando Pirates in September 2025.



His decision has already paid off. Playing under Roscoe Krieling in the DStv Diski Challenge, Padime scored 10 goals and provided nine assists during the 2025/26 season. His 19 goal contributions helped the Buccaneers win the reserve league title with a record-breaking 75 points.

The winger also travelled with the first team on their pre-season tour of Spain. He featured against Córdoba CF and UD Las Palmas, where he continued to impress the technical team.

ORLANDO PIRATES HAND PADIME ICONIC NUMBER

With Mofokeng completing his move to Europe earlier this month, Orlando Pirates have handed the number 38 jersey to one of the club’s brightest young prospects.



The shirt became synonymous with Mofokeng, who developed into one of South Africa’s biggest stars before securing his overseas move. Padime will now hope to build his own legacy in the same number.

The jersey change also reflects the club’s growing faith in academy talent. Padime is among several DStv Diski Challenge graduates promoted to the senior squad as Abdeslam Ouaddou prepares for his first season in charge of the reigning Betway Premiership champions.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs willing to sacrifice centre-back to land top striker!
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are willing to sacrifice centre-back Given Msimango in order to land Langelihle Phili from Stellenbosch FC.

Amakhosi have been doing all they could to sign Phili but it appears Stellies are not eager to let their top striker go for peanuts.

The Glamour Boys had already offered Ashley du Preez plus cash in an attempt to sweeten the deal.



However, Stellies stuck to their guns and demanded more from the Soweto giants, and for that reason, Chiefs have now included Msimango in the deal.

Msimango, with just 13 league appearances last season, has battled to own that centre-back position since his arrival from TS Galaxy.

The arrival of Thabo Moloisane on a free transfer from Stellies will certainly not make things easy for Msimango.

Should this deal go through, Msimango will join a growing list of players deemed surplus to requirements by Chiefs, including Thabo Cele.

KAIZER CHIEFS OFFER MSIMANGO AND DU PREEZ PLUS CASH FOR PHILI

“SABC Sport has established that defender Given Msimango is one of two players Kaizer Chiefs have offered, together with a cash payment, to Stellenbosch FC in an effort to secure the signing of highly rated winger Langelihle Phili,” reads part of a report by SABC Sport.

WHY AMAKHOSI NEED PHILI…

At 21, Phili has proven himself to be a reliable striker, and Chiefs are looking for a long-term solution to their goalscoring problems.



Nonetheless, Phili understands that he will not just walk into the starting line-up as there is stiff competition upfront.

As things stand, Fernando da Cruz has Flavio da Silva and Etoisa Ighodaro as his target men, meaning Phili will have to fight for his position.

Phili has 11 goals and two assists in 72 topflight matches, meaning he will have to up his game given the expectations at Chiefs.

World.title: Stokes should return for 'one more Ashes': Australia coach McDonald
World.content:
MELBOURNE - Australia coach Andrew McDonald says Ben Stokes has "a lot of good cricket left in him" and believes England's new Test coach should lure him of international retirement for the Ashes.

The all-rounder called it quits in extraordinary fashion during the third Test against New Zealand at Trent Bridge in late June, making his exit public on the fourth afternoon.

The bombshell announcement came after he returned to duty following the fall-out from a London nightclub incident also involving teammate Gus Atkinson earlier that month.

Brendon McCullum was sacked soon after as England's red-ball coach, with British media reporting this week that another New Zealander, Stephen Fleming, is poised to take over.

McDonald, whose side travel to England for the latest instalment of the Ashes next year, said Stokes still had plenty to offer and his return would be an ideal storyline for the series.

"The fairytale would be that he comes back out of retirement and takes on one more Ashes and builds a lot of hype on the way in," McDonald told Australian radio station SEN late Wednesday.

"If you're looking at promoting that series, that's probably the angle that you would want, that he comes out of retirement.

"To me, he's still got a lot of good cricket left in him," he added.

"It'll be a fascinating watch. I think that whoever the new head coach that comes in potentially has a conversation with him."

Stokes, who is still playing at domestic level for Durham, is only 35.

By comparison, Australia could field as many five players in their Test against Bangladesh next month who are older -- Nathan Lyon (38), Steve Smith and Scott Boland (both 37), Mitchell Starc (36) and Josh Hazlewood (35).

"We don't know why Ben left. I don't think there's been anything on the record around the definitive reason as to why," added McDonald.

"He may have just called it a day on Test cricket, and that's it, so there might be a full stop there.

"Or there might be an opportunity for that new head coach to potentially twist his arm and bring him back in."

World.title: Australian regulator says Telegram breached online safety law
World.content:
MELBOURNE - Australia's cyber safety watchdog took court action against Telegram, alleging the global messaging platform had failed to remove terrorism material.

Under Australia's online safety law, Telegram faces a maximum penalty of up to AU$54.6 million ($38 million).

The development comes a day after Russia announced it was seeking the arrest of Telegram's founder and CEO Pavel Durov, alleging his "complicity in terrorism".

Durov, who holds French and UAE passports, was accused of allowing the platform to be used for recruitment by Ukraine's security services.

Australia's eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant said Thursday the watchdog would allege Telegram had failed to remove pro-terror material including videos of terrorist executions and mass shootings, including "some of the most notorious acts of known extremist violence in recent history" despite being put on notice.

This included content linked to the live-streamed 2019 Christchurch Mosque shooting and a 2022 Buffalo mass shooting in New York, she said.

"When platforms are alerted to terrorist content, they must act," she told a press conference in Sydney.

"This action comes at a time when Australia is experiencing a heightened security environment against the fresh backdrop of the Bondi tragedy," she said, a reference to an antisemitic mass shooting at a Sydney beach that killed 15 people last year.

Telegram, registered in the United Arab Emirates, is a major global platform visited by Australians 1.5 million times a month, the regulator said.

Durov has lived in both Dubai and France.

In 2024, he was arrested by French police on charges related to the distribution of illegal content, but was later released on bail.

He left France after authorities there lifted a travel ban.

World.title: US actor Jared Leto denies latest accusations of sexual assault
World.content:
LONDON - US actor and singer Jared Leto on Wednesday denied allegations of sexual assault and harassment levelled against him by ten women in a new documentary aired by the BBC.

The women said they were victimised by Leto between 2002 and 2016.

Two of them accused him of sexual assault when they were 17 years old, while another said the actor threatened her with sexual assault when she was 19.

A fourth woman recounted receiving multiple sexually explicit phone calls from the actor when she was 16, who allegedly propositioned her for sex.

Four other women described sexual harassment during phone calls from the lead singer of the rock band Thirty Seconds to Mars.

"I have never sexually assaulted anyone in my entire life," the 54-year-old actor said in a statement. "These claims are absolutely and categorically false."

Nine of the ten women are speaking out for the first time in the BBC documentary titled "Jared Leto: Hollywood’s Dark Secret."

The actor, who won a Best Supporting Actor Oscar in 2014 for "Dallas Buyers Club," has faced such accusations before.

In 2025, several other women accused him of sexual assault in an investigation conducted by Air Mail, a US digital magazine. At the time, Leto also denied any inappropriate conduct.

World.title: Danube drops to 'historic lows' as fresh heatwave hits
World.content:
BUDAPEST - Plummeting river levels have already brought shipping to a standstill in parts of Serbia, squeezing fuel imports and energy production -- and now heatwave warnings have been issued in the Balkans.

Serbian forecasters said a long-term heatwave had begun, with temperatures expected to reach around 40C in some places on Friday, and the intense heat could last for close to a fortnight.

Similar warnings were also issued across the region, and the authorities braced for an increase in wildfires as rising temperatures coupled with drought conditions.

The warning comes as successive heatwaves hit Europe, driving deadly wildfires amid a major drought -- conditions scientists say have been worsened by human-induced climate change.

Along the Serbian stretch of the Danube, a lack of rainfall has left vessels stranded and exposed sandbanks, with some parts now shallow enough to cross on foot.

World.title: 'Flip-flop knee-jerk': Madlanga hears Andrea Johnson not stickler for rules
World.content:
PRETORIA - Former Investigating Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) Andrea Johnson was not a stickler for the rules.

State Advocate Drushantha Ramsamy alleges that Johnson frequently departed from established "IDAC Bible" procedures.

Ramsamy told the Madlanga Commission on Thursday that the deviations were often accompanied by intimidation.

"Advocate Johnson would deviate, constantly," Ramsamy told the commission.

LIVESTREAM | Madlanga Commission continues focus on IDAC

"It was a situation where we had this, but she would also have her own way of doing things with different groups, different investigations, different structures.

"There was a constant deviation from what was in black and whites. And it was always from her office that the deviation was done. And when the deviation was done, it always came with intimidation," she added.

Asked by Madlanga to explain intimidation in this context, Ramsamy said: "The nickname for Advocate Johnson in the office is 'flip-flop-knee-jerk'. You would get instructions in the morning and then during the course of the day there would be a conversation between her and Dylan Perumal, and the flip flop would happen."

World.title: Bride advert seeking young girls sparks child protection concerns
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A newspaper  by a 58-year-old Free State man seeking a bride aged between 16 and 25 has sparked widespread backlash, with child protection advocates warning that it could expose vulnerable young women and girls to exploitation.

The man, whose name is known to eNCA, describes himself in the  as a wealthy farmer seeking what he calls “a pure, marriageable lady” with “biblical values”.

The advert, published in Die Burger on 24 July 2026, promises a R100,000 bride price for the woman’s parents and a R5 million inheritance for the successful applicant.

The inclusion of 16- and 17-year-olds has drawn particular concern.

While the age of consent in South Africa is 16, anyone under the age of 18 is legally regarded as a child, and child-protection organisations say the advert raises serious safeguarding concerns.

Shaheda Omar, director of the Teddy Bear Foundation, said the advert could place vulnerable young people at risk, regardless of whether it was intended as a genuine proposal, satire or a publicity stunt.

"Whether it's genuine, a publicity stunt or intended satire, the potential consequences are serious because vulnerable individuals may perceive it as a legitimate opportunity," she said.

"The promise of a R100,000 bride price and a R5-million estate provision could be particularly appealing to young women and girls experiencing poverty, unemployment or family hardship."

Omar said financial desperation can impair judgement, making people more susceptible to exploitation and coercion.

She also criticised the inclusion of 16-year-olds, saying the advert shared characteristics commonly associated with grooming.

"The inclusion of 16-year-olds in such an advert is deeply concerning because it targets an age group that requires protection rather than recruitment into intimate relationships with unknown adults."

The advert states that the prospective bride should be a non-smoker with “deep core beliefs”, and that the husband would be the head of the household in accordance with what it describes as “original Biblical principles”.

World.title: L'vovo fundraiser highlights entertainment industry's failure, says Devnarain
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The entertainment industry needs to acknowledge its own failure, says Jack Devnarain.

“We have failed to provide social security for our creatives,” he says.

His comments come after members of the public took to social media to raise funds for musician Thokozani Ndlovu, better known as L’vovo.

Ndlovu suffered a near-fatal stroke in December 2022, forcing him to step away from the spotlight to focus on his recovery.

He had been performing at a show in Ndwedwe when he suffered the stroke, which left the left side of his body weakened and affected his speech.

Last week, Ndlovu gave an emotional interview to Gagasi FM, prompting social media user Yenziwe Qiniso Ndimande to launch a fundraising campaign.

She wrote on Facebook: “Please note that L’vovo did not ask for donations. Many people were touched by his interview, and from there, we decided to come together and support him.”

Within hours, more than R100,000 had been raised. By the end of the week, that amount had doubled.

Devnarain said the news of Ndlovu’s health struggles had been unsettling.

“He is one of those iconic performers. He is recognised and celebrated,” he said.

“To hear that he’s going through this difficult time is where the industry itself needs to acknowledge its own failure.”

Devnarain said the industry has failed to establish structures to regulate the entertainment sector.

He said these structures would ensure that creatives’ earnings and workers’ rights are protected by law.

“We have petitioned the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture, which has failed to introduce the necessary safeguards,” he said.

World.title: FIFA proposal 'an opportunity but not an obligation', says Infantino
World.content:
PARIS - FIFA president Gianni Infantino said that the proposed launch of a private subsidiary to exploit the commercial benefits of the World Cup was "an opportunity but not an obligation".

A proposal to sell stakes in FIFA's major competitions sparked disbelief and outrage globally since it was revealed Tuesday, but Infantino defended the idea, saying too little of football's commercial value reached the parts of the game that need it most.

"FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer. It's part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation," Infantino said in a video released Wednesday evening.

"It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

Infantino insisted the proposal was centred on unlocking "previously uncaptured commercial value" and was conditional on a democratic vote of FIFA's 211 member associations and approval by the FIFA council.

"Capturing that value requires additional expertise, additional insight, distinct from governing and developing the sport," he said.

"It would simply commercialise and organise all FIFA-owned competitions along with sponsorship, broadcast, licensing and new ventures for the benefit of FIFA's 211 member associations."

Infantino said the game would not change and the fans would be happier.

"Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries," he said.

World.title: 'It follows you to your grave': Ndung'u accuses Ruto of overrunning state institutions
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Treasury Cabinet Secretary Njuguna Ndung'u. [File,Standard]

Former Treasury Cabinet Secretary Njuguna Ndung'u has accused President William Ruto of overrunning state institutions, saying fear of lifelong repercussions forces officials to conform.

Speaking during a meeting in Nairobi, Ndung'u said independent institutions exist but are weakened when leaders seek to dominate them.

"Right now, the current president overruns all the institutions. And that is why everybody in those institutions will have to conform for fear," Ndung'u noted.

Ndung'u said he refused to engage in improper deals during his tenure at the National Treasury despite pressure, warning that the consequences of compromising public office can last a lifetime.

"I refuse to do deals in the Ministry of Finance. I can't do deals. I know, it follows you to your grave," he observes.

He argued that the consequences of institutional compromise outlast the political regimes in which they occur.

"It doesn't go away with the regime, by the way. There are people who are my friends; they were caught up in some of those things, including in the central bank. And even by the time they died, they were still being followed by those things," he recalled.

Ndung'u added that some of the cases involving his associates were never concluded because of the severity of the consequences they carried.

He served as Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) from March 2007 to March 2015 before President Ruto appointed him Treasury Cabinet Secretary in September 2022.

Ruto dropped him from the Cabinet in July 2024 during a broader reshuffle.

World.title: Lawyer seeks orders to suspend court boycott
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Advocate Adrian Kamotho argues that LSK's actions create the impression that court orders can be overturned through a boycott. [File, Standard]

A city lawyer has moved to the High Court seeking conservatory orders to suspend the Law Society of Kenya's (LSK) ongoing targeted boycott of judges and judicial officers.

In a petition filed under a certificate of urgency, Advocate Adrian Kamotho has sued LSK led by President Charles Kanjama, over its nationwide and targeted court boycott of Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Philomena Mwilu and other judges, arguing that the action is unconstitutional, undermines judicial independence and denies litigants access to justice.

"The LSK's actions create the impression that lawful court orders can be overturned through a boycott, setting a dangerous precedent to the rule of law and thereby undermining the proper administration of justice," Kamotho states in the petition.

The lawyer has named the Judicial Service Commission (JSC), Chief Justice Martha Koome, Deputy Chief Justice Mwilu, several Supreme Court, High Court and Environment and Land Court judges, Court of Appeal Judge Sankale Ole Kantai, Kibera Chief Magistrate Stella Atambo and the Kenya Magistrates and Judges Association as interested parties in the case.

He is seeking orders to immediately suspend the implementation of the LSK's targeted boycott announced through statements and operational guidelines issued on July 17, July 20 and July 22, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the petition.

"Pending the hearing and determination of this Petition, the court be pleased to issue a conservatory order restraining the LSK, whether by itself, its Council, officers, agents or any person acting under its authority, from implementing, enforcing or giving effect to the targeted boycott," Kamotho seeks.

According to the petition, the targeted boycott, which commenced on July 23, directs advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before judges listed by the LSK.

East Africa Law Society president Ramadhan Abubakar Mukira addresses the media on the court boycott outside the Supreme Court of Kenya in Nairobi on July 22, 2026. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Lawyers are also required to seek adjournments, transfers or recusals of matters regardless of their clients' instructions.

"The Respondent has directed advocates not to participate in fresh hearings, part-heard matters or new applications before the listed judges and judicial officers," Kamotho states.

He adds: "Advocates appearing before the targeted judges and judicial officers have been directed to seek the transfer, recusal or adjournment of pending proceedings, irrespective of their clients' instructions, the circumstances of the individual case or the applicable legal principles."

Kamotho further claims the society has threatened disciplinary action against judges, judicial officers and advocates who decline to implement the boycott.

"The LSK has further directed that any judge, judicial officer or advocate who declines to facilitate the boycott be reported to it for 'appropriate action,' including possible complaints before the Judicial Service Commission and such further action as its Council may deem necessary," he says.

According to the petition, every day the boycott remains in force exposes court users to delayed justice and unnecessary hardship.

"Every day that the targeted boycott remains operative exposes litigants and court users to adjournments, disruption of part-heard proceedings, expiry of interim protection measures, prolonged detention, additional expense and denial or delay of access to justice," Kamotho argues.

He also faults the LSK for allegedly including the late Supreme Court Judge Mohammed Ibrahim in its list of judges affected by the boycott.

"The targeted list of judges includes Hon. Justice Mohammed Ibrahim (deceased), demonstrating unconscionable casualness on the part of the LSK and apparent failure to verify elementary material facts before imposing measures of such gravity," the petition states.

Kamotho contends that the boycott creates an unlawful mechanism for exerting pressure on judges outside the constitutional framework.

He argues that the dispute raises fundamental constitutional questions, including whether the LSK has the legal authority to organise an indefinite boycott, compel advocates to withhold legal services from clients and determine which judicial functions judges may perform.

He maintains that the boycott threatens litigants' constitutional rights to equality before the law, access to justice, legal representation and a fair hearing, particularly in urgent and criminal matters.

In his supporting affidavit, Kamotho says advocates have been placed in an impossible position by the LSK's directives.

"The directions therefore place advocates in an immediate and irreconcilable conflict between their lawful professional duties and the Respondent's threatened enforcement measures," he says.

He further says litigants are innocent parties caught in an institutional dispute.

"The practical burden of the boycott consequently falls upon litigants and court users who are strangers to the institutional dispute forming the alleged basis of the boycott," he states.

Kamotho insists the conservatory orders sought are intended only to preserve uninterrupted court operations and judicial independence pending determination of the constitutional petition, arguing that the public interest favours continued access to courts and legal representation rather than disruption of judicial proceedings.

The petition is pending directions and hearing.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: FM, US Envoy discuss regional de-escalation efforts
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty held a telephone conversation on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, with US Special Envoy for the Middle Eas Steve Witkoff to discuss regional developments and efforts to reduce tensions.

The two officials exchanged assessments of the latest developments and stressed the importance of preventing further escalation and avoiding a broader regional conflict that could threaten security and stability and increase the humanitarian and economic impact of the ongoing crisis.

Abdelatty stressed the need to uphold the principles of good neighborliness, respect international law and preserve the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of all states.

He also called for intensifying diplomatic efforts and pursuing political solutions to restore stability and reduce regional tensions.

The minister condemned all attacks targeting the Gulf states and Jordan, reaffirming Egypt’s firm rejection of any actions that undermine the sovereignty, security or stability of Arab countries.

World.title: President al-Sisi, Tebboune stress regional de-escalation, reaffirm solidarity after Algeria wildfires
World.content:
President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi held a phone call on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, with his Algerian counterpart Abdelmadjid Tebboune, expressing Egypt’s full solidarity with Algeria in the wake of devastating wildfires and reaffirming the two countries’ commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation and regional coordination.

Presidential Spokesperson Mohamed al-Shennawy said President al-Sisi extended his condolences over the victims of the fires and wished a speedy recovery to those injured, stressing Egypt’s readiness to provide any support needed to help Algeria deal with the emergency.

The Egyptian president also underscored the deep historical ties between the two countries and welcomed the growing momentum in bilateral cooperation, calling for continued implementation of the understandings and agreements reached by both sides, particularly the outcomes of the Egyptian-Algerian High Joint Committee held in Cairo in November 2025

.For his part, Tebboune thanked Sisi for Egypt’s expression of solidarity, saying such support reflected the longstanding bonds between the two nations and their peoples.

He also briefed the Egyptian president on the intensive efforts being undertaken by the Algerian authorities to contain the wildfires and protect citizens and property.

The Algerian leader praised the steady progress in Egyptian-Algerian relations and highlighted the significant opportunities for expanding cooperation across various sectors by leveraging the two countries’ capabilities and human resources.

The two leaders also discussed a number of regional issues of mutual concern, reaffirming their support for peaceful efforts to resolve the Iranian crisis while rejecting any infringement on the security and sovereignty of Arab states.

They further agreed on the need to intensify regional and international efforts to prevent a return to full-scale escalation and to enhance Egyptian-Algerian coordination and consultations on regional developments amid current challenges.MENA

World.title: Indonesia eyes increasing trade volume with Egypt
World.content:
Indonesian Ambassador to Cairo Kuntjoro Giri Waseso affirmed his country’s aspiration to increase trade volume with Egypt, which currently exceeds $1 billion annually, given the historical relations between both nations.

This came during the ambassador’s meeting on Wednesday, July 29, 2026, with board members of the Aswan Chamber of Commerce, chaired by Hossam Al-Ansari, in the presence of Suhair Al-Masry, Head of the Businesswomen Economic Council at the chamber, along with Indonesian embassy officials.

The ambassador pointed out that Indonesia occupies an advanced position among investing countries in the Egyptian market through various projects, expressing happiness over visiting Aswan to solidify joint work and investment.

For her part, Suhair Al-Masry highlighted the ambassador’s eagerness to meet chamber members to enhance cooperation, urging utilization of joint opportunities with Indonesia, a major global exporter of modern technology.She explained that chamber officials presented the governorate’s immense natural resources, particularly in mining, quarry materials, and the marble industry.

Al-Masry noted she reviewed the pivotal role of the Businesswomen Economic Council in supporting working women across agricultural and industrial sectors. She added that a proposal was made to organize a joint meeting between exporters, importers, and manufacturers from both countries.

The Indonesian embassy’s commercial attaché promised to organize this meeting soon to establish a shared market via Aswan, alongside agreeing to provide the chamber with a database of Indonesian traders and market needs.

Meanwhile, Chairman Hossam Al-Ansari welcomed the ambassador’s visit to discuss cooperation in industry, mining, and foodstuff sectors.

Al-Ansari stated that the chamber presented a list of Aswan’s mining resources and solar energy fields, seeking Indonesian expertise to support manufacturing solar power station components, which are currently imported.

He added that Egypt’s vision to expand into Africa and Sudan via its southern gateway was presented, positioning Aswan as a hub for Indonesian exports to Sudan and the continent.

He revealed that an invitation was extended to the Indonesian side to invest in the logistics zone being implemented in Karkar, south of Aswan, leveraging Egypt’s logistics support and investment facilities.

Al-Ansari concluded that the ambassador invited the chamber and local investors to participate via Zoom in an upcoming investment exhibition organized by Indonesia to showcase trade and partnership opportunities.

World.title: Egypt, Pakistan discuss efforts to reduce regional tensions
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty received a phone call from Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar to discuss regional developments and efforts to restore security and stability.

The two ministers exchanged views on the rapidly changing situation in the region, stressing the need to reduce tensions, halt military operations and pursue political and diplomatic solutions to regional crises.

They also agreed to maintain close coordination and consultations in support of diplomatic efforts aimed at restoring stability and preventing further escalation.The conversation also addressed the Palestinian issue.

Abdelatty expressed deep concern over the deteriorating situation in the occupied Palestinian territories and condemned continued Israeli actions in the West Bank, Gaza and occupied East Jerusalem, warning that they undermine prospects for peace and the two-state solution.

Additionally, Abdelatty stressed the importance of implementing all phases of the US peace plan for Gaza to help sustain the ceasefire, ensure the full delivery of humanitarian aid and create the conditions needed to move forward with the next stages of the process.

World.title: Unidentified object lands deep inside Poland causing explosion as Russia launches deadly, Ukraine-wide attack
World.content:
Poland had earlier reported scrambling fighter jets in response to Russia’s attack on Ukraine, which hit large swathes of the country and killed at least eight people, including children, and left several people trapped under rubble.

The object crashed in an undeveloped area near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia in Lublin province, Poland’s army said. Polish police said residents reported hearing a powerful blast.

“During the Russian massive missile attack on western Ukraine, a violation of Polish airspace occurred,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said in a post to X. A government spokesperson said Tusk was on his way to the crash site.

Separately, Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said a Russian cruise missile had “crossed into Poland as part of Russia’s massive strike against Ukraine” in a post to X. It was not clear if Sybiha was referring to the unidentified object which crashed in Lublin.

Russia’s Ministry of Defense said it carried out a “massive strike using long-range precision weapons from land, air, and sea” as well as attack drones on military sites across Ukraine, in a statement posted to Telegram Thursday.

Poland’s army said the country’s air defenses observed at least a dozen missiles over western Ukraine, which posed a potential threat to Polish airspace.

It is not yet clear if the unidentified object that crashed in Poland was a Russian missile. But any potential Russian attack so deep into a NATO member’s territory would risk being perceived as an escalation in Moscow’s yearslong war on Ukraine.

CNN has reached out to NATO for comment.

Russia’s overnight assault on Ukraine follows a visit by President Volodymyr Zelensky to the White House Tuesday, where he asked President Donald Trump to provide Ukraine with additional air defense systems.

Smoke over the Kyiv skyline during Russian strikes on Thursday, July 30 Sergei Supinsky/AFP/Getty Images

The attack damaged or destroyed dozens of homes, businesses and infrastructure facilities, Zelensky said on Telegram Thursday, and used more than 70 missiles and over 280 attack drones.

Ukraine intercepted more than 260 drones, according to Zelensky, in what he said was a commendable feat given a “critical shortage of air defense missiles from our partners.”

On his way home on Wednesday, Zelensky stopped in the Polish city of Lublin – not far from the site of the next day’s crash – to meet with Tusk. The two leaders discussed “the outcomes of (Zelensky’s) visit to the United States and the security of Poland, Ukraine, and all of Europe,” according to a post to X by Tusk.

Poland has routinely scrambled jets in response to Russian attacks on western Ukraine, though they have rarely entered its territory. NATO fighter jets shot down multiple Russian drones that violated Polish airspace last September, denouncing Moscow for “absolutely dangerous behavior.”

In November 2022, two people were killed after a Ukrainian air defense missile unintentionally landed in the Polish village of Przewodow, about four miles (6.4 kilometers) west of the border.

Deadly month for Ukraine

The attacks – which come as Ukraine has seen its heaviest number of civilian casualties in one month since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022 – killed at least one person in the capital Kyiv, and another person in Poltava region, central Ukraine, according to local authorities.

Videos posted on social media showed families sheltering in crowded Kyiv metro stations, some bedding down on the floor beneath blankets or inside small tents.

People take shelter inside a metro station during a Russian missile and drone strike in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Thursday, July 30. Alina Smutko/Reuters

In the village of Radushne, near the southern Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih, parents and three children were killed after a ballistic missile blew a family home “into smithereens,” Zelensky said. Two more children were pulled alive from the rubble, he added.

Two girls, aged 5 and 12, were among the three children killed, Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the city’s military administration, said on Telegram, calling it a “dark night.”

Graphic video from Radushne showed bodies strewn amid the rubble of a shattered building, with fires still burning.

Two unseen women could be heard speaking. “We’ve pulled one child out. There are still some lying over there,” one said.

“There are children here. There are many children,” the other said.

Rescue workers were also trying to save people trapped under rubble after an attack on a residential building in Lviv, Zelensky said. Dozens across the country were wounded.

Russian warehouse on fire

Also on Thursday, a warehouse for the Russian retailer Wildberries caught fire in the western city of Penza after a Ukrainian drone attack, regional governor Oleg Melnichenko said on Telegram. One person was wounded and about 200 people were evacuated from the site, Melnichenko said.

Ukraine has repeatedly targeted Wildberries distribution centers, Russia’s Amazon equivalent, bringing Moscow’s war even closer to home by disrupting the lives and livelihoods of ordinary Russians.

Kyiv has claimed the Wildberries facilities are legitimate military targets because they supply Russia’s frontline troops in Ukraine, which Moscow denies.

This story has been updated with additional developments.

World.title: Death toll rises in Japan. Why does the country experience so many large earthquakes?
World.content:
Almost no other country in the world is rocked by such frequent and damaging earthquakes as Japan – an island nation that sits on the boundary of four tectonic plates, the constantly-shifting slabs of the Earth’s crust.

It also lies on the “Ring of Fire,” a 25,000-mile arc that stretches around the Pacific, where the world’s most active volcanoes are located – and the most earthquakes take place.

The impact of these quakes was on full display this week after a deadly 6.8-magnitude earthquake hit Japan’s southern Kumamoto prefecture, prompting thousands of emergency responders to mobilize in search, rescue and relief efforts.

Speaking Thursday, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said 30 people had died. Earlier, Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said some deaths were being investigated to confirm their link to the disaster.

Japan is well-prepared for disasters like these, having invested billions of dollars into cutting-edge quake detection technology, response and evacuation systems, and quake-proof infrastructure.

For residents, quakes are a regular part of life – children start practicing earthquake and evacuation drills from kindergarten. But the threat looms large in the public imagination, especially with the government regularly warning that Japan could eventually see a once-in-a-century “megathrust earthquake.”

The latest quake

Tuesday’s earthquake hit around 4:30pm local time in Uki, a city with a population of 56,000 people, south of the Kumamoto prefecture.

A wave of aftershocks has struck since, with the strongest measured at 5.4-magnitude further south, according to USGS, as authorities warn that similarly strong tremors could shake the region in coming days.

Rescuers are still working to locate people trapped beneath the rubble – the quake brought down buildings and a shopping mall in Kumamoto was partially destroyed after a suspected gas leak and explosion.

Five died in Aeon Mall Kumamoto, while several others were killed when a chimney collapsed at a paper factory in Yatsushiro.

High temperatures are making the rescue efforts increasingly difficult. Authorities have warned residents about the dangers of heatstroke and are reminding people to stay hydrated. Temperatures are expected to pass 35 degrees Celsius (95 degrees Fahrenheit) from Thursday.

The Kumamoto region had just recovered from a larger quake that hit in 2016, causing widespread damage and killing more than 270 people.

“Why? Why does this keep happening around us here in Kumamoto?” local resident Shoji Yonemitsu told CNN.

“The shaking back then was on a whole different level. But yesterday’s quake was still pretty terrifying,” he said.

Long history of disasters

Japan’s history is littered with devastating quakes.

Throughout its classical and feudal eras, quakes regularly swept through cities and towns, wiping out structures made of wood and paper that were acutely vulnerable to fires breaking out in the aftermath. One particularly damaging quake in 1498 is thought to have killed more than 30,000 people, though estimates differ.

The Great Kanto earthquake of 1923 was another devastating moment, laying waste to swathes of the capital Tokyo and killing some 140,000 people.

Japan began introducing stronger building codes in the 1980s – which demonstrated their effectiveness in the 1995 Kobe earthquake, which killed more than 6,000 people. Nearly all of the collapsed buildings were built prior to the new codes, kickstarting a major drive to improve the country’s quake resilience, emergency response systems, and retrofitting older buildings with new standards.

A Kobe resident passes by a central office building on January 18, 1995 that was damaged in an earthquake the previous day. Toru Yamanaka/AFP/Getty Images

As one of the world’s wealthiest nations, Japan was in a strong position to embrace technology and spending to fortify itself against the threat of tectonic catastrophes.

But technology can only go so far.

The 2011 Tohoku disaster is the worst in living memory – a magnitude-9.1 earthquake and tsunami that triggered the Fukushima nuclear meltdown and killed nearly 20,000 people. Thousands more were never found. It remains one of the strongest quakes of this century.

Smaller quakes can still routinely bring death; a magnitude-7.1 earthquake killed more than 700 in Noto in 2024, western Japan.

Other countries such as Chile, Indonesia, the Solomon Islands, and the west coast of the United States all lie on the “Ring of Fire” on either side of the Pacific Ocean. It’s where the Pacific Plate – the oceanic plate that lies beneath the water – meets surrounding continental tectonic plates. When these plates move against each other and produce friction, energy builds up and is released through earthquakes.

“About 10% of the world’s earthquakes of magnitude 6 or higher occur in or around Japan, so the risk is much higher than in places like Europe or the eastern United States, where earthquakes are rare,” Shoichi Yoshioka, a professor at Japan’s Kobe University, told CNN in 2024.

“Each time, we witness the tragic loss of lives, buildings being crushed, and tsunamis causing devastation, leaving a lasting impression of fear,” he added. “This fear is likely shared by many citizens. I think this contributes significantly to why Japan is so prepared.”

Is it safe to travel to Japan?

Even among other quake-prone countries, Japan is famed for being a world leader in earthquake preparedness and resiliency.

Buildings are required to have anti-seismic technology, such as walls and floors that can absorb vibrations and shaking, or flexible structures that allow buildings to move during quakes but not collapse. “Most buildings are fairly resistant to earthquakes,” advises one government site for tourists.

But travelers have still been spooked by the threat.

Last summer, a spate of earthquake-related “predictions” caused superstitious travelers across East Asia to cancel or delay their holidays to Japan. These included a Japanese comic book that warned of a “real catastrophe,” a psychic who predicted mass destruction, and a feng shui master who urged people to stay away.

Japan’s government itself has fed these fears – warning for many years that the country could soon see the Nankai Trough megathrust earthquake, the most powerful of its kind.

The Nankai Trough is a 700-kilometer long (435-mile) subduction zone, which refers to when tectonic plates slip beneath each other. Severe earthquakes in this area have been recorded every 100 to 200 years, according to the government’s Earthquake Research Committee.

By calculating the intervals between each major quake, the government has warned there is a 70% to 80% chance that Japan will be rocked by another Nankai Trough earthquake within 30 years, expected to be between magnitude 8 and 9.

But the science is disputed. Some have pushed back against these forecasts, arguing that earthquakes don’t happen in predictable cycles; even those who give credence to the prediction say it’s not necessarily useful to make such long-term, imprecise predictions.

The best thing Japan can do now, several experts told CNN, is to get ready – plugging gaps in parts of the country that are less well-prepared, and raising public awareness on emergency response.

World.title: Saudi defense minister meets with Vance and Trump following joint US-Saudi strikes
World.content:
Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman met with Vice President JD Vance in Washington, DC, on Wednesday, as the US-Iran war threatened to embroil the kingdom.

According to sources familiar with the matter, Prince Khalid was originally scheduled to travel to the United States last week, but his trip was postponed. His visit to Washington was brief, and he left after his meeting with Vance, according to the sources.

His visit came less than a day after the US and Saudi Arabia conducted joint military operations against Iran-linked “logistics and weapons sites” in Iraq. He was also in Washington at the same time as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, though one source said that timing was coincidental.

The Saudi defense minister discussed a number of issues with Vance, including the joint strikes and Saudi Arabia’s response to attacks on its infrastructure, according to one of the sources. He also had a message from Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman that he wanted to deliver in person, the source said. Another source told CNN that Khalid wanted to convey his country’s view on the ongoing war.

The Saudi defense minister also met with President Donald Trump and discussed regional developments, a source familiar told CNN.

The meeting with Trump was added after Khalid’s meeting with Vance. The Saudi defense minister conveyed a message from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to Trump about the kingdom’s view on the war, a source familiar said.

The kingdom’s assessment, according to the sources, is that Iran will seek to create leverage through escalation and will continue trying to use pro-Iranian militias in Iraq and Yemen’s Houthis to do so. Saudi Arabia still wants to see de-escalation and believes that escalation and prolonging the war comes with major risks, the sources said, but that it will respond if necessary, as it did on Tuesday.

The Saudi response to the Houthis and the Iraqi militias was meant to make clear that attacking civilian infrastructure is a red line that will not go unanswered, although the kingdom still seeks de-escalation. It was also intended to send Iran’s proxies a message that this is not their war to fight, the sources said.

This post has been updated with additional details.

World.title: Why Iran chose to restart the fight after the US stopped firing
World.content:
Iran has brought days of relative calm in the Middle East to an end after launching what the US called a “surprise” attack in a striking change to the pattern of fighting.

Rather than responding to a fresh American strike, Tehran chose to restart the fight itself, showing a growing willingness to use military force to shape the course of the war on its own terms.

This in turn sets the stage for fresh escalation. “We are going to beat the f**king sh*t out of them,” US President Donald Trump told Fox News Wednesday morning. “We’ll be hitting them hard. They’re going to get a beating.”

That threat could hardly have surprised Tehran, which launched its missiles knowing they might bring US bombers back.

Trump had attributed last week’s pause to a request from Iran because “they asked us very nicely” and wanted talks. Tehran never publicly committed to the recent pause, although a senior Iranian official said “our armed forces also decided not to take military action.”

That makes Iran’s decision to resume fire all the more significant.

Hours after publicly signaling that it would match the US restraint, Tehran targeted American forces – apparently deciding that raising the pressure was worth the risk of restarting the nightly bombardment.

“Something appears to have changed fundamentally in Iran’s approach, particularly regarding its willingness to initiate a strike if it considers that to be the only viable option,” Hamid Reza Azizi, a researcher at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs, wrote on X.

US President Donald Trump, right, meets Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at White House on Tuesday. Maâayan Toaf/GPO/Anadolu/Getty Images

Iran’s strike came soon after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s meeting with Trump in Washington, DC, which the Israeli leader described as “one of the best conversations” the two have had following growing friction between the pair. Hours before the meeting, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Israel had wanted to strike Iranian energy infrastructure but had been held back by the Trump administration.

“The attack appears to have been a signal related to Netanyahu’s visit to the White House earlier in the day,” wrote Azizi. “It suggests that Iran’s military strategy may have changed and that Tehran is now prepared to launch a preemptive strike if it detects signs of an imminent threat.”

Shortly after the attack in Jordan, the US and Saudi militaries jointly struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq. US Central Command framed the Iraq operation not as retaliation for the Jordan attack, but as a response to more than 30 drone attacks against US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure over the previous 72 hours.

The overnight escalation showed how the war is widening. Saudi Arabia, long wary of being pulled directly into the conflict, is becoming more deeply involved as it faces threats on three fronts: the Houthis in Yemen, Iran-backed militias in Iraq, and Iran itself.

Damage at a site belonging to Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) following airstrikes that the PMF said were carried out by US and Saudi forces, in Bartella, Nineveh province, Iraq, on Wednesday. Khalid Al-Mousily/Reuters

“The central challenge facing Washington and its Gulf partners is that neither Iran nor its regional allies appear willing to retreat from what they now define as core strategic objectives,” Danny Citrinowicz, a senior researcher at Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies and a former head of the Iran branch in Israeli military intelligence, wrote on X.

“Tehran continues to insist on maintaining its leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, while the Houthis have made clear that they will not end their campaign unless the Saudi-led (blockade) imposed on them (is) lifted.”

‘Nothing more than a fantasy’

In an interview with Iranian state television published just hours before the attack in Jordan, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi offered perhaps one of the clearest articulations of Tehran’s position yet. Iran had stopped firing, he suggested, but would not hesitate to resume hostilities if its claim of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz was challenged.

Tehran could not consider itself victorious if the strait returned to its prewar status, the deputy foreign minister said. The waterway had become central to the country’s national security and a “defensive tool.”

When the interviewer asked why Tehran had risked restarting the war by attacking commercial ships despite a functioning ceasefire, Gharibabadi said Iran regarded efforts by Oman and the US to establish a rival shipping route through the strait as a red line. Allowing that route to operate, he argued, would have reduced Iran’s claim to the “effective exercise of sovereignty” over the waterway to “nothing more than a fantasy.”

“One might look at it simply and ask why Iran would hit three commercial ships with missiles just because they turned off their GPS, potentially restarting a war,” he said. “But if you look behind the scenes, you see that the arrangements applied to the Strait of Hormuz will have a long-term impact on the security of the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

From Tehran’s perspective, Washington’s pause in attacks on Iran reflects “strategic weakness rather than restraint,” Citrinowicz wrote. That perception risks fueling a cycle in which Iran escalates to impose greater costs, while neither side backs down for fear of losing credibility.

The US and its partners therefore face a choice, he argued: accommodate some Iranian demands, or accept the prospect of a prolonged conflict marked by mounting attacks on shipping, energy infrastructure and trade routes.

Aida Karimi, Eyad Kourdi, Dana Karni, Mohammed Tawfeeq and Tal Shalev contributed to this report.

World.title: Kangwa encourages professionalism in the public service
World.content:
Secretary to the Cabinet Patrick Kangwa has called on senior public servants to uphold professionalism, accountability and integrity while accelerating the implementation of government policies.

Mr Kangwa charged that public confidence in government depends not only on sound policies but also on professionalism, accountability, transparency and prudent management of public resources by public servants.

“Public confidence in government depends not only on the policies we formulate, but equally on the integrity, efficiency and transparency with which we implement them,” said Mr Kangwa.

The Secretary was speaking today at the Seventh Senior Public Service Management meeting held under the theme: “Economic Growth and Future Prospects for Our Country,” in Lusaka.

He noted that the theme was both timely and relevant, reminding public workers that sustainable economic growth is not an end in itself, but a means of improving the lives of citizens.

“Through employment creation, poverty reduction and enhanced public service delivery,” he added.

The Secretary to the Cabinet explained that sustainable economic growth must translate into improved livelihoods through job creation, poverty reduction and efficient public service delivery.

Mr Kangwa said the government’s macroeconomic reforms implemented over the past five years have strengthened economic growth, reduced inflation, restored investor confidence and enhanced the country’s investment climate through prudent fiscal management and structural reforms.

He said balanced regional development remains a key priority, noting that while mining continues to be a major pillar of the economy, sectors such as agriculture, tourism, manufacturing, energy and fisheries offer significant opportunities for economic diversification and inclusive growth across all provinces.

He identified climate-smart agriculture, renewable energy expansion, value addition in mining, tourism diversification, digital transformation and human capital development as critical priorities for sustaining Zambia’s economic growth.

He also appealed to Zambians to maintain peace before, during and after the forthcoming general elections, stressing that elections should unite rather than divide the nation.

Paying tribute to the late southern Province Permanent Secretary Namani Monze, who died on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, Mr Kangwa described Dr. Monze as a dedicated public servant whose career spanned more than two decades in the health sector and public administration.

He narrated that Dr. Monze served as a Resident Doctor, Senior Registrar, Medical Superintendent, Senior Medical Superintendent, Provincial Health Officer and later Acting Permanent Secretary before being confirmed as Permanent Secretary for Southern Province in 2021.

Mr Kangwa noted that Dr. Monze’s professionalism, humility and inclusive leadership earned him respect across government and that his passing is a great loss to the public service and the nation at large.

World.title: First Consignment of Ballot Papers Arrives in Lusaka
World.content:
The first consignment of ballot papers for the August 13 General Election has arrived in the country, with the final consignment expected tomorrow.

A total of 202 out of the expected 387 pallets of ballot papers arrived aboard a chartered flight at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport in Lusaka this morning.

Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) Chairperson Mwangala Zaloumis said the verification of the ballot papers by stakeholders will begin on Friday, July 31, 2026, at 09:00 hours at the ECZ Silverest Warehouse in Lusaka.

Ms Zaloumis said the Commission is satisfied with the arrival process, which was witnessed by various stakeholders, adding that the ballot papers will be securely stored at the ECZ warehouse in Silverest.

She also appealed to political parties to conduct peaceful campaigns as the country approaches polling day.

Meanwhile, stakeholders who witnessed the arrival and transportation of the first consignment of ballot papers to the Silverest Warehouse expressed satisfaction with the process.

UPND Media Director Mark Simuwe described the process as transparent.

Citizen First Lusaka Province Secretary Glenda Lupa also expressed satisfaction with the first consignment received.

And SACCORD Executive Director Arthur Muyunda appealed to Zambians to obtain information from credible sources.

World.title: Angry Villagers Burn Vehicle Belonging to Parliamentary Candidate
World.content:
A vehicle belonging to Kapoche Independent Parliamentary Candidate Stephen Miti was burnt by angry villagers in Chieftainess Kawaza’s area of Sinda District after it was allegedly suspected of being used for stock theft.

Eastern Province Police Commanding Officer Robertson Mweemba confirmed the incident, saying the vehicle, a pearl white Ractic bearing registration number CAD 2547 and valued at K120,000, was destroyed in the fire.

Mr Mweemba said the blaze also destroyed two bales of chitenge materials valued at K2,280 and K3,850 in cash, bringing the total value of the property lost to K126,130.

He said the incident occurred around 19:30 hours at Lemmy Village.

According to Mr Mweemba, the driver had initially parked the vehicle at a football pitch but was advised by some residents to move it into the village to avoid it being mistaken for a vehicle used by cattle rustlers.

He said shortly after the vehicle was parked in the village, a group of people began searching for its owner, accusing him of being in the area to steal cattle.

Mr Mweemba said the driver sensed danger and attempted to flee in the vehicle but was unable to proceed after the road became impassable. He then abandoned the vehicle and ran away.

He said when Mr Miti noticed that the driver had taken longer than expected to meet him, he called and was informed about the incident.

Mr Mweemba said the parliamentary candidate later went to Lemmy Village, where he found the vehicle engulfed in flames.

Police have since opened an inquiry file, and investigations into the incident have commenced.

World.title: Sate Sate” retires again, becomes Nkana strikers coach ‎
World.content:
Nkana Football Club legend Ronald “Sate Sate” Kampamba has retired from active football for the second time.

‎

‎The club on Thursday announced that the Super League star is taking up the role of strikers coach on the Nkana technical bench.

‎

‎Kampamba first retired in August 2024 before rescinding his decision six months later after being persuaded by Coach Mwenya Chipepo. He featured in a few games in the just-ended 2025/2026 season for Kalampa.

‎

‎“Nkana Football Club is pleased to announce the appointment of former striker Ronald ‘Sate Sate’ Kampamba as the club’s strikers coach, marking the beginning of an exciting new chapter in the Kalampa legend’s football journey,” the club confirmed in a statement.

‎

‎“A familiar face to the Nkana faithful, Kampamba transitions from the pitch to the technical bench after a distinguished playing career that saw him become one of the club’s most admired forwards. His appointment reflects Nkana FC’s continued commitment to nurturing home-grown talent and preserving the club’s rich football heritage by integrating former players into the technical set-up,” the club stated.

‎

‎At his peak, Kampamba won the Super League title twice with his boyhood club Nkana. He also won the Super League golden boot twice.

‎

‎In 2015, the striker had unsuccessful stints at Egyptian side Wadi Degla and Belgian club Lierse SK.

‎

‎Locally, Kampamba played only for Nkana and Kansanshi Dynamos after being groomed by Kitwe Soccer Academy.

‎

‎He earned 11 caps for the Chipolopolo.
