World.title: Kalaba asks ConCourt to dismiss petition seeking to bar him from presidential race
World.content:
Kalaba asks Constitutional Court to dismiss petition seeking to bar him from presidential race

Citizens First president Harry Kalaba has asked the Constitutional Court to dismiss with costs a petition seeking to bar him from contesting the 13 August presidential election, arguing that the withdrawal of his running mate does not invalidate his candidature.

In his response to the petition, Kalaba says he remains a duly nominated presidential candidate because neither the Constitution nor the Electoral Process Act provides that the withdrawal of a running mate after nominations automatically nullifies a valid presidential nomination.

He states that he was lawfully nominated by the Electoral Commission of Zambia together with his running mate after meeting all constitutional and legal requirements. Kalaba admits that his former running mate, Moses Mawere, withdrew, but contends that the development has no legal effect on his candidature.

“The Constitution does not provide that the subsequent withdrawal of a running mate automatically nullifies a valid nomination or disqualifies a presidential candidate. Having been validly nominated by the Electoral Commission of Zambia, the 2nd respondent’s nomination remains valid,” Kalaba states.

He argues that the petitioner has misinterpreted the Constitution by assuming that the withdrawal of a running mate automatically disqualifies a presidential candidate, when no such provision exists.

Kalaba also denies violating articles 90, 110 and 266 of the Constitution, arguing that the cited provisions do not regulate the validity of presidential nominations or prescribe disqualification following the withdrawal of a running mate.

“Where the Constitution intends to disqualify a presidential candidate, it does so in clear and mandatory language. In the absence of such a provision, this court ought not to read into the Constitution a ground of disqualification,” he states.

Kalaba has urged the Constitutional Court to dismiss the petition with costs.

The petition was filed by Youth Alliance Party president Mark Mwachilenga, who wants the court to declare Kalaba and Organised People’s Party president Brian Mushimba ineligible to contest the 13 August presidential election. He says both men are no longer eligible because they no longer have running mates.

Alternatively, Mwachilenga seeks an order allowing the two candidates to nominate replacement running mates before polling day.

The case is one of several legal disputes stemming from an unusually high number of candidate and running-mate withdrawals ahead of this year’s election, a trend that Governance Elections Advocacy Research Services Initiative board chairperson Luckson Lungu has said prompted recent constitutional amendments to prevent the electoral calendar from being disrupted.

The Constitutional Court has yet to rule on the matter, with polling day fourteen days away.

World.title: Boxer Ngulube exits Glasgow 2026 after narrow loss
World.content:
Team Zambia boxer Albert Ngulube’s quest for a Commonwealth Games medal came to an end on Wednesday night after a spirited performance in the Men’s 60kg Quarter-Final at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

‎

‎Ngulube narrowly lost to Jude Gallagher of Northern Ireland by a 2–3 split decision, following a closely contested bout that showcased his determination and fighting spirit.

‎

‎Despite the defeat, the young boxer can hold his head high after an impressive debut at the Commonwealth Games, where he competed confidently against one of the tournament’s top-ranked boxers.

‎

‎According to the National Olympic Committee of Zambia, his performance reflects the bright future of Zambian boxing, with valuable experience gained on one of the biggest stages in Commonwealth sport.

‎

‎On the running track, Team Zambia sprinter Edna Ng’andula’s quest for a place in the Women’s 200m final came to an unfortunate end after she was disqualified in the semi-final.

‎

‎Ng’andula had crossed the finish line in second place with a personal best time of 23.50 seconds, but was disqualified for stepping on the lane line during the race.

‎

‎She will now turn her attention to the Mixed 4x400m Relay, where she will aim to help Team Zambia deliver another strong performance.

‎

‎In lawn bowls, Mildred Mkandawire lost in the Women’s Singles competition to Bridget Herselman of South Africa in straight sets, 13–1 and 8–4.

‎

‎Despite the setbacks, Team Zambia continues to compete with determination, resilience, and pride as the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games enter the decisive stages.

World.title: YUYI’S SUDDEN EXIT: Transfer followed by unverified arrest claims
World.content:
Yuyi’s abrupt exit fuels speculation as unverified arrest claims circulate

The sudden transfer of former Copperbelt Police Commissioner Yuyi Mwala to Lusaka has taken a dramatic turn after unverified reports circulating on social media alleged that the senior police officer had been arrested in connection with the alleged theft of six trucks reportedly loaded with copper.

The Zambia Police Service has not issued any official statement confirming the alleged arrest, and by press time Lusaka Times had been unable to independently verify the claims. Nevertheless, the reports have spread rapidly across several online platforms, emerging barely days after police authorities confirmed Mwala’s transfer from the Copperbelt command.

On Monday, police announced that former Police Service spokesperson Rae Hamoonga had been appointed Copperbelt Police Commissioner, replacing Mwala, who confirmed in a farewell message that he had been transferred to Lusaka for redeployment.

The timing of the transfer, coming less than three weeks before Zambia’s general election, immediately attracted public attention, with many questioning whether it formed part of an ordinary reshuffle or was linked to other undisclosed developments.

Those questions intensified on Wednesday after social media accounts and online publications began circulating claims alleging that Mwala had been arrested and was being transported to Mufulira as part of investigations into the alleged theft of six trucks. The allegations remain unverified, and no official confirmation had been issued by police authorities at the time of publication.

If confirmed, the developments would represent a dramatic fall for one of Zambia’s most prominent and controversial provincial police commanders, whose policing style has repeatedly drawn criticism from opposition political parties during successive deployments.

Throughout his tenure on the Copperbelt, Mwala frequently found himself at the centre of politically charged disputes involving opposition leaders. During this year’s election campaign, National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity presidential candidate Brian Mundubile accused police under Mwala’s command of frustrating opposition activities and applying the law selectively, allegations the commissioner consistently rejected.

One of the most publicised incidents followed the vandalism of vehicles belonging to the NRPUP campaign team in Kitwe. Opposition officials accused police of failing to arrest those responsible despite allegedly knowing their identities, accusations that Mwala denied while maintaining that police had acted professionally.

Former Nkana Member of Parliament Binwell Mpundu, who publicly criticised Mwala following that incident, reacted at the time by accusing the commissioner of refusing to pursue suspects linked to political violence. In a social media post that has resurfaced following the latest developments, Mpundu wrote that “time settles all matters,” comments many online users have since linked to the circulating reports, although no evidence has emerged connecting his earlier remarks to the current allegations.

Mwala’s time on the Copperbelt was not his first encounter with political controversy. During previous provincial postings, opposition parties repeatedly accused police under his command of selectively enforcing the Public Order Act and restricting opposition political activities, allegations consistently denied by the Zambia Police Service.

He also featured prominently in several high-profile policing decisions involving former President Edgar Lungu and other opposition leaders during the politically tense period following the 2021 general election. Supporters of the former Head of State accused police of imposing excessive restrictions on his movements and public engagements, while police maintained that their actions were solely intended to preserve public order.

Supporters of the ruling United Party for National Development, however, often defended Mwala, arguing that he was simply enforcing the law during an increasingly polarised political environment.

For now, the circumstances surrounding his redeployment remain officially unexplained. Equally, the allegations circulating online regarding his purported arrest remain unconfirmed.

Lusaka Times will continue to seek comment from Zambia Police Headquarters and will update readers should official confirmation or further information become available.

World.title: DC narrowly escapes lynching after urging mourners to vote UPND
World.content:
Mazabuka District Commissioner Oliver Mulomba narrowly escaped being lynched by angry mourners at a funeral on Tuesday after urging them to vote for President Hakainde Hichilema and United Party for National Development candidates in next month’s election.

The incident occurred during the burial of a community member when Mulomba addressed mourners and asked them to support Hichilema and the ruling party’s candidates. Witnesses said the gathering turned hostile almost immediately, accusing Mulomba of politicising a solemn occasion.

“The situation quickly escalated, forcing Mr Mulomba to leave under tight security to avoid being attacked,” witness Josphat Munjila said.

Mulomba was forced off the podium and required a security escort to leave the cemetery safely. The incident comes amid growing political tension in parts of Southern Province ahead of the general election, with residents citing frustration over the high cost of living and poor service delivery.

In a separate incident, UPND cadres disrupted an authorised campaign rally for independent Monze Central parliamentary candidate Elvis Mainza in Katimba Ward. The Electoral Commission of Zambia’s official campaign timetable had confirmed Mainza was cleared to hold activities in the area.

Instead, a group of UPND cadres arrived in an unregistered white Toyota Hilux and disrupted the gathering, attacking Mainza’s supporters and chasing people with stones, according to eyewitnesses Rabecca Choombwa and Cynthia Habukali. They said armed and masked cadres took over the venue while beating people, bringing the rally to a sudden halt.

Mainza’s team described the attack as a clear attempt to intimidate voters and suppress alternative voices in Monze Central.

A third and separate incident was reported in Kitwe, where several vehicles belonging to National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity presidential candidate Brian Mundubile’s campaign team had their windows smashed during a Copperbelt tour. One victim appeared in a widely circulated video bleeding and claiming attackers had also stolen money from him.

Eyewitnesses said the attackers were youths suspected to be aligned with the ruling party, with some reportedly using unregistered vehicles in what appeared to be an organised effort to disrupt the opposition campaign. Images also circulated showing a young man brandishing what appeared to be a pistol during the disturbance. Police say some suspects have been arrested, drawn from both the ruling party and the Tonse Alliance, though it remains unclear whether the individual seen with the firearm is among those detained.

National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity information and publicity chairperson Elias Kamanga condemned the Kitwe violence, accusing Hichilema of having endorsed attacks on the opposition by failing to condemn them.

“That is why this man you have at community house has never condemned his party for the violence, and this is an eye opener that even under the previous administration the violence you experienced was UPND,” Kamanga said.

The three incidents have added to mounting concern from civic and religious leaders over the tone of the campaign with just fourteen days remaining before polling day, with calls growing for police to act even-handedly against perpetrators regardless of party affiliation.
