World.title: Dream Wknd, partners ready to welcome thousands to MoBay
World.content:
Mobay Mayor Richard Vernon addresses the recent launch of Dream Wknd 2026 held at Pier 1.

MONTEGO BAY, St James — Dream Entertainment Limited, St James Municipal Corporation, and Jamaica Constabulary Force say all systems are in place for Dream Wknd’s inaugural staging in Montego Bay.

With months of planning and cross-agency collaboration will culminate in what is expected to be one of Jamaica’s largest entertainment events of the summer.

More than 30,000 patrons are expected to descend on the tourism capital over the coming days for the festival’s first staging outside its long-time home of Negril, bringing a significant boost to the local economy while showcasing Montego Bay’s growing capacity to host major international events.

Chairman of Dream Entertainment Kamal Bankay said organisers have spent months working alongside government agencies, venue operators, and service providers to ensure every aspect of the festival is ready ahead of Thursday’s opening.

“We have been working very closely with the venues and the planning authorities in St James,” Bankay said. “That includes the municipal corporation, the Jamaica Constabulary Force, the Ministry of Health, the Jamaica Fire Brigade, and the other agencies responsible for issuing the relevant approvals.”

He said the work has extended beyond regulatory requirements to include detailed coordination with venue operators and event partners responsible for delivering the festival experience.

“Based on where we are now, all of those preparations have been completed and the necessary systems are in place, so we’re ready to welcome patrons when the events begin on Thursday,” he said.

Bankay added that while Dream Wknd will deliver its signature entertainment experience, the festival also provides visitors with an opportunity to experience Montego Bay beyond the event venues.

“When you come to Montego Bay, just know that it’s a great city in its own right, and Dream Wknd is really there to elevate what’s already on offer,” he said. “Visitors can enjoy the city’s hotels, restaurants, beaches, and attractions throughout the weekend.”

Mayor Richard Vernon described Dream Wknd’s arrival in Montego Bay as a significant milestone for the city, saying it reinforces its standing as one of the Caribbean’s leading tourism and entertainment destinations.

“Dream Wknd’s expansion to Montego Bay is a landmark moment for Jamaica’s tourism capital,” Vernon said. “It affirms our city’s reputation as a premier entertainment destination in the Caribbean and demonstrates confidence in our ability to continue hosting world-class events, even during our most challenging times.”

Vernon said his team has worked closely with partners to ensure the city is prepared to welcome the influx of visitors. Traffic management plans have been finalised, public health protocols activated, and emergency contingencies established to support the festival weekend.

“Our hospitality sector has mobilised to meet demand, while local businesses are prepared… This readiness ensures that Dream Wknd will be a successful event and drive sustained economic activity across Montego Bay,” said Vernon.

Senior Superintendent Eron Samuels, commander of the St James Police Division, said the police have developed a comprehensive security plan in partnership with other stakeholders.

“Our objective is to create a safe environment where patrons can enjoy the festivities while residents and visitors continue to feel secure,” Samuels said.

He encouraged patrons to celebrate responsibly by planning their transportation in advance, avoiding drinking and driving, securing their personal belongings, remaining aware of their surroundings and following the instructions of police officers, event security personnel and emergency responders.

“Our message is simple: Enjoy the event, make lasting memories, but make safety your priority,” he said.

In addition to extensive logistical preparations, organisers say patrons can also expect an elevated festival experience through the involvement of Dream WKND’s major brand partners, each bringing unique activations designed to complement the music and entertainment.

Red Stripe and its portfolio of brands will deliver vibrant social spaces across four signature events: Guinness at Dream Live, Casamigos at Daydreams, Red Stripe at YUSH, and Smirnoff at Igloo. Meanwhile, the Campari Group will bring premium activations, signature cocktail experiences, and interactive brand engagements to Wet ‘N Wild with Magnum, Foul Play with J Wray & Nephew, and Xodus Remedy presented by Campari.

Festivalgoers can also look forward to high-energy experiences from Boom Energy Drink, whose touchpoints are designed to keep the excitement going throughout the weekend. Mother’s will round out the culinary experience with specially curated dishes prepared throughout the weekend, providing hearty, flavourful meal options to keep patrons fuelled while they enjoy the overall festival atmosphere.

Dream Entertainment says the collective investment by its corporate partners reflects a shared commitment to delivering a world-class entertainment experience, with immersive brand experiences carefully integrated into the festival to ensure patrons enjoy much more than just the performances onstage.

World.title: LEAPING TO HISTORY
World.content:
Tajay Gayle (Photo: AFP)

TAJAY Gayle created history on Wednesday when he won Jamaica’s first-ever men’s long jump gold medal at the Commonwealth Games (CWG).

Shot putter Lloydricia Cameron claimed a bronze medal at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow, Scotland, as Jamaica’s medal tally went up to four — inclusive of three gold and a bronze — at the 23rd edition of the Games.

Romaine Beckford and Demario Prince had opened Jamaica’s medal account on Monday with gold medals in the men’s high jump and 110m hurdles, respectively.

Expectations are high for more medals on Thursday with finals in the women’s triple jump and discus throw competitions.

After placing fourth at the 2018 Commonwealth Games in Australia, Gayle jumped 8.15m (1.5m/s) to become the first Jamaican man to win a long jump competition. He is the first Jamaican man to win a medal at the Games since Wesley Clayton won back-to-back bronze in 1962 and 1966.

India’s Sreeshankar took consecutive silver medals after a best mark of 8.09m (1.3m/s), just ahead of Stephen Mackenzie of Scotland who was third with 8.08m (0.9m/s). Jamaican Jordan Turner was ninth with 7.65m (0.1m/s).

Cameron, who won her first national championships title this year, improved on her fourth-place finish from four years ago in Birmingham, England, taking the bronze with a best of 17.87m in the final round to eclipse Manpreet Kaur of India.

Canada’s two-time World Athletics Indoor champion Sarah Mitton defended her title with an effort of 19.88m. Nigeria’s 19-year-old Jessica Oji took the silver medal with 17.87m, getting the edge over Cameron with a better second throw.

National champion Ackelia Smith and NCAA winner Shantae Foreman are set to take on world leader and Olympic champion Thea Lafond of Dominica in the women’s triple jump on Thursday.

Jamaica’s Samantha Hall is the Commonwealth leader in the women’s discus throw and will start as pre-championships favourite going into the final.

There will also be qualifying in the 100m hurdles in which Kerrica Hill and Megan Simmonds are set to compete. In the men’s triple jump Jordan Scott, who is ranked number one, is also down to feature.

Kelly Ann Beckford qualified for the final of the women’s 800m after placing third in her semi-finals in 1:59.96, beaten to the finish line by Lilian Odira (1:59.39) of Kenya and Shafiqua Maloney (1:59.81) of St Vincent and the Grenadines.

Adelle Tracey was fourth in her heat in 2:01.54 for 10th overall.

Other Jamaicans, including 200m and women’s 400m hurdles runners, progressed past the first round of their respective events on Wednesday.

National champion Sanique Walker and Shiann Salmon, the latter who was second four years ago in Birmingham, topped the qualifying in the women’s 400m hurdles.

Walker won her heat in 54.83 seconds and Salmon topped hers in 55.30 to booked places in Friday’s final.

National champion Assinie Wilson was second in his first round heat in the men’s 400m hurdles in 49.19.

Lavanya Williams and Alana Reid were also the fastest in the women’s 200m first round.

Williams ran 22.91 (0.8m/s) to win heat five and national champion Reid clocked 22.95 (1.7m/s) to claim heat six as they made safe passage through to Thursday’s semi-finals.

All three Jamaican men also advanced in the 200m.

Christopher Taylor was second in his heat in 20.36 (1.6m/s), the same time given to Ghana’s Joseph Paul Amoah, who was declared the winner.

Roshawn Clarke won his heat in 20.56 (1/0m/s) and Jevaughn Powell recorded a wind-aided 20.28 (2.6m/s) to top his heat.

World.title: Chef Colin Brown’s HOMECOMING CHAÎNE FEAST
World.content:
Yellowfin tuna crudo with lime-ginger marinade, Scotch bonnet oil, ripe mango salsa and breadfruit crisp (Photo: Aceion Cunningham)

Sun-kissed afternoon, the hum of conversation, and the clink of glasses set the scene at Uncorked Ochi at Drax Hall on Sunday, July 26 as Chaîne des Rôtisseurs Jamaïque, Select Brands, and Uncorked hosted a celebratory bistro brunch showcasing the return of Chef Colin Brown to Jamaican shores. Brown — back from an international run of kitchens — teamed with Uncorked’s culinary team to present a lively fusion of island flavours and classic French techniques that won praise from members and guests alike.

The cold and seafood station opened the meal with refined island flair: Yellowfin tuna crudo brightened with a lime-ginger marinade, Scotch bonnet oil, ripe mango salsa, and a crisp of breadfruit; and an escoveitch conch paired with calabash lobster, spiced pickled vegetables, allspice, and lime zest that married Caribbean acidities with steely seafood sweetness.

The opening of the smoked and slow-roast station followed. A pimento-smoked salmon with a rustic salsa; golden goat, glazed with Appleton rum and finished with a nutmeg-thyme jus offered deep, caramelised rum notes; and Blue Mountain coffee-crusted pork belly, lacquered in a tamarind-molasses glaze balanced bitter, sweet and savoury. Braised oxtail croquettes, stuffed with a butter-bean purée with chive oil, provided a textural and flavourful nod to Jamaica’s comfort-cook traditions, while a live action station with pimento-smoked roasted leg of lamb, scented with rosemary, orange zest and tarragon, rounded out the roast offerings.

Side dishes and local provisions were treated with equal care: roasted sweet potatoes and breadfruit crowned with coconut butter and toasted pimento, herbed yam croquettes, creamy coconut rice with gungo peas, callaloo-pak choi sautéed with ginger, garlic and island five-spice, and an inventive green banana risotto studded with aged local artisan cheese. These accompaniments anchored the menu in terroir while supporting the international techniques on display.

Dessert showcased Jamaica’s signature ingredients in elegant formats: Wray & Nephew rum and gingerbread pudding bathed in warm coconut custard, a sorrel-hibiscus panna cotta with candied ginger, and a guava tart in flaky coconut pastry. Sweet finishes were complemented by a chilled limoncello cooler pairing that cut through the richness.

Select Brands curated the beverage pours, pairing the menu with a sparkling and wine line-up that included Veuve Clicquot Brut NV, Kettmeir Pinot Grigio 2024, Terra Alpina Chardonnay 2022, Aqua di Venus Rosé, Tassajara Pinot Noir 2022 and Dominio Fournier 2020. The thoughtful beverage selection underscored the brunch’s balance of celebration and culinary craft.

The event was both a welcome-home for Chef Brown and a statement of culinary collaboration — a tasteful fusion that celebrated Jamaica’s pantry while leaning into French technique and presentation, a thrust Brown is quick to emphasise in the Jamaican culinary space.

“We have to cook our own food, add our cultural perspective and use the techniques from France, Italy and we’ll become masters by taking an indigenous cuisine and refining it. For today’s menu we used the Seville orange, rice vinegar, Mirin, sushi ginger, ripe mango, tomato and we boiled the breadfruit in the skin, sliced thinly, fried it to make a nice crisp and this came out really well for the yellow fin tuna. escoveitch conch and lobster, we made a lobster bisque for the base, boil it and season only with Scotch bonnet powder, sear it, keeping it fresh and nice. For the conch we cooked it for hours and sliced it thinly, tossed and fried keeping it crispy,” Brown explained.

“The salmon was done of more a jerk style but with more kick to it. Everyone is more use to curry goat, but we slow-cooked the goat with Appleton rum, nutmeg and thyme, making it a well-balanced dish. The crispy pork belly was cooked in Blue Mountain coffee jerk for two and half hours and glazed with June plum and lime and dusted with Blue Mountain coffee, giving you the sweet, sour, coffee flavour and the jerk. The oxtail was also slow cooked and the lamb leg we marinated for three days,” Brown added.

World.title: Jamaica snatch last minute draw against Panama in U20
World.content:
Jaquan Brown of Jamaica celebrates his equaliser in the young Reggae Boyz' Concacaf Under-20 Championship match against Panama on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. The game ended 2-2. (Photo: Concacaf/Instagram)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Jamaica rallied from two goals down to earn a courageous draw against Panama in their Concacaf U20 Championships Group C at Estadio Universitario BUAP in Puebla, Mexico on Wednesday.

The result kept Jamaica’s hopes of advancing to the quarterfinals alive as they are on four points, one more than Canada who will play Honduras in the second game, while Panama are on one point from two games.

Jamaica are also third in the overall rankings that include teams from the other groups, only behind the USA and Mexico, both of who have won their first two games.

Desperate to earn a win after losing 3-0 to Canada on Sunday, Panama got off to a fast start and were ahead 2-0 after 22 minutes with goals from Moisés Richards in the 13th minute and Carlos Rodriguez in the 22nd minute.

It could have been worse had VAR not ruled out another goal for Panama in the 36th minute.

Jahmarie Nolan, who had scored the first goal in the 2-1 win over Honduras, pulled a goal back for Jamaica in the 62nd minute before Jaquan Brown headed home a freekick from second half substitute Jamione Lyle in time added.

It was the second time in a row that Jamaica scored on the final play of the game, in time added, after Brandon Bent had scored the winner against Honduras in time added.

The coaches had made one change to the starting team, Che Gardner of Stockport County replacing Sean Leighton.

Starting team:

Joshua Grant, Jaquan Brown, Jahmarie Nolan, Jermaine Young, Jabarie

Howell, Jahmani Bell, Che Gardner, Duwayne Burgher, Santana

Headley, Kimarly Scott, Brandon Bent

—Paul A Reid

World.title: No social media ban
World.content:
Health and Wellness Minister Dr Christopher Tufton (left) in discussion with Dr Ganesh Shetty (right), acting director, adolescent mental health, Ministry of Health & Wellness, as well as lead researcher and fellow at The University of the West Indies and consultant with the Ministry of Health Dr Stephen Johnson during Tuesday’s media briefing to present the findings from a National Study on Social Media Use and the Protection of Children. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

In what is said to be “one of the most comprehensive national assessments ever undertaken” on social media use by minors in Jamaica, the majority of citizens surveyed have baulked at a total ban but say Government must lead the way in implementing policy with strong parental involvement when it comes to enforcement.

“The results show overwhelming public support for some level of Government action,” said Health and Wellness Minister Dr Christopher Tufton.

He was delivering the main address, Tuesday, during a press conference to release findings of the National Study on Social Media Use and the Protection of Children.

The event was held at the Courtyard by Mariott Hotel in St Andrew.

According to Tufton, nine out of every 10 respondents, or 90.2 per cent, support Government regulation of minors’ social media use, while 2.9 per cent expressed opposition. In addition, he said, nearly 84 per cent believe Jamaica should establish a clear national policy framework governing minors’ use of social media.

Tufton said from reading the study he formed the opinion that the subject has been “a long-standing concern, but not talked about as much”.

“I was surprised when I saw the results. A strong message: The Jamaican people recognise that this is an issue requiring national attention, and they expect thoughtful leadership on the issue. But perhaps the most significant finding is not simply that Jamaicans support some levels of Government action; it is that they believe this responsibility must be shared, and I was very heartened at that,” the minister stated.

Citing the report, he said only 12.7 per cent of respondents believe Government should lead this effort alone.

“Again, that’s very good to know, because it means people will want to engage,” Tufton said, while adding that 40.5 per cent of respondents believe parents/guardians should play the leading role, while another 39 per cent favoured shared responsibility among parents, schools, Government, communities, and other stakeholders.

“The finding is especially important, because it reminds us of something we already know: No Government policy can replace active parenting, and that’s very important to note. No legislation can replace guidance within the home. No technology platform can replace the influence of families, teachers, and communities. Protecting children online, therefore, must be a national partnership, and that’s a very big theme. A takeaway from this: A national partnership,” said the minister.

He noted that the survey also revealed that Jamaicans favour balance rather than extremes, and the preferred approach was not simply stronger legal restrictions.

While acknowledging the positives brought by social media the health minister emphasised that the results of emerging research from 2025-2026 for Jamaica “confirms a strong link between social media use and increased anxiety, depression, and digital addiction, particularly among young persons and content creators”.

He said youth under 24 spend an average of six hours daily on social media, compared to five hours for adults and four hours for seniors.

Tufton stressed that the study is “intended for public consumption and discourse in the first instance, not any decision”, while at the same time assuring that there was no intention to “just wholesale adopt what entails elsewhere” as far as regulations are concerned.

Delving into the study during the event, Dr Stephen Johnson, lead researcher and fellow at The University of the West Indies and a consultant with the Ministry of Health, said the use of social media by minors has become a public health issue.

“We have data from the National Council on Drug Abuse [NCDA] indicating that 70 per cent of our minors sleep less than eight hours on an average school night. In terms of body image, [there is] low self-esteem; [we see] digital addiction from excessive screen time [of] three hours or more; having 68 per cent of our population being addicted. [There are issues of] online safety, cyberbullying, grooming, and being exposed to harmful content. Now, of course, there’s a need for Government not necessarily to be preventative, but to be proactive,” he said.

The sample of 1,027 individuals surveyed included Gen Zers, millennials, Gen X, and Boomers educated at the primary, vocational, and tertiary levels.

Dr Johnson emphasised that while the overwhelming majority, over 80 per cent of those interviewed, supported “a clear policy framework for minors’ social media use… the appetite for an outright ban it’s not really here… Persons are saying, while you’re doing this, be mindful that minors have rights,” the lead researcher disclosed.

Dr Ganash Shetty, acting director, adolescent mental health in the Ministry of Health, who pointed out that the algorithms behind social media platforms are created by behavioural specialists, spoke directly to youngsters in attendance.

World.title: Bounty Killer gets key to Kingston
World.content:
Rodney “Bounty Killer” Price delivering his acceptance speech Tuesday after receiving the Keys to the City of Kingston and the renaming of Wenchman Road in his honour.(Photo: Karl Mclarty)

FROM the inner-city community of Seaview Gardens in western St Andrew that raised him to conquering the global dancehall stage, Rodney “Bounty Killer” Price returned home Tuesday to receive the Key to the City of Kingston and the renaming of a road in his honour.

“It’s official, the king of Kingston with the keys to Kingston,” a jubilant Price declared as he accepted the city’s highest civic honour during a ceremony at Seaview Gardens Primary School.

In a further tribute to the dancehall icon, Wenchman Road — where Price spent much of his youth — was officially renamed Rodney Price Drive, following a petition from Seaview Gardens’ residents and approval by the Kingston and St Andrew Municipal Corporation (KSAMC).

Visibly moved by the recognition Price, who has also received the Order of Distinction for his invaluable contribution to Jamaica’s music scene, described the occasion as another meaningful milestone in his career, admitting that words could not fully express his gratitude.

“Today is really the unfolding of another historical chapter in my career. And this milestone is a very unusual and an uncommon accomplishment — the Keys to the City of Kingston,” he said, thanking the KSAMC, mayor of Kingston Andrew Swaby, and other officials for the honour.

Pointing to the road which now bears his name, Price recalled how his life was defined by it, noting that it had witnessed both the beginnings of his journey and some of his darkest moments. “This is more than just a ceremony. This is a celebration of troubles and trial and triumph and greatness. It’s just right round the road, that’s where I got shot when I was 16, right around there,” he said.

He thanked the KSAMC for immortalising the name, the battles, and the triumphs he carried long before he became known to the world as Bounty Killer.

“Our community is a golden garden. Hard work and dedication leads to these accomplishments and accolades in life. And then they say a king has never been crowned in his town, so what is this then?” questioned an evidently elated Price.

The entertainer who has won a Grammy award for his feature on No Doubt’s multi-platinum hit song Hey Baby and received a solo Grammy nomination, told the ceremony that the significance of the occasion far surpassed international acclamation.

“This is more than a Grammy to me. These are people who watched me emerge as a young artiste. These people are people who are personally involved in my upbringing, and for them to decide that I deserve the key to Kingston, this is something phenomenal,” he said.

For his part, Kingston Mayor Andrew Swaby congratulated Price and noted that the recognition is more than celebrating the successful musician, describing it as a statement about the values of the city and the potential that exists within communities such as Seaview Gardens.

“Too often communities like Seaview Gardens are viewed through the lens of their challenges rather than their possibilities. People sometimes make assumptions about what someone can achieve based on where they come from, but as we all should know by now an address does not determine one’s personal potential. What Bounty Killer’s life demonstrates is the clearest possible term that potential exists in every community; talent discipline and determination can emerge from anywhere for our young people,” said Swaby.

Announcing the renaming of Wenchman Road to Rodney Price Drive, Swaby said the tribute would ensure that the artiste’s legacy remains permanently etched in the community that shaped him.

“His name will remain fixed to this day, in this very community that raised him, so that anyone who passes through Seaview Gardens will know that greatness comes from these streets. So Bounty Killer, on behalf of the citizens of Kingston and St Andrew, thank you. Thank you for your music, for your mentorship, and for the contribution that you have made to Jamaica’s culture. This city is proud to recognise you as a son of Kingston, and it is an honour today to place this key in your hands,” said the mayor.

World.title: Grand day-long celebrations for Rita Marley’s 80th
World.content:
These young performers enjoyed the kids’ zone. (Photo: Rahyme McKenzie)

The Bob and Rita Marley foundations brought together supporters, partners, artistes, and community members to honour Alferita “Rita” Marley as she celebrated her 80th earthstrong under the theme ‘Thank You Jah 80’.

The day-long tribute celebrated Marley’s extraordinary legacy as a musician, philanthropist, entrepreneur, cultural advocate, and matriarch whose impact continues to inspire generations around the world.

Celebrations began at 6:30 am with Rise in Grace, a wellness and fitness experience at Bob Marley Museum that invited participants to embrace healthy living while reflecting on Rita Marley’s lifelong commitment to holistic well-being.

From 11:00 am to 3:00 pm Tuff Gong International came alive with a Family Fun Day, offering free entertainment and activities for all ages. Families enjoyed interactive games, storytelling, face painting, karaoke, water attractions, creative activities for children, dominoes, ludo, and complimentary health screenings. The activation reflected Rita Marley’s lifelong commitment to strengthening families, promoting wellness, and building resilient communities.

The festivities officially began with a prayer and blessing led by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, followed by cultural performances from students of Half-Way Tree Primary, Linstead Primary, Central Branch Primary, Meadowbrook Primary and Old Harbour Bay Culture Camp.

Music then took centre stage during the lunch hour concert, held from 1:00 pm to 2:00 pm and powered by Tapedeck, an independent music streaming and digital download platform.

Through a partnership with the Jamaica Cultural Development Commission (JCDC), the concert also provided a national stage for the 2026 Festival Song Competition finalists, reinforcing both organisations’ shared commitment to preserving and celebrating Jamaican culture.

Tim Quirk, founder of Tapedeck, commented: “Rita Marley’s musical journey is a living blueprint for creative independence. What she and Bob Marley established through Tuff Gong by leveraging their voices to amplify other independent artistes and producers resonates strongly with us at Tapedeck. We are honoured to be a part of this milestone birthday celebration as we welcome Tuff Gong International Distributors to Tapedeck and look forward to bringing Jamaica’s creative community to our audience.”

The day’s celebrations culminated with the highly anticipated Thank You Jah 80 Digital Celebration Concert at 5:00 pm, streamed on the Tuff Gong TV YouTube channel and Bob Marley’s Tuff Gong Radio on SiriusXM Channel 19. Hosted by Kamila McDonald and Ron Muschette, the concert featured performances by Tessanne Chin, Nadine Sutherland, Romain Virgo, Alaine, and Makeda, reaching audiences around the world and allowing supporters everywhere to join in celebrating the milestone.

CEO of the Bob Marley Group of Companies Cedella Marley shared: “We celebrate mommy every day, but turning 80 is a milestone that deserves to be honoured in a truly special way. She has spent her entire life showing up for us — not just as our mother, but as a guide, a protector, and an unwavering source of love. Beyond our family, she’s poured that same love into communities around the world, serving others with grace, compassion, and humility. Everything she has done has been rooted in love, so celebrating her is one small way for us to say thank you. She deserves every flower, every tribute, and every moment of appreciation. This celebration is our way of letting her know just how deeply she is loved.”

World.title: Spain, France, UK warn megafires show climate change is ‘threatening our way of life’
World.content:
Members of the Emergency Military Unit use controlled burns to halt the spread of wildfires in the Madrid border region on July 28, 2026. | Pablo Blazquez Dominguez/Getty Images

In joint statements, the three countries reaffirmed their commitment to fighting global warming.

BRUSSELS — The massive blazes raging in Spain and France epitomize the threat climate change is posing to Europe, the British government said in joint statements issued with the two fire-stricken countries overnight.

Wildfires have burned tens of thousands of hectares near Madrid and Bordeaux this week, razing hundreds of homes and displacing more than 300,000 people in one of the biggest fire-related evacuations Europe has seen to date.

Blazes have also erupted in other parts of the continent, which is suffering from widespread drought after Europe’s hottest June on record, including in the United Kingdom.

World.title: Tusk: ‘Everything indicates’ Russian cruise missile hit Poland
World.content:
Prime Minister of Poland Donald Tusk on his arrives for a dinner hosted on the occasion of the Summit of the Coalition of the Willing to Support Ukraine in Paris France on July 13, 2026. \ Bastien Ohier/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images

The object left a 10-meter crater but no casualties in Poland’s Lublin province near the Ukrainian border.

An airborne object crashed in eastern Poland early Thursday during Russia's latest attack on Ukraine, leaving behind a 10-meter-wide crater and scattered debris, said Polish authorities.

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha quickly claimed on X that it was "a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile" that violated NATO airspace. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk — who visited the site on Thursday morning — seemed to agree, saying that Poland was "ready to shoot down the missile if it continued its flight. Everything indicates that it was a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile."

The object was detected moving westward through Polish airspace at 3:40 a.m., according to the country's Operational Command. An F-16 fighter jet was sent to identify and intercept it, but the object disappeared from radar six minutes later, before it could be identified.

World.title: Watch out Brussels and Kyiv, Poland’s conservatives are veering right
World.content:
Allies of pro-EU Prime Minister Donald Tusk read it as good news. When Kaczyński stepped to the microphone to kick out Morawiecki, two lawmakers from Tusk’s governing coalition filmed themselves watching the speech, eating popcorn.

You can see why they might be happy. Before the split, POLITICO’s Poll of Polls put Tusk’s Civic Coalition at 32 percent support and PiS at 26 percent. PiS has now slumped to 22 percent.

But that is hardly the whole story. The combined forces of right-wing parties are still in a strong position if they team up for the 2027 election. And Friday’s split means that PiS is more likely to veer right in its alliances, choosing ideological consolidation over an attempt to win back the center.

The wing of PiS led by Morawiecki had argued the party needed to broaden its appeal and adopt a less combative approach toward Brussels. Kaczyński instead appears determined to recapture voters who have defected further right.

It is far from certain, however, how successfully Poland’s far-right parties can agree on a common agenda with PiS.

Among the potential beneficiaries of Friday’s split are parties that oppose Ukraine joining the European Union — and, in the case of Grzegorz Braun’s Federation of the Polish Crown movement, advocate taking Poland out of the bloc altogether.

World.title: The first election of the Andy Burnham era is already here
World.content:
“Let’s go in and have a look. Let’s open it up,” she said at a food market in Altrincham, a town in the south-west of Greater Manchester. Astley said Labour has had “an absolute stronghold of a vice-like grip” across the region for too long. “This is really the first time this level of political choice has been available to the voters,” she said.

Geraldine Coggins is the Green Party pick. She has stood in seven elections, and been elected as a councilor in Trafford three times.

Having joined the party in 2010, she is now relishing the growth in campaign resources after recent electoral successes, and said at a community garden cafe in Manchester that activists had come from as far away as Aberdeen and Cornwall to help out on the doorsteps.

Coggins’ pitch is that Greater Manchester needs a mayor to stand up to government — rather than a “Labour apologist,” a term she used to describe Craig. She also wants more devolution — including for mayors to be given the power to impose rent caps — and has her own bus pledge: to make them free for anyone under 22.

How will the vote be decided?

The mayoralty will once again be decided using the supplementary vote system — and that’s caused a little disquiet from Labour’s opponents on the right.

Voters will be asked to pick a first and second preference. If no candidate gets 50 percent or more of first preference votes, all but the top two candidates will be eliminated. The second preferences of voters who initially backed those losing candidates are then redistributed.

World.title: 'Crude language of MAGA’: Author Joyce Carol Oates defends 'The Odyssey' after translator's scathing review
World.content:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is officially 2026's fourth highest-grossing film, having surpassed the $700 million mark at the worldwide box office after just over two weeks in cinemas.

 

While audiences continue to flock to theatres to watch Nolan's take on Homer's epic poem, the film has become something of a cultural lightning rod. It has sparked renewed interest in the source material and Greek culture, a positive side-effect tempered by Elon Musk taking against the film from the get-go, fuelling a culture war surrounding the film's diverse casting.

He even announced that his AI tool Grok Imagine would make a “historically accurate” full-length feature version of Homer’s text.

Then there are purists who have been left frustrated with Nolan's take on the source material – specifically the use of contemporary English language.

One recent criticism came from British-American translator Emily Wilson, whose 2017 translation of Homer's poem was the first by a woman into English verse. Wilson wrote a viral review for the London Review of Books in which she attacked Nolan's film, writing that it lacked “psychological, emotional, political and ethical depth” and had “nothing convincing to say.”

Wilson summed up her take with: “I would be ashamed to have written any part of this script.”

Now, American author Joyce Carol Oates has come to the defense of The Odyssey, taking issue with Wilson's language and tone, which Oates describes as one of "dismissal & haughty superiority".

“Rather than disagreeing with interpretations of Homer in a collegial manner, this person, who has benefited enormously from Nolan’s film, speaks in the crude language of MAGA folks attacking someone with ideas that differ from hers,” Carol wrote on X. “One would expect a translator, of all people, beholden to a text, in service to a text, to be just a wee bit more thoughtful & respectful of others who are acting in good faith just as (she would claim) she is.”

Nolan previously praised Wilson for her translation of the ancient text, telling Empire that he used the opening line of her version, “Tell me about a complicated man,” as inspiration when developing Matt Damon's role as Odysseus.

Oates, who has won the National Book Award, been a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize four times and is best known for her books "Blonde" and "We Were Mulvaneys" (both of which were made into films), added in separate posts on X that she highly recommended Nolan’s adaption and that she wasn’t a fan of Wilson’s translation.

“What I’d read of Emily Wilson’s translation was not for me,” she wrote, adding that she assumes it was “deliberately written to appeal to an audience comfortable with YA (young adult) directness & spareness of vocabulary - that is, with the intention of being marketable, adopted by high school classes."

"With a more poetic, elevated speech, you are naturally limiting your audience," continued the author, who added that there was nothing wrong with a direct, commercial approach. "Why not profit from a classic work not protected by copyright? A graphic novel of "The Odyssey" could be terrific, too.)"

Oates also responded to critics of the film’s modern dialogue.

“The most elegant translation of The Odyssey is by Daniel Mendelsohn; it is ‘poetic,’ each word chosen with care, precision; it is beautiful, melodic but if that translation had been used in Nolan’s film the charges would not be that the language is banal or boring but rather that the language is too elevated, ‘poetic.’ I do not think that Nolan’s film will be considered a great classic but really, it seems that whatever Nolan did, it would disappoint hordes of people. Most moviemakers/creators just try the best they can – it seems odd that this director has drawn such angry criticism.”

The author also noted that such criticism “is chilling, dampening for any creative artist. To attack a creative artist as if he were a criminal, had done something to harm, hurt, kill–this is alarming. If you hate a movie, fine – no need to recommend it. No one expects every work of art to be a classic, perfect… Rage seems just weirdly inappropriate.”

She also said she would “highly recommend both Nolan’s film & the 1997 miniseries co-produced by Francis Coppola."

While debate rages on, The Odyssey should continue its trajectory towards the $1 billion mark at the global box office – even if its numbers are expected to dip now that Spider-Man: Brand New Day (also starring The Odyssey cast members Tom Holland, Zendaya and Jon Bernthal) has hit cinemas.

Read Euronews Culture's full review of The Odyssey here, check out where it falls in our ranking of Nolan's filmography and in our ranking of the Best Movies of 2026 So Far. And when you're done with all that reading, find out what we think of Spider-Man: Brand New Day here.

World.title: Europe’s fastest-growing economies in Q2 2026: Who led and who lagged?
World.content:
The eurozone economy was expected to lose momentum in the second quarter of 2026.

 

Instead, it surprised to the upside.

Eurostat's preliminary estimate showed GDP expanding by 0.4% quarter-on-quarter, up from flat growth in the first quarter and ahead of economists' expectations for a 0.2% increase.

Across the European Union, growth accelerated to 0.5%, from 0.1% previously. Annual growth also strengthened, reaching 1.0% in the euro area and 1.2% across the EU.

At first glance, the figures suggest the bloc is proving more resilient than feared despite higher energy prices and continued geopolitical uncertainty.

But the headline hides a much more interesting story.

Growth is becoming increasingly uneven.

Ireland, Lithuania and Sweden led European growth

"The Eurozone economy blew past the consensus in Q2 and was even stronger than our above-consensus forecast, despite the energy price shock triggered by the US-Iran war," commented Claus Vistesen, chief eurozone economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

Among the countries that have already released second-quarter data, Ireland posted by far the strongest quarterly expansion, with GDP surging 3.9%.

According to Pantheon Macroeconomics’ calculations, the rebound in Ireland alone added 0.1 percentage points to headline eurozone growth.

It was followed by Lithuania, where the economy grew by 1.7%, and Sweden, which expanded by 1.4%.

Southern Europe also remained resilient. Portugal recorded 0.8% quarterly growth, while Spain continued to outperform the eurozone's largest economies with a 0.7% expansion.

At the other end of the ranking, Belgium and Austria stagnated, recording no growth during the quarter.

Germany, France and Italy all expanded, but at a slower pace than previously.

Europe's largest economy shows slower expansion

Germany's economy grew by 0.2%, slowing from 0.4% in the first quarter but still outperforming market expectations of 0.1%.

Pantheon Macroeconomics’ Vistesen said the data leave "a picture of resilience in the first half of the year", helped by upward revisions to previous quarters.

The composition of growth was equally revealing. "Net exports were the main driver of Q2 GDP growth, while consumption slowed and investment fell," Vistesen said, suggesting Germany is relying more on foreign demand than domestic spending to keep its economy expanding.

France also returned to growth, with GDP rising by 0.2% after contracting in the previous quarter.

Yet the details were less convincing.

Vistesen said "the rebound in GDP growth is encouraging, but the details are less so, particularly for investment", pointing to weak capital spending despite a recovery in consumer demand.

If there was one large economy that continued to defy expectations, it was Spain.

GDP accelerated to 0.7%, extending a run that has consistently outpaced its eurozone peers.

"The Spanish economy appears to have been unscathed by the energy shock so far," said Ankita Amajuri, Europe economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

Strong household spending, resilient exports, fiscal support and the country's growing renewable energy capacity have all helped cushion consumers from rising energy prices.

Italy also expanded by 0.2%, slowing from 0.3% but beating expectations of 0.1%.

Amajuri cautioned that "Italy's economy is more vulnerable to the recent surge in energy prices than Spain's", making it one of the eurozone economies most exposed if energy costs remain elevated through the second half of the year.

A stronger eurozone, but inflation is stirring again

Taken together, the latest figures suggest the eurozone entered the summer on firmer footing than many economists had expected.

But they also point to a bloc growing at different speeds. Ireland recorded the strongest quarterly growth, Spain remains the strongest of the major economies, while Germany, France and Italy are expanding at a much more modest pace.

Just as growth appears to be regaining momentum, another challenge is beginning to re-emerge.

Early inflation readings for July suggest price pressures are picking up again across parts of Europe.

Pantheon Macroeconomics estimates German headline inflation rebounded to around 2.7% in July from 2.3% in June, after regional data showed stronger price growth in Bavaria, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saxony and Hesse.

Spain also reported firmer inflation. Preliminary data showed consumer prices rose by 3.5% year-on-year in July, up from 3.2% in June and the highest reading since May 2024. Core inflation, which strips out energy and unprocessed food, edged up to 3.0%.

Attention now turns to Thursday's eurozone inflation release, with economists expecting annual inflation to edge up to 2.9% in July from 2.8% in June.

If those trends persist, the European Central Bank may keep the door open to another interest rate increase after the summer.

World.title: The world’s top 10 cities for street food have been revealed
World.content:
When you think about street food, you probably picture bánh mì in Vietnam, tacos in Mexico, or even pizza al taglio in Italy.

 

Certain countries and cities are well known for their offerings, with foodies heading specifically to a destination to grab miscellaneous meat on sticks on-the-go and the like.

But a new study has revealed the best street food city in the world, and it’s not where you would expect at all.

Paris in France came out on top in the research conducted by Radical Storage, which looked at 6,897 street food vendors in the 100 most-visited cities around the globe.

For the analysis, the team looked at the number of vendors with a star rating above four, the variety of cuisines on offer, the availability of vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, the proportion of budget-friendly eats, and the vendor density per square kilometre.

Street food was defined as food stalls and trucks, as well as sit-in restaurants that serve classic street food bites.

The vendor density had the highest impact on the score, with a weighting of 30%, followed by the budget-friendly proportion at 20%. The number of vendors over four stars, the average vendor rating, the cuisine varieties, the vegetarians and vegan options and the gluten-free options were all weighted 10% each.

The French capital came out with a score of 7.2 out of 10 – with 69.1% of the 401 eateries rated four stars or more. Paris has a density of 3.82 street food vendors per square kilometre, too.

Next up on the list are two Greek destinations: Athens and Thessaloniki. Athens scored 6.9 out of 10 thanks to the number of cuisines on offer (29), and the number of food vendors per square metre at 4.21.

Thessaloniki meanwhile scored 6.1, with 77.1% of street food options being budget-friendly.

Rhodes in Greece topped the list for the best-rated street food, with 82% of vendors rated four stars and up, while London won out for the best variety, with dishes from 39 distinct food types.

World.title: FIFA opens disciplinary cases against Argentina for World Cup final scuffle and 'Malvinas' banner
World.content:
FIFA has lodged disciplinary charges against two Argentina players for their behaviour towards Spanish players after losing the World Cup final, as well as showing a political banner about the Falkland Islands after beating England in the semifinals.

 

The list of disciplinary cases opened by FIFA against Argentina also includes “discriminatory chants and gestures” by fans, alleged assault by an assistant coach after the final and “throwing of objects by spectators in relation to several matches” at the World Cup.

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes faces three charges of assault in the post-game clashes after Spain’s 1-0 win on July 19, defender Nahuel Molina faces two charges and coach Roberto Ayala one.

Paredes physically tangled with Spain players Eric Garcia and Gavi, and Spain captain Rodri was hit in the stomach as he ran past Molina.

Argentina's Leandro Paredes (5) knocks down Spain's Gavi (9) during scuffle after the World Cup final match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, July 19, 2026. AP Photo/Julio Cortez

Molina and Thiago Almada are also charged with unsporting behaviour, with the same charge levelled against Spain player Gavi.

Last week, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente has described the incidents as “intolerable and unacceptable.”

“It cannot be allowed,” De la Fuente told Spanish public broadcaster TVE, adding he did not see the incidents at the time while “celebrating with other people.”

“In any case, I find it intolerable and unacceptable from players of that caliber, whom I had been praising in the days before and who have a magnificent coach,” the Spain coach said.

Argentina also faces a charge of “using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature", FIFA confirmed on Wednesday.

Argentina's Giovani Lo Celso holds a banner with the words "The Malvinas are Argentine", at the end of the World Cup semifinal match against England in Atlanta, July 15, 2026. AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell

After beating England 2-1 in the semi-finals, the Argentina players unfurled a banner bearing the slogan "Las Malvinas son Argentinas" — “The Malvinas are Argentine”.

Argentina claims sovereignty over the archipelago, which it calls the Malvinas Islands, while the United Kingdom refers to it as the Falkland Islands. In 1982, the then Argentine military dictatorship invaded the territory, triggering a ten-week war that ended in a British victory.

Following the display of the banner, members of the British government called on FIFA to investigate the matter.

World.title: What are the deadliest countries for driving in Europe?
World.content:
Driving across Europe by car is a great choice for those looking to take in the scenic route this summer while also squeezing in multi-city adventures.

 

However, safety standards on those roads vary wildly from border to border.

Serbia, Bulgaria, and Romania are Europe's deadliest countries for driving, according to a study by Vignette Switzerland, an online sales company for the Swiss e-vignette, a digital road toll pass.

Serbia registered 74 road deaths per million people, putting the country a staggering 72% above the EU average. It's the second consecutive year the country topped the list.

However, its latest road fatality figures are slightly down from last year's.

Bulgaria followed next in second place with 71 road deaths per million people, and Romania ranked third with 68 road deaths per million people.

In addition, popular tourism hubs, including Portugal, Greece, Italy and France, came in among the top 10 deadliest European countries for driving, according to the study.

On the other hand, Nordic countries still dominate the safety rankings, with Norway now tied with Sweden, recording just 19 deaths per million inhabitants, making them nearly four times safer than Serbia.

Which European country has improved — and who hasn't?

Lithuania has achieved a 43% reduction in road deaths over the last decade, according to Vignette Switzerland.

Latvia, Bulgaria, Greece and Hungary also showed long-term progress in protecting drivers and pedestrians alike, with decreases of 37%, 36%, 35%, and 30% in road deaths, respectively.

Nevertheless, road safety progress has stalled in some common holiday destinations such as Portugal, where road deaths have fallen by just 1% since 2015.

France has also shown a slow rate of improvement, reducing fatalities by 6% over the same period.

Experts suggest that drivers looking to travel this summer should check local rules, plan their routes carefully, and stay alert on unfamiliar roads to avoid incidents.

World.title: Here's the salary you need to afford a €1 million home across Europe
World.content:
A €1 million home may be an ordinary flat in central Paris or a luxury villa near Sofia. But wherever buyers look, they need an income far above the national average to afford one.

 

So how much would they need to earn?

Euronews Business calculated the salary needed using a typical mortgage scenario: a 20% deposit, a fixed interest rate of 3.5% and a 30-year repayment term. It also assumed that buyers would spend no more than 33% of their gross income on the mortgage.

That means a deposit of €200,000 and a mortgage of €800,000.

The calculation does not include property taxes, insurance, transaction costs or other fees, and actual lending conditions vary between countries and borrowers.

The monthly payment is almost €3,600

Under these assumptions, the annual mortgage payment would be €43,108. This equals €3,592 a month.

Since 33% of gross income is set aside for mortgage payments, the buyer would need an annual gross income of €130,631. That is €10,886 a month.

Income levels differ significantly across Europe. This income may be easier to reach in some countries than others. The burden can also vary within a country.

The calculations in this article are based on Eurostat’s 2025 gross earnings figures for a full-time single worker without children earning 100% of the average wage. Since two incomes make a €1 million home more attainable and couples are likely to be interested, the calculations also show how the burden changes for a couple in which both partners earn the average salary.

Buyers in Bulgaria need nearly eight times the average salary

The number of average salaries needed to afford a €1 million home varies widely across Europe. Within the EU, the gap between the lowest and highest figures is almost fivefold.

Average workers in Bulgaria are in the most challenging position, while those in Luxembourg come closest to being able to afford the mortgage. In Bulgaria, a single person with no children earning 100% of the average salary would need an income equivalent to 7.8 average salaries. In Luxembourg, this figure is below two, at 1.6.

The number of average salaries needed ranges from two to three in Denmark (2.1), Ireland (2.3), Belgium (2.4), Austria (2.5), the Netherlands (2.6), Germany (2.7), Finland (2.8) and Sweden (2.8).

Average workers in these countries come closest to being able to afford a million-euro home.

Among the EU's 'Big Four' economies, Germany has the best position at 2.7 average salaries, compared with 3.1 in France, 4.0 in Spain and 4.1 in Italy.

The figure also stays below four in Slovenia (3.7) and Malta (3.9).

Ten EU countries need more than five salaries

To afford a million-euro home, an income equivalent to more than five average salaries would be necessary in ten EU countries. Greece (7.2) closely follows Bulgaria (7.8), giving it the second-highest requirement in the EU.

Hungary (6.7), Slovakia (6.3) and Poland (5.8) complete the top five.

Romania (5.8), Latvia (5.7), Czechia (5.2), Portugal (5.2) and Croatia (5.2) also require more than five average salaries. Estonia sits at exactly 5.0, taking the total to eleven countries requiring the equivalent of five salaries or more.

Two average earners qualify only in Luxembourg

For a couple in which both partners earn the average salary, the affordability ratio is halved because the calculation is based on their combined income. In Luxembourg, the required income is equivalent to 0.8 times the couple’s combined gross earnings, meaning two average earners would fall within the assumed 33% mortgage limit.

Denmark comes close, with the required income equivalent to 1.05 times a two-earner couple’s combined salary. Ireland and Belgium both have a ratio of about 1.2, meaning that even the combined salaries of two average earners would not be enough. Under the assumptions used here, however, Luxembourg is the only EU country where two average earners would meet the affordability threshold.

In Bulgaria, a couple earning average salaries would still need an income equivalent to almost four times their combined earnings, still making the home very difficult to afford.

How much are the average salaries?

Average annual gross earnings vary widely across Europe as of 2025 according to Eurostat. For a single person with no children, average gross monthly salaries, calculated by dividing the annual figure by 12, range from €1,398 in Bulgaria to €6,713 in Luxembourg.

Average gross monthly earnings also exceed €4,000 in Denmark (€5,300), Ireland (€4,708), Belgium (€4,630), Austria (€4,306) and the Netherlands (€4,167).

In contrast, the average salary is below €2,000 in seven countries. This is far from covering the €3,592 monthly mortgage payment. Besides Bulgaria, they are Greece (€1,510), Hungary (€1,625), Slovakia (€1,734), Poland (€1,862), Romania (€1,885) and Latvia (€1,904).

Gap between the salary and mortgage

Since the calculation assumes that only 33% of the salary can go towards the mortgage, one average salary is not enough in any EU country for a single person.

In Bulgaria, this leaves a deficit of €3,131. This is the gap between the €3,592 mortgage payment and €461, or 33% of the salary.

In Luxembourg, the shortfall is €1,377, as 33% of the gross salary is €2,215.

World.title: Why Germany may stand up against FIFA's World Cup sell off
World.content:
Leading figures in German football have lined up to criticize Gianni Infantino’s plans to sell a stake in the World Cup. Germany is showing signs that they may ready to oppose Infantino's re-election.

"We must not let it become a pawn in the hands of investors. We must not lose the fans' support, but we are well on our way to squandering that support. I consider this extremely problematic and unacceptable."

Those were the words of the head of Germany's football association, the DFB, in response to FIFA's plan to form a commercial subsidiary to sell to private investors. Bernd Neuendorf, the DFB president, is on the FIFA Council, which FIFA describes as its "main decision making body" but was blindsided by Tuesday's proposal.

The Day with Brent Goff – Troop Boost for Russia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Neuendorf said he "had to learn the news from the newspaper. That's no way to treat people." He said Infantino's method was "extremely troubling. When you sit on the committee, you want to be able to actively participate in decisions and express your opinion. That has to be a process, but none of that is happening at FIFA — not on important issues, and especially not now with the investor issue."

Bundesliga clubs slam FIFA World Cup plan

As well as widespread fan discontent, expressed via social media, leading German clubs have voiced their dissatisfaction with the plans.

"I am ashamed that we even discuss such ideas in football. Football does not belong to us," Bayern Munich's board member for sport Max Eberl told Sky.

"I have the feeling that FIFA exists solely to make a profit. It disgusts me," he added.

"Why does FIFA feel it needs to reinvent the wheel? In my view, this initiative is not a good idea at all," said Borussia Dortmund's CEO Carsten Cramer, while his equivalent at Stuttgart, Alexander Wehrle, lent his support to the DFB and European football governor UEFA's stance against the proposal.

"Driving the commercialization of football in this direction without even a semblance of a common, sensible goal would send a disastrous message," he said.

Earlier this year, Germany declined to sign a document recommending Infantino's re-election and Neuendorf was also critical of FIFA's suspension of a World Cup red-card ban for US striker Folarin Balogun following an intervention from US President Donald Trump.

New Germany manager Jürgen Klopp, working as a TV pundit during the tournament, criticized that decision too.

"Let's just say: this is our game, not theirs. These two people (Infantino and Trump), who both have no idea about football, should have nothing to do with that," he said.

Germany and UEFA keen to make voice heard

Despite falling behind on the pitch in recent times, Germany still holds plenty of sway in European football's governing body and will likely be a key voice when that organization meets, reportedly on Thursday. Neundorf added that: "If UEFA rejects this request (for approval of the plan), then it is dead, because I believe that you won't be able to find any investor who would be willing to go ahead with this project if UEFA is out."

Bernd Neundorf (right) has been critical of how Gianni Infantino has handled his latest proposal Image: Federico Gambarini/dpa/picture alliance

This is not the first time that Germany has protested against a FIFA decision. At the Qatar World Cup in 2022, the men's team covered their mouths before a game against Japan in protest at not being allowed to wear the rainbow armband to support LGBT+ rights. The lack of support from other federations for that action made Germany hesitant to repeat it in World Cup 2026 despite widespread concerns about ticket prices, the failure to issue visas to fans and officials from certain countries and Infantino's relationship with Trump.

Fan engagement means DFB must be strong in message and action

But the Balogun case, and the new sell off proposal may have been beyond the pale. The DFB know that they must toe a particularly careful line on these issues due to the country's football culture.

In 2024, the DFL, the organization that operate the Bundesliga, was forced to climb down from plans to sell a share of its TV rights to foreign investors due to fan protests that included tennis balls and remote control cars with smoke bombs being thrown on the pitch during matches.

Fan protests against commercialization are common in the Bundesliga. This reads "No to investors in the DFL" Image: Moritz Müller/IMAGO

More recently, fans of Bayern and Stuttgart unfurled a huge banner featuring a crossed out DFB logo at this year's German Cup final in protest at high ticket prices.

Such actions are commonplace in German football, with the 50+1 ownership model, that bars single investors owning a majority stake in a club, ensuring fans retain more power than in most other European nations.

Even if Germany and UEFA continue to protest Infantino's decisions and presidency, the Swiss executive will likely retain control unless other confederations, particularly Africa and Asia, follow suit. Although UEFA only has 55 of 211 votes, it remains the most powerful confederation within FIFA and with leadership from a powerful nation like Germany, Infantino may start to feel the heat.

Edited by: Chuck Penfold

World.title: Poland says Russian ballistic missile violated airspace
World.content:
Polish authorities have said that a Russian ballistic missile crashed within its borders during Moscow's overnight attacks on Ukraine. No injuries were reported as Kyiv warned air defense in the region needs boosting.

Polish authorities on Thursday said they were inspecting a crater near the city of Lublin for information clarifying a violation of its airspace.

Police and military said a crater, 10 meters in diameter (about 33 feet), had been created upon impact by what was likely a Russian missile during Moscow's massive overnight bombing campaign on neighboring Ukraine.

Russia's attacks not only targeted the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, but also western cities such as Lviv. The point of impact in Poland, said to have been a field in Tarnawa Kolonia near Lublin, was located about 80 kilometers (50 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk headed to the site, accompanied by his defense and interior ministers.

Writing on X before he departed, Tusk wrote: "During the Russian massive missile attack on western Ukraine, a violation of Polish airspace occurred. In connection with this, I have convened a coordination team with the participation of the Minister of Defense and the relevant services, which have been working on-site for many hours and are systematically providing me with information about all the circumstances of the incident."

In Lublin, Tusk said: "Everything points to it being a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile, but we do not wish to pre-empt the results of a thorough investigation."

Local police say residents reported hearing a large explosion that rattled windows around 4:00 a.m. local time (0200 GMT) after which police quickly discovered a massive "crater" and "debris from a non-identified object."

A military helicopter confirmed the finding during a flyover.

Poland attempts to hold NATO's front line against Russia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Poland's military said it had scrambled an F-16 prior to impact after radar picked up a violation of the NATO member's airspace around 3:40 a.m.

Though the origin of the object has not been confirmed, Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha wrote on X that a "Russian Kh-101 cruise missile” had "crossed into Poland" and violated NATO airspace.

Sybiha continued, "This is yet another clear demonstration that strengthening Ukraine's air defense now is urgent and serves as a guarantee for the protection of the entire Euro-Atlantic community."

Russian jets, drones and missiles have repeatedly violated the airspace of several NATO member states throughout over four years of war.

Putin's drones: NATO's nightmare? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

NATO said it was in close contact with Polish authorities.

The Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR), General Alexus G. Grynkewich, spoke earlier today with Poland's Chief of Defense General Wieslaw Kukulan about NATO and Poland's response to the incident, which remains under investigation.

He underlined the military alliance will continue to take all necessary measures to defend NATO territory.

Edited by: Louis Oelofse

World.title: Danube water levels: Hungary, Romania cut nuclear output
World.content:
Historically low water levels along Europe's second-longest river have led Hungary and Romania to reduce output at key nuclear plants. Danube tourism and river cargo have also been severely affected by Europe's heatwave.

Hungary and Romania have drastically reduced output at their nuclear power plants due to insufficient water flow from the Danube river, which has sunk to historically low levels.

Hungary's Paks nuclear plant, located 120 kilometers (74.5 miles) south of the capital, Budapest, cut output by 50% at ⁠reactor ⁠2 on Thursday morning.

⁠The plant operates four Russian-built ⁠reactors ​with a combined capacity of 2 gigawatts. Output had already been cut by 254 ⁠megawatts ​on reactor ​1 on Monday, ​before reactor 3 powered down on ​Wednesday.

Down river in Romania, one of two reactors at the Cernavoda nuclear plant, 160 kilometers east of Bucharest, was shut down earlier this week due to lower water levels.

The Romanian Energy Ministry was set to shut down the plant's second reactor on Thursday due to "unfavorable developments in hydraulic conditions" – but ultimately managed to keep it operating overnight.

Water from the Danube is vital for cooling operations at nuclear power plants along Europe's second-longest river (2,857 kilometers, after the Volga which meanders 3,790 through Russia).

In Budapest, Hungary's national water authority measured the Danube's gauge level at 23 centimeters (9 inches) on Wednesday morning, well below the previous record low of 33 centimeters (13 inches) set in 2018.

The Hungarian nuclear power plant in Paks, just south of Budapest, has reduced reactor output due to low Danube water levels Image: Daniel Kiss/MTI/AP Photo/picture alliance

Heatwave in Europe: Danube river traffic on hold

And it's not just nuclear power plants which are affected; river traffic from cargo ships to tourist cruises has also been put on hold.

In Hungary, the low water level has forced popular cruise ships, where passengers usually disembark for sightseeing in Budapest, to dock further upriver, while cargo ships have stopped operating nearly entirely, according to the country's Ministry of Transport and Investment.

In neighboring Romania, the water level along parts of the Danube is already one meter (three feet) below the navigable minimum.

"This is an exceptional situation," Adrian Maizel, from the administration monitoring traffic on the Danube, told the AFP news agency, adding that dredging efforts were underway to enable shipping to continue.

"We are making efforts to maintain a navigable channel as much as possible – albeit a narrower one – so that navigation is not completely blocked," he explained.

In Bulgaria, where the Danube forms a border with Romania, police on Tuesday evacuated 186 tourists from a cruise ship that had run aground near the port city of Vidin.

And in Serbia, hundreds of small boats and dozens of cargo ships were marooned on the dried out river bank near the northern city of Novi Sad, where the water in the Danube had withdrawn up to 20 meters (65 feet) away from the river's usual shore.

"The summer season is over now, as far as boat rides are concerned," Radovan Segrt, a house boat owner who runs river excursions on his vessel.

Tourists and locals were able to walk on the exposed Danube river bed beneath the Margaret Bridge in Budapest Image: Daniel Alfoldi/ZUMA/picture alliance

Budapest: Margaret Bridge base exposed

Back in Budapest, the receding water levels have exposed the base pillars of the city's famous Margaret Bridge, where authorities discovered a Second World War era bomb last week.

"The bare rocks, the dry sand bars around the bridge pillars ... it's shocking to see how things were before and how they are now," photographer Gabor Kertesz told AP. "Where will this lead, what will happen? We don't know that yet, but this must be the result of climate change."

Indeed, the plunging Danube water levels across eastern Europe come as the continent continues to endure one of its hottest summers on record.

Germany bracing for next heatwave

In the west of the continent, French and Spanish authorities area battling unprecedented wildfires while Germany is bracing itself for another heatwave, with temperatures in some regions expected to approach 40°C (104°F) again this week, according to the German Meteorological Service (DWD).

Berlin's Robert Koch Institute (RKI), the federal government agency responsible for disease control and prevention, said on Thursday that 9,800 people had died due to heat-related conditions this summer – more than in any entire year since 2016.

The RKI attributed over 5,000 of those fatalities to the severe heatwave in the second half of June, where temperatures hit 40°C in several parts of the country.

New heatwave could worsen France, Spain fires To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

World.title: Crete wildfires cause evacuations and firefighter deaths
World.content:
Wildfires on the Greek island of Crete are forcing thousands of residents and tourists to evacuate. Three firefighters have died as Greece becomes the latest country, after France and Spain, to face summer blazes.

Greek firefighters battled deadly wildfires on the island of Crete for a second day on Thursday as strong winds made it difficult to contain the flames.

Two firefighters were killed while responding to fires on the island, while a third died fighting a separate blaze on the Greek mainland.

Thousands evacuated as fires spread

Fires advancing across southwestern Crete forced several villages in the Rethymno region to be evacuated. Flames also neared the popular resort town of Agia Galini on the island's southern coast, pushing tourists to leave.

In total, roughly 8,000 people were evacuated, the island's deputy governor Maria Lioni said.

The fires have already destroyed large areas of farmland, including olive groves, as well as residential homes.

Has Europe lost control of its wildfires? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Why is it so difficult to stop the fires?

Firefighters have struggled to contain the blazes because of strong and constantly shifting winds, which have reached speeds of up to 102 kilometers (63 miles) per hour.

As a result, emergency services said aircraft used to drop water on the fires were severely limited or could not be deployed at all.

"Unfortunately there is no improvement, and the latest information ​indicates that winds will increase later in the day," Giorgos Tsapakos, the deputy regional governor for civil protection on Crete, told Greek television.

Two firefighters died combating the flames in Crete after being trapped on a mountain road, losing their bearings as smoke enveloped them. A third firefighter collapsed and died while on duty near Gytheio on the Southern end of the Peloponnese peninsula.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis paid tribute to the fallen firefighters on Wednesday, acknowledging the "new harsh reality” they face each year, as wildfires worsen.

Greece, like other Southern European countries, is facing a heightened risk of wildfires as climate change exacerbates droughts, high temperatures and extreme winds which create ideal conditions for blazes.

A firefighter near Bordeaux, France, responding to a fire that ravaged a popular summer vacation spot Image: Ed Jones/AFP

How are the fires in France and Spain developing?

In France and Spain, meanwhile, firefighting efforts on Thursday seemed to be turning a corner.

In France, authorities permitted the return of 84,000 evacuees forced out by a wildfire near the southwestern city of Bordeaux, as cooler temperatures and rain offered some respite. The fire had led to around 220,000 people being displaced.

In Spain, too, wildfires threatening Madrid were abating, as authorities reported "almost no flames" left.

Edited by: Louis Oelofse
